We compute the Hamiltonian of several theories, one of which has Chern--Simons terms, using our prescription and show that, in black-hole backgrounds, the Hamiltonian gives directly the quantum statistical relation including terms related to non-gravitational charges and chemical potentials, as expected.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Linearized $\mathcal{N}=2$ conformal supergravity in the harmonic approach
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Using the harmonic superspace approach, we construct the superconformal harmonic action for $\mathcal{N}=2$ Weyl supermultiplet. The fundamental objects of the theory are unconstrained analytic potentials $h^{++α\dotα}, h^{++α+}, h^{++\dotα+}, h^{(+4)}$, which distinguishes our construction among the previously known ones. An important role is played by the ``half-analyticity'' conditions introduced in arXiv:2407.08524 [hep-th]. The structure of the harmonic linearized $\mathcal{N}=2$ Weyl action to large extent repeats the structure of the $\mathcal{N}=2$ Maxwell action, which suggests a conjecture on the possible structure of the complete nonlinear $\mathcal{N}=2$ Weyl theory action in the harmonic superspace. We provide a detailed study of the rigid superconformal properties of the proposed action and prove its invariance in both harmonic and chiral superspaces. First steps are also undertaken towards constructing the nonlinear $\mathcal{N}=2$ Weyl action, based on an analogy with $\mathcal{N}=2$ Maxwell action just mentioned and a generalization of the concept of half-analyticity to curved harmonic superspace.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: General relativity and its modifications as effective field theories of $GL(4)$ breaking
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We discuss General Relativity and some of its modifications as effective field theories of the breaking of the affine general linear group using the coset approach and the Maurer-Cartan form. While the ultimate goal is to break the symmetry down to the Lorentz subgroup, we argue that there are three interesting breaking cascades in which the affine general linear group is first broken to a larger subgroup that contains the Lorentz group. In all cases, the breaking of translations always generates Goldstone modes that can be interpreted as metric degrees of freedom. We argue that the effective field theories that emerge as a result of the different breaking patterns are all dynamically equivalent at the lowest order of the derivative expansion, e.g., using Einstein-Hilbert-like actions, but can differ beyond the leading order.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Gravitational wave echoes as probes of the maximum mass of strange stars in quadratic curvature-matter coupled gravity
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Gravitational wave astronomy provides a powerful avenue for probing exotic compact stars. Recent analyses of GW170817 have reported possible post-merger gravitational wave echoes with a significance of $4.2σ$ and a dominant frequency near $72,\text{Hz}$. Such echoes may arise from ultracompact remnants possessing photon spheres that partially trap gravitational perturbations. In general relativity, photon-sphere formation requires the stellar compactness to lie between one-third and four-ninths, a condition difficult to achieve with realistic equations of state. Here, we investigate this possibility in quadratic curvature gravity with non-minimal matter coupling, considering strange stars described by the MIT bag model equation of state. By solving the modified Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations, we obtain mass-radius relations and identify configurations capable of supporting photon spheres and gravitational wave echoes. The modified Buchdahl limit permits more compact stellar solutions, while photon-sphere constraints restrict the viable parameter space. We find that increasing the bag constant reduces the maximum mass and echo time, shifting the echo frequency toward the kHz regime. The echo constraints impose more stringent maximum mass-radius limits than hydrostatic equilibrium, suggesting revised maximum mass bounds for strange stars. We further compute the critical impact parameter and eikonal quasi-normal modes, demonstrating how modified gravity parameters systematically alter the photon-sphere radius and associated observational signatures. These results establish post-merger strange stars as potential GW echo sources and highlight echoes, optical shadows, and QNMs as complementary probes of modified gravity for next-generation detectors such as the Einstein Telescope and Cosmic Explorer.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Codimension-Zero Holographic Complexity and Spectral Three-Point Correlators
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Holographic complexity is expected to capture the linear growth of black hole interiors, with quantum corrections ultimately leading to a late-time saturation. We develop a spectral formulation of holographic complexity measures associated with codimension-zero bulk regions in the framework of the complexity=anything proposal. The corresponding generating function of complexity is governed by three-point correlation functions of the density of states, establishing a direct connection between bulk geometric observables and nonperturbative Euclidean spacetime wormholes. We find that the codimension-zero holographic complexity reduces to the sum of two codimension-one contributions and exhibits a universal time evolution, characterized by an exponentially long regime of linear growth followed by saturation at the Heisenberg time. The late-time plateau is a direct result of the spectral level repulsion, a generic feature of quantum chaotic systems, thereby providing a universal mechanism for the saturation of holographic complexity. We also develop a complementary operator interpretation, in which Euclidean wormhole corrections render the semiclassical basis of fixed-complexity states overcomplete. Constructing a complete orthonormal basis then yields well-defined holographic complexity operators that reproduce the same universal time evolution. Our results establish a unified connection among black hole interiors, chaotic spectral statistics, and Euclidean wormholes in quantum gravity.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: The point-particle-limit effective-source approach for computing gravitational self-force in the Lorenz gauge
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The traditional effective-source method is hampered by complex analytical expressions and the inherent smoothness limit, which incur high computational costs and complicate implementation. To overcome these limitations, we introduce the point-particle-limit effective source method, which analytically takes the size of the effective source to zero, thereby transforming the problem into a well-defined jump condition of retarded metric field at the particle position governed by the local singular field. This formulation naturally pairs with a discontinuous Galerkin scheme, whose inherent capacity for accommodating solution discontinuities enables highly accurate enforcement of the jump conditions. We apply both the traditional and point-particle-limit effective source method to calculate the time-domain gravitational metric perturbation and gravitational self-force in the Lorenz gauge on a point particle in a circular orbit around a Schwarzschild black hole. The comparison of numerical results shows the excellent advantage of the point-particle-limit effective source method, which validates the correctness and efficiency of the point-particle-limit effective source method and thereby establishes a numerical foundation for computing generic geodesic orbits or long-time self-consistent orbital evolution.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 25 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables; Accepted for publication in Chinese Physics B

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Learning Schwarzschild Geodesic Motion with Lagrangian Neural Networks
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Lagrangian Neural Networks (LNNs) learn dynamics from trajectory data by parameterizing a scalar Lagrangian and deriving accelerations through the Euler--Lagrange equation, providing a variational inductive bias that improves physical consistency over purely data-driven models. LNNs have recently been extended to general relativistic settings, leaving Schwarzschild geodesics as an open challenge. Training on complex relativistic systems is hindered by the diversity of the dynamics, as well as numerical instabilities and the difficulty of adequately sampling physically relevant, diverse orbital regimes. We introduce two coordinated improvements: a decoupled position--velocity normalization scheme that independently rescales each coordinate and its time derivatives, reweighting acceleration targets to balance contributions across all channels; and an energy-constrained log-uniformly sampled dataset generation strategy informed by the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) structure. With these improvements, our model accurately reproduces perihelion precession and relativistic time dilation, conserves energy and angular momentum to within a few percent even after completing multiple orbits around the central mass and predicts orbital trajectories across eight orbital scenarios in close, medium, and far-field regimes. These results establish that LNNs, augmented with physically motivated normalization and sampling, can reliably learn geodesic dynamics in curved spacetime. Our work also represents the first successful training of LNNs on Schwarzschild geodesics and offers a promising direction for data-driven modeling of complex relativistic systems.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Generalized First Law and Smarr-type Relation: Beyond Additivity and Extensivity
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: In this work, we develop a general framework for deriving the first law of black hole thermodynamics and the associated Smarr-type relation for 4-dimensional static spherically symmetric spacetimes within a broad class of generalized entropy models. In addition, by employing the entropy representation for the Reissner--Nordström (RN) black hole, we determine a concise curvature functional that depends only on this representation and its derivatives. A general flatness condition is derived, demonstrating that when the entropy Hessian metric is regular and nondegenerate, both homogeneous power-law transformations and a separate logarithmic branch leave the RN black hole's Ruppeiner geometry flat. On the other hand, Rényi, Sharma-Mittal, Kaniadakis, and LQG-inspired entropy deformations typically give rise to nonvanishing curvature in the regular thermodynamic regime, demonstrating that the extremality of the RN black hole does not by itself require a curvature divergence.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 14 pages, title changed, further investigations added

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: A structural criterion for asymptotic states in Supersymmetry
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The occurrence of a field in a quantum field theory does not by itself establish the existence of a corresponding asymptotic particle. We formulate a structural criterion separating operator admissibility, dynamical spectral realization, and particlehood, using the exterior-polynomial classification of gravitino mass bilinears as a prototype. Particlehood is organized as an ordered filtration of geometry and state, effective algebra, dynamics, and spectral analysis, with the localization criterion $Λ[Ψ]$ defined by the presence of a physical spectral atom of non-zero weight. We obtain four results. First, conventional linearly realized global supercharges are obstructed on a positive-definite de Sitter Hilbert space when the full diagonal odd--odd bracket satisfies a positivity-reversal condition; the spacetime part is shown to be reversible in $\mathfrak{so}(4,1)$, while internal generators require a separate check. Second, invariant scalar de Sitter product decompositions remove the Minkowski additive two-particle threshold in principal-series channels. Third, a spectral-transfer decomposition shows how continuum weight in a mediator propagator can open absorptive support for an external field below the atomic mediator threshold. Fourth, in a reduced effective-operator basis, the fermionic vector derivative coupling is redundant under current-conservation assumptions, whereas the axial dimension-five coupling is physical unless excluded by parity or CP; under that symmetry hypothesis the residual fermionic derivative potential starts one operator dimension above the scalar one. Exact unbroken supersymmetry enforces multiplet rigidity of the atomic criterion.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 20 pages, 1 table. Substantially revised version with strengthened de Sitter positivity analysis, a refined spectral localization criterion, and a clarified Majorana derivative-sector discussion. Submitted to International Journal of Geometric Methods in Modern Physics

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Binary Ellis-Bronnikov wormholes in 3+1 numerical relativity: mergers, fly-bys and gravitational waves
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We present what are, to our knowledge, the first 3D numerical-relativity evolutions of wormhole binaries: pairs of massive Ellis-Bronnikov drainholes held open by a ghost scalar field. Each throat is an unstable fixed point whose e-fold time matches the González-Guzmán-Sarbach linear rate to within 1.9%. Two throats obey a charge-sign rule: like scalar charges repel and opposite charges attract, with a measured attraction-to-repulsion ratio of $1.462\pm0.022$ against the predicted 3/2, so only opposite-signed pairs merge. A head-on collision forms a common MOTS around both still-open throats, born with about their combined area. The horizon then loses 28% of its area as it swallows the phantom field, and by $t=100$ lies within 1.4% of the Schwarzschild radius of the pair's mass, still shrinking. Fly-by pairs form no horizon and both mouths inflate, the one nearest capture radiating the most gravitational-wave energy measured. A lone collapsing throat sheds its seeded quadrupole as a burst ringing at the Schwarzschild frequency of the black hole it becomes, and every encounter radiates its own burst of gravitational waves and a scalar dipole of comparable energy and negative sign. A throat survives at most a few orbital periods for any plausible perturbation, and the negative-energy dipole would pump rather than drain the orbit, so these binaries have no inspiral.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 25 pages, 12 figures, 5 tables; 12 movies as ancillary files. Code and data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23257999

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Causality, Redshift, and Matching-Scale Cancellation for Reflective Black-Hole Horizons
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The Boltzmann flux reflectivity used in quantum-horizon models does not by itself define a causal black-hole boundary response. We study two related questions for stationary Schwarzschild scattering. First, a classical Hardy-space condition excludes an exact Boltzmann modulus on the entire positive frequency axis for any nonzero bounded causal reflection amplitude at a fixed matching plane. We construct causal completions that preserve the modulus on any prescribed finite band. Second, we prove a low-frequency outer-phase expansion for a class of completions with fixed profiles and a common Boltzmann slope, including an exact-band completion and a smooth crossover completion. The logarithmic coefficient is common to this class, while the linear constant is an explicit functional of the completion. When the fixed proper-frame cutoff is redshifted to the matching surface and the local temperature is the Tolman redshift of the Hawking temperature, the outer phase cancels the leading logarithmic dependence of the propagation phase on the matching distance. The geometric remainder is quadratic in the proper distance, while a separate dispersive remainder depends on the completion. This is a low-energy comparison of specified response families, not an exact matching invariance or a phase fixed by causality alone. In an axial Schwarzschild example at a fixed matching plane, accounting for the predicted linear-delay difference reduces the maximum relative cavity-factor difference between two cutoffs from about $21\%$ to $0.11\%$ on the sampled frequency band. A passive quantum completion supplies the associated absorption-noise relation and checks the consistency of the asymptotic output.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Fire at the Tip of the Throat: Hagedorn Phase after brane-antibrane inflation?
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We study the post-inflationary open-string Hagedorn phase in perturbatively moduli stabilized brane-antibrane inflation. In this class of models, the volume modulus is stabilized by perturbative corrections rather than by non-perturbative effects to the superpotential, thereby avoiding the standard brane-antibrane $η$-problem. Since inflation ends through tachyon condensation and brane-antibrane annihilation, the endpoint is intrinsically stringy and need not be described immediately by an ordinary radiation bath. We analyze whether the energy released at annihilation can drive the visible sector into an open-string Hagedorn phase, and study the consequences for dark radiation. If the Standard Model (SM) branes lie in the same throat as where the annihilation occurs, we find that a modest fraction of the released energy deposited into surviving visible open strings is sufficient to enter the Hagedorn regime and can suppress the effective number of relativistic species $ΔN_{\rm eff}$ below current observational bounds. If the SM lies in a different throat, the result depends on inter-throat energy transfer: prompt or delayed transfer can still yield a visible Hagedorn phase. However, the mechanism is most efficient when the local string scale in the SM throat is lower than or comparable to that in the annihilation throat.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 12 pages, 2 figures, Replaced with the version matching the one published in EPJC

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Primordial Black Hole interpretation of the subsolar merger event S251112cm
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) candidate event S251112cm suggests that at least one component has a subsolar mass. Since such objects cannot be produced through standard stellar evolution, this observation provides a possible indication of nonstandard formation channels. Primordial black holes (PBHs), formed from the collapse of primordial density fluctuations in the early Universe, are a well-motivated candidate. We investigate the interpretation of S251112cm as the merger of two PBHs in the mass range $0.20$-$1\,M_\odot$, within the parameter space directly covered by the O4a subsolar search. Combining analytic estimates of the PBH merger rate with current observational constraints on their abundance and the sensitivity of LVK searches, we compute the probability of observing such an event. We consider both a monochromatic PBH mass function and extended lognormal distributions. Within the relaxed constraint scenario, the detection probability can approach unity toward the upper end of the mass range. A lognormal mass distribution of moderate width can enhance the probability relative to the monochromatic case, whereas a broader distribution can instead suppress it. Our results show that a PBH interpretation of S251112cm is compatible with current observational bounds even for a subdominant PBH abundance. Owing to the dependence of our results on astrophysical uncertainties, such as those affecting the constraints on the abundance of PBHs, they cannot be regarded as conclusive with respect to the nature of the detected event. At the same time, our analysis highlights the potential of subsolar gravitational wave events as a probe of PBHs and their contribution to dark matter.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 7 pages, 2 figures. Accepted for publication in Physics Letters B

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Stability of Vacuum and Quantum Dynamics in Anti-de Sitter Spacetimes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Canonical quantization on scalar and Maxwell fields is studied for the stability of vacuum and construction of quantum dynamics in Anti-de Sitter spacetimes. The $ξRφ^2$ term in the Lagrangian of scalar field with $ξ> 5/48$ (mass term just introduces shift of $ξ$) can cause the spectrum of the self-adjoint Hamiltonian with negative value not bounded from below. The degrees of freedom corresponding to the negative values are constrained system and are ambiguous in space direction and in commutation relation. The only other algebra accommodated in 3-dimensional space consistent with locality, the anti-commutation relation, is definite confronting the constrain, and trivialize the negative spectrum to be inactive and absent degrees of freedom. Thus only the physical bosons corresponding to the non-negative spectrum span the Hilbert space. For the Maxwell fields as another constrained system, the gauge invariant canonical energy momentum tensor straightforwardly leads to the gauge invariant non-negative Hamiltonian. The 2-dimensional independent dynamical degrees of freedom are quantized in temporal gauge. The energy momentum tensors for both quantized fields are renormalized to be finite at operator level, which guarantee the stable vacuum maximally symmetric and the particle Fock states the representation of the AdS symmetry SO(2,3). Adopting Weinberg's framework, the new covariant free quantum scalar field is reconstructed in the corresponding mode function space isomorphic to the free boson Hilbert space, allowing various local effective interaction terms among fields introduced. The Yang-Feldman equations relate the free fields and the interacting fields with the Green functions determined properly in the mode function space.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 27 pages, no figures. This version emphasizes that the negative energy sector is constrained, leaving a physical Hilbert space with a stable vacuum. Following Weinberg, a covariant free scalar field is reconstructed in a mode function space isomorphic to the physical Hilbert space. Interactions follow Yang Feldman equations, with Green functions defined in the physical mode function space

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Loop integrals in de Sitter spacetime: The parity-split IBP system and $\mathrm{d}\log$-form differential equations
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We develop integration-by-parts (IBP) reduction and differential equations for massive loop integrals of cosmological correlators in de Sitter (dS) spacetime, demonstrating the feasibility of this approach. We identify a structural property of the dS IBP system: for an $n$-propagator family, it splits into $2^n$ closed subsystems classified by the parity of the propagator indices. We further formulate a Baikov representation for loop integrals in dS space and derive the corresponding dimensional recurrence relations. In flat spacetime, intersection theory shows that $\mathrm{d}\log$-form master integrands lead to $\mathrm{d}\log$-form differential equations. Motivated by fibration intersection theory, we conjecture that this construction extends to dS integrands involving Hankel functions. We verify this conjecture in the one-loop bubble family and determine the associated alphabet.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 8+5 pages, 1 attachment; v2: typo fixed, references added; v3: corrected the master integrals and the alphabet

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Quantum geometric inflation
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Geometric Inflation adds an infinite tower of curvature invariants to the Einstein-Hilbert action while preserving certain key features such as leading to second order modified Friedmann equations for FRW backgrounds. Sourcing them with a perfect barotropic fluid can easily produce a slow-roll inflationary regime, no inflaton field is required. In this work, we perform the Wheeler-DeWitt quantization of minisuperspace Geometric Inflation models. First, we construct an effective 1D FRW action and perform the Hamiltonian formulation using both Ostrogradsky's approach and Dirac's algorithm for constrained systems. The Lagrangian and Hamiltonian treatment of the perfect fluid is based on Schutz's formalism. Second, we postulate the Wheeler-DeWitt equation and investigate its solutions both analytically and numerically. For radiation we are led to a system of fractional differential equations for which we use Caputo fractional derivative operator. We construct wave packets in momentum space, with the fluid's variable acting as external time parameter.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Non-minimally coupled Weyl connection gravity in the Solar System and at the Galactic Center
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We explore the phenomenological viability of non-minimally coupled Weyl connection gravity by confronting its static, spherically symmetric black hole solutions with classical weak-field Solar System tests and stellar-orbit observations near Sgr A*. In this geometric framework, non-metricity is encoded via a Weyl vector field, giving rise to two distinct families of Schwarzschild-like vacuum solutions characterized by a free parameter \(ω\) with dimensions of length. We compute the corrections to four classical observables---gravitational redshift, Mercury's perihelion advance, light deflection, and radar echo delay---and derive stringent lower bounds on \(ω\) using current observational data. For Solution I (purely radial Weyl vector), the leading metric corrections scale as \(1/ω\), yielding bounds as strong as \(ω\gtrsim 10^{30}\) m from perihelion precession. For Solution II (time-radial Weyl vector), the corrections scale as \(1/ω^2\), resulting in weaker constraints, with \(ω\gtrsim 10^{20}\) m from the same test. This marked difference arises from the distinct behavior of the linear corrections in each solution: while Solution I exhibits an unsuppressed linear term \(2r/ω\) that dominates in the Solar System regime, Solution II features a linear term suppressed by an additional factor of \(M/ω\), making the quadratic term \(-r^2/4ω^2\) dominant throughout. We then analyze stellar orbits near the Galactic Center, finding that current observations of the S2 star provide complementary constraints on both solutions. (...)
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 27 pages, 2 figures, v2: 23 pages (two columns), 2 figures, 3 tables, accepted for publication in EPJC

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Chaos bound for spinning particles in Kerr-Newman-AdS black holes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: In this paper, we investigate the chaos bound violation of spinning charged test particles in the Kerr--Newman--AdS spacetime by comparing the Lyapunov exponent of unstable circular orbits with the black hole surface gravity. We find that the violation is governed by the relative balance between the local orbital-instability and surface gravity scales, while spacetime rotation, charge, AdS curvature, and particle spin modify this balance in different ways. In rotating backgrounds, the violation depends strongly on the relative orientation between the particle total angular momentum and the black hole rotation, with anti-aligned configurations generally favoring violation. Particle spin further shifts the violation boundary through spin--curvature coupling, although its influence remains comparatively weak over the spin range considered. The cosmological constant has a background-dependent influence. These results show that the parameter dependence of chaos bound violation reflects the competition between the local orbital-instability and surface gravity scales.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Non-Stationary Wormholes and Matter Source Reconstruction in General Relativity
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We investigate non-stationary wormhole geometries in General Relativity embedded in evolving cosmological backgrounds. We employ a Simpson-Visser-like regularization of the temporal coordinate of the $(n+1)$-dimensional FLRW metric, together with a homogeneous Cuscuton field, to construct cosmological backgrounds in which the scale factor remains finite and non-zero at the would-be initial singularity. We then consider two specific dynamical wormhole geometries: the four-dimensional defect wormhole and the topologically charged Perry-Mann type wormhole. We show that the former can be supported by a canonical scalar field with vanishing potential, while the latter requires a mimetic matter sector to support its spatial structure, with the Cuscuton governing the cosmological evolution in both cases. We subsequently generalize the analysis to a separable non-stationary spacetime and derive a scaling condition that strongly constrains the admissible matter sources. In particular, for minimally coupled scalar and nonlinear electrodynamics fields, this condition removes the functional freedom available in static reconstruction schemes. We show that, within this framework, regular, asymptotically flat wormhole geometries cannot be obtained while simultaneously satisfying the required smoothness and reflection symmetry conditions. Our results illustrate both the possibility of constructing specific non-stationary wormholes in regular cosmological backgrounds and the restrictions that arise when attempting to generalize such constructions to arbitrary spatial geometries.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: No-Go Theorem for Phantom Crossing in Scalar-Tensor Gravity with Non-Minimal Derivative Coupling and Soft Scale-Invariance Breaking
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Recent baryon acoustic oscillation measurements from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI 2024) reveal a preference for dynamical dark energy with an equation of state parameter crossing the phantom divide ($w < -1$) at low redshifts. We investigate whether this phantom crossing can be realized within scale-invariant scalar-tensor theories featuring non-minimal derivative coupling (NMDC) between the scalar field and the Einstein tensor. Employing the effective field theory of dark energy formalism, we systematically derive the ghost-free and gradient stability conditions, and examine their compatibility with the swampland conjectures from quantum gravity. We establish three rigorous no-go theorems demonstrating that: (i)~phantom crossing necessitates $ξ_{\text{eff}} < 0$, directly violating the no-ghost stability requirement $ξ_{\text{eff}} > 0$; (ii)~the swampland de Sitter and distance conjectures independently obstruct phantom crossing; and (iii)~these theoretical obstructions are mutually reinforcing. Our results show that scale-invariant NMDC models cannot account for the DESI preference for $w < -1$, providing robust theoretical guidance for dark energy model building beyond this class.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Observational Indistinguishability and the Beginning of the Universe
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Can we infer whether all of physical reality began to exist? Several novel results are offered suggesting a negative verdict. First, two necessary (but not necessarily sufficient) conditions are offered for a cosmic beginning. Second, I discuss three theorems which show that, in a wide range of spacetimes, observers cannot infer the global structure of their spacetime; one of the three shows that spacetimes satisfying a condition necessary for a cosmic beginning are observationally indistinguishable from spacetimes which do not satisfy that condition. Next, I offer two extensions to the aforementioned theorems. The two extensions show that, in an equally wide range of spacetimes, observers cannot collect sufficient data to determine whether the application conditions for the class singularity theorems are satisfied or whether their spacetime satisfies the two necessary conditions for a cosmic beginning. Lastly, a reply is offered to the objection that the skeptical consequences of the aforementioned theorems can be overcome with induction. Importantly, all past singular dust FLRW spacetimes are observationally indistinguishable from counterparts which, while sharing a number of important local properties, either do not include a singularity to the past of every point or else do not have the sort of time ordering intuitively required for a cosmic beginning.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: Fixed some mathematical issues from an earlier draft. Deleted a section on confirmation theory. Expanded the section on induction

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Gravitational redshift of broadband relativistic quantum photons
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Gravitational redshift is a key prediction of general relativity that has been experimentally verified. Nevertheless, its existence in the context of relativistic and quantum physics has not yet been established. We employ linearized quantum gravity to study the effects of quantum coherence on gravitational redshift of broadband photons that interact with a planet via graviton exchange. We find that gravitational redshift, as predicted by general relativity, occurs when the initial photonic state contains no quantum coherence between orthogonal photonic modes, such as position states. If quantum coherence is initially present, different photonic modes overlap, a genuine quantum correction occurs solely for single-photon states. Our work not only explains gravitational redshift as the interaction of gravitons and photons in flat spacetime, but also shows that deviations from the theory occur already at low energies when quantum interference of photonic states is important.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Semiclassical state on algebra of observables for de Sitter space and time reversal symmetry
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: In de Sitter static patch holography, coupling bulk quantum fields to an observer's dynamical clock yields a type II$_1$ von Neumann algebra $\mathcal{M}_+$ of gauge-invariant observables. However, the unique tracial state on this algebra fails to reproduce semiclassical bulk correlation functions. We resolve this issue by introducing a family of heavy-clock states, representing an observer reference frame with heavy inertia. We prove that in the heavy-clock limit, $n$-point correlation functions of gauge-invariant dressed observables reproduce the bulk quantum field correlation functions on de Sitter spacetime. Furthermore, we investigate a generalized observer Hamiltonian $\widehat{H}_{\rm obs}=|\widehatπ|$ that incorporates both forward-running ($π\geq 0$) and backward-running ($π<0$) clocks. The resulting von Neumann algebra $\mathcal{M}$ of gauge-invariant observables remains a type~II$_1$ factor and is isomorphic to $\mathcal{M}_+\otimes M_2(\mathbb{C})$, where $M_2(\mathbb{C})$ is the algebra of $2\times2$ complex matrices transforming between the two clock orientations. Time-reversal symmetry is implemented in this setting as an anti-unitary operator that exchanges the two clock orientations, yielding a type~II$_1$ von Neumann algebra $\mathcal{F}$ of gauge-invariant, time-reversal-invariant observables. We generalize the heavy-clock state construction to both $\mathcal{M}$ and $\mathcal{F}$, showing that $n$-point correlation functions calculated in heavy-clock states match the corresponding semiclassical bulk correlation functions. Finally, by coupling Einstein gravity to the Brown--Kuchař dust field, we derive the observer Hamiltonian $\widehat{H}_{\rm obs}=|\widehatπ|$ from a perturbative reduction along the observer's worldline in the $G \to 0$ limit. This provides a field-theoretic foundation for the observer model developed in this work.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Evidence of Taste-Symmetry restoration for Kähler-Dirac fermions on Euclidean Dynamical Triangulations
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We study the spectrum of two-particle bound states of Kähler-Dirac fermions coupled via gravity in Euclidean Dynamical Triangulations (EDT). We work in the quenched approximation, where the geometry is allowed to fluctuate, but there is no back-reaction from the matter on the geometry. The Kähler-Dirac action respects an exact $U(1)$ symmetry that is related to continuum chiral symmetry, and this $U(1)$ symmetry ensures that some of the bound-state masses vanish in the chiral limit of vanishing fermion bare mass. The bound-state masses that are not protected by the $U(1)$ symmetry do not vanish in the chiral limit, but the scale associated with the symmetry breaking does not appear to be a physical scale like the Planck mass or the curvature scale of the emergent de Sitter background. Rather, the mass scale associated with this non-degeneracy appears to be a positive power of the lattice spacing, decreasing as the continuum limit is approached. This suggests that Kähler-Dirac fermions in EDT can be interpreted as the gravity analog of staggered fermions in flat-space lattice field theories, with similar behavior.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Stochastic Path Sampler For Lattice Field Theory
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: In lattice field theory, target distributions are known only up to normalization, (\tildeπ(φ)\propto e^{-S(φ)}), while the partition function is intractable. Markov chain Monte Carlo simulations often become inefficient near phase transitions or the continuum limit due to critical slowing down. In this work, we propose a novel sampler based on nonequilibrium thermodynamics, called Stochastic Path Sampler (SPS), which can generate configurations for the unnormalized target distribution without requiring training data. The central idea of SPS is to establish a trajectory-level balance for learnable forward and backward stochastic dynamics between two equilibrium states, namely the prior and target distributions. This is achieved by minimizing the path-space variational free energy, equivalently an entropy-production upper bound, defined by the log-ratio of forward and auxiliary backward trajectory measures, thereby enhancing the reversibility of the forward and backward processes. The learned forward process provides independent proposals, which are subsequently corrected by an extended-space Independence Metropolis--Hastings step. In two-dimensional (φ^4) theory, we demonstrate that our neural sampler can achieve the same sampling quality as HMC but with a much shorter autocorrelation time in the critical region. This sampler offers a stochastic-quantization-inspired route to data-free proposal construction for lattice field theory by leveraging a variational free-energy principle derived from path-space irreversibility.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Perturbative Renormalization of Noether Currents in SYM with Improved Discretizations
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We investigate the perturbative renormalization of Noether currents associated with chiral symmetry and supersymmetry transformations in $\mathcal{N}=1$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory, regularized on the lattice using improved discretizations. In particular, we study the chiral current and the supercurrent operator for a broad class of lattice actions: Wilson fermions with one-step stout-smeared links and a clover term, together with a family of Symanzik-improved gluon actions. Since the supercurrent mixes with both gauge-invariant and gauge-noninvariant operators, we compute the corresponding renormalization factors and mixing coefficients at one-loop order. We analyze the impact of improved gluon and gluino actions on this mixing pattern and investigate whether suitable choices of lattice parameters, such as the clover and stout coefficients, can reduce unwanted lattice artifacts at one loop. Our results provide perturbative input for the implementation of Ward identities and for matching lattice observables to their continuum counterparts, while also offering guidance for simulations aimed at restoring supersymmetry in the continuum limit.
High Energy Physics - Lattice.comment: 10 pages, 2 figures, 1 table, Contribution to the 43rd International Symposium on Lattice Field Theory (Lattice 2026)

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: A brief introduction to dispersive methods
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: These lectures aim to provide a basic introduction to dispersive methods and their modern applications to the phenomenology of the Standard Model at low energy. This approach exploits analyticity properties of Green functions and scattering amplitude, often combined with unitarity constraints. To find a logically coherent set of topics in this vast subject, I start with the two-point Green's function, show that this needs the three-point function as input which in turn needs the four-point function. The sequence stops here, just like these lectures, because the four-point function is related only to itself (if one ignores inelastic effects), I will discuss these dispersion relations both in the case of toy models, simple scalar theories, as well as in the phenomenologically relevant case of QCD.
High Energy Physics - Lattice.comment: 46 pages. Lectures give at the CERN-Nordic Lattice school "Continuum Foundations of Lattice Gauge Theories". Few typos corrected. Agrees with published version

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Solutions of Roy equations for variable pion mass
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary:
The Roy equations for the $S$ and $P$ waves are solved for pion
  masses below the physical value in the region between threshold and
  $s_A=0.84\GeV^2$. The analysis is based on the assumption that the
  phenomenological input above $s_A$ can be used essentially
  unchanged. Moreover, for $M_π\le M_{π,\mathrm{phys}}$, the chiral
  perturbation theory predictions for the two $S$-wave scattering lengths
  provide a very reliable additional input to the Roy equations. The
  outcome is an accurate description of the $S$ and $P$ partial waves as
  the light-quark masses decrease towards the chiral limit. As a test of
  the approach, we evaluate the first few threshold parameters of the $S$,
  $P$, and $D$ waves via Wanders' sum rules and find excellent agreement
  with chiral perturbation theory across the entire range $0 \le M_π\le
  M_{π,\mathrm{phys}}$. We further solve the Roy equations for pion masses
  above the physical value (up to $240\MeV$) and show that the resulting
  solutions agree well with existing lattice data at $M_π=239\MeV$. The
  present work paves the way for analyses of lattice data that fully
  incorporate the constraints of analyticity, unitarity, and crossing
  symmetry, and provides the basis for an accurate study of the dependence
  of the $σ$ and $ρ$ resonances on the light-quark masses, both of
  which will be addressed in future work.

Atomic Physics.title: Information-theoretic measures of electron correlation in a double quantum dot
Atomic Physics.summary: In this work, we investigated how variations in spatial confinement affect the electron correlation between two electrons in a symmetric double quantum dot. In strong confinement regime, the ground-state energy can be obtained using the Hartree-Fock method neglecting the electron-electron repulsion term. Under a weaker confinement, the FCI method provides a more accurate description. Using the mutual information as a measure of correlation, we determine the confinement regions where electronic motion is uncorrelated. We conjecture that the Shannon entropy can serve as a qualitative guide to to study the electron correlation. We identified an approximately linear relationship between mutual information and relative correlation energy.

Atomic Physics.title: Collective tunnel ionization in atomic systems
Atomic Physics.summary: We present a theory of the collective tunnel effect in atomic systems subject to strong low-frequency laser fields. Using an analytic semi-classical method and numerical solution to the time-dependent Schrödinger equation we demonstrate the collective channel of the nonsequential double ionization in a model two-dimensional two-electron system with ionization potentials reproducing those of neutral xenon and of the negative bromine ion. Collective tunneling in the presence of the electron-electron repulsion comprises the joint sub-barrier motion of the two electrons along quantum trajectories transversely shifted in opposite directions with respect to the direction of the external electric field. Analytic results for the rates of collective tunneling allow indicating the intervals of laser intensity, where this effect can be expected to compete with sequential tunneling in helium, xenon, and negative bromine. Momentum distributions of the electron pairs carry clear signatures of the collective channel in the form of shoulders in the direction lateral to the field polarization.

Atomic Physics.title: Theory of Sub-Doppler Spectroscopy of Alkali Metal Vapors in the Field of Counterpropagating Bichromatic Laser Beams: Probe Beam Regime
Atomic Physics.summary: Sub-Doppler resonances observed in miniature cells ($V \ll 1 cm^3$) with Rb or Cs atoms in the field of counterpropagating bichromatic laser beams are of interest for the creation of a miniature quantum frequency standard (QFS) of the optical range. However, a theory of these resonances that takes into full account the real structure of energy levels in an atom has not yet been constructed, which would make it possible to obtain explicit analytical expressions for the absorption coefficient of the medium. This paper addresses this gap using the density matrix formalism and the algebra of irreducible tensor operators. Namely, we obtained an analytical expression for the absorption coefficient of the probe beam in the presence of a more intense counterpropagating beam (pump-probe regime). Moreover, the calculations were carried out for arbitrary parameters of laser beam polarization, arbitrary angular momenta of optical dipole transitions in the atom and various relaxation processes. The constructed theory allows us to correctly take into account the simultaneous action of various nonlinear optical effects, in contrast to the simplified three-level model of the atom, and also to investigate the partial contribution of each of them to the overall observed resonant circuit. The analysis performed, in particular, made it possible to predict an increase in the amplitude of the sub-Doppler resonance when using counterpropagating light beams with opposite circular polarizations in relation to the configuration of counterpropagating beams with orthogonal linear polarizations, which is often used in practice.

Atomic Physics.title: Breakdown of sequential tunnel ionization in ultrashort electromagnetic pulses
Atomic Physics.summary: We consider double ionization of one- and two-dimensional atomic systems modeling neutral helium, xenon and the negative bromine ion in intense low-frequency electromagnetic fields. By solving numerically the two-electron time-dependent Schr{ö}dinger equation under conditions which exclude recollisions, we demonstrate that while for pulses of a few tens of femtoseconds duration and longer the sequential single-electron approximation perfectly describes the ionization dynamics, for pulses as short as few femtoseconds this picture breaks down entirely, and the electron-electron interaction suppresses the rate of ionization by roughly one order of magnitude.

Atomic Physics.title: Collision inside an atom: quantum ion-atom dynamics
Atomic Physics.summary: Rydberg atoms occupy a central role in quantum science; their loosely bound outer electron gives rise to properties that enable quantum information processing1 or the formation of exotic molecular bonds2. Beyond these roles, they have been proposed as a neutral platform for the observation of quantum effects in collisions and reactions of the ionic core with neutral particles3, 4, a long-standing goal of ion-based chemistry and physics. However, all of the experimental results so far could be explained using a classical description of the internuclear motion5. Here we demonstrate cold collisions inside a Rydberg helium atom, achieved by merging helium Rydberg and ground-state helium beams and imaging individual scattering events. We resolve the fully quantum-coherent motion and observe matter-wave diffraction and tunnelling-driven shape resonances down to collision energies of 90 mK. In the case of identical helium nuclei, we demonstrate a new regime of identical-particle Mott interference6, where quantum statistics begin to govern the total scattering cross section. For distinct isotopes, we show the breakdown of the Born-Oppenheimer approximation and benchmark parameter-free, state-of-the-art theory. We directly measure the helium isotope ionization-energy difference to be 15.0 +/- 0.1 K. Our experiments establish Rydberg atoms as a platform for the direct observation of quantum dynamics with a general class of ions, atoms and molecules.

Atomic Physics.title: A Photonic Integrated Light Generation, Control, and Delivery Engine for Creating Cold Atoms
Atomic Physics.summary: The creation of cold atoms underpins quantum sensing and precision metrology, computing, timekeeping, and fundamental science experiments. Miniaturizing the lasers and optical infrastructure, which occupy over 80% of the volume of these experiments, through photonic integration could improve robustness, reliability, and manufacturability while reducing cost and enabling portable space-based precision measurements and quantum tools for non-experts. Yet, there has been limited progress towards integration of the laser and optical infrastructure required to generate cold atoms onto a single chip. We demonstrate a photonic engine that generates, controls, and delivers precision light to create cold atoms in a rubidium 3-dimensional magneto-optical trap (3D-MOT). We integrate on a single chip two frequency-agile self-injection-locked lasers, laser frequency and intensity control, passive beam combining and splitting, signal monitoring, and high-efficiency beam delivery to a rubidium vapor cell. The integrated engine is shown to support multiple functions required for generating cold atoms including stable generation of low-noise cooling and repump light, frequency control for atom spectroscopy and stabilization, real-time laser monitoring, routing for laser offset locking, optical power modulation, and large-area three-beam delivery of 3 mW to the physics package. Fully electrically controlled, the engine enables sustained 3D-MOT operation, trapping more than 1 million atoms at an average temperature of 350 uK and supporting atom-number and temperature measurements. These results demonstrate the first single-chip integration of light generation, control, and delivery for cold-atom generation, offering a path toward smaller, more robust, and manufacturable cold-atom systems for applications including cold-atom clocks and sensors.

Atomic Physics.title: Scattering phase shifts from overlap relations in the $J$-matrix method
Atomic Physics.summary: We present an approach to the quantum mechanical scattering problem in which computation of a wave function and determination of scattering parameters are separate steps. This approach is built on the $J$-matrix formalism, but in place of the usual $J$-matrix procedures, we introduce a novel formula that extracts phase shifts accurately from scattering states computed in a square-integrable basis. This formula is closely analogous to existing integral relations or overlap integrals in a (continuous) position basis. We then demonstrate the extraction of phase shifts from wave functions in single-channel potential scattering. For a soft but realistic nucleon-nucleon potential, Daejeon16, we obtain good phase shifts with as few as six oscillator basis states, using the Lippmann-Schwinger equation to obtain scattering states at arbitrary energies even in this highly truncated space. These results constitute a step towards calculations in which scattering observables are extracted from scattering states generated in a many-body framework with square-integrable basis functions, such as the configuration-interaction shell model.

Atomic Physics.title: Fast charging of quantum batteries assisted by nonlinear couplings
Atomic Physics.summary: Charger-mediated quantum batteries offer promising opportunities for efficient energy transfer and storage at the quantum level, with potential advantages beyond their classical counterparts. Here, we theoretically demonstrate that nonlinear charger-battery interactions can substantially accelerate the charging of quantum batteries. In the weak-driving regime, sufficiently strong nonlinear coupling can dominate over the effect of dephasing and significantly reduce the charging time. In the strong- and optimal-driving regimes, where the optimal driving strength maximizes the steady-state ergotropy in the linear-coupling regime, nonlinear coupling gives rise to a new optimum in the charging time beyond that of the linear-coupling regime, accompanied by nearly critically damped dynamics. Remarkably, even in the absence of external driving, nonlinear coupling alone can substantially reduce the charging time, providing an alternative route toward fast battery charging. Our results establish nonlinear charger-battery coupling as an effective resource for accelerating quantum-battery charging and broaden the scope of interaction-enabled quantum advantages in energy transfer and storage.

Atomic Physics.title: Resonant photoionization dynamics during optical trapping of lithium atoms
Atomic Physics.summary: Photoionization induced by trapping and auxiliary laser fields is an inherent feature of many laser-cooling and optical trapping experiments, yet its microscopic dynamics are rarely investigated directly. In this work, we employ a reaction microscope implementing an event-by-event photoionization time retrieval technique to extend momentum-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy to continuous-wave laser--atom interactions. We investigate low-intensity multicolor photoionization of laser-cooled lithium atoms confined in an all-optical trap. Complete three-dimensional electron momentum distributions and kinetic-energy spectra recorded for different laser wavelengths and polarization configurations identify resonant excitation of the $5p$ and $5f$ states and reveal an additional ionization channel following spontaneous decay from the $5f$ to the $4d$ state. A pronounced polarization dependence of the photoionization yield is explained by magnetic-sublevel selection rules and the coherent interference of different virtual excitation pathways. These results demonstrate that reaction microscopy combined with event-by-event time reconstruction provides a powerful approach for investigating microscopic electronic dynamics in laser-cooled atomic systems and offers new insight into photoionization processes occurring during optical trapping.

Atomic Physics.title: Photoemission study of Iodoalkanes
Atomic Physics.summary: Core level atomic photoionization is influenced by the molecular environment of the emitting atom. To probe this influence we used extreme ultraviolet (XUV) radiation to measure the I$\left(4d\to\varepsilon f \right)$ photoemission of four iodine substituted alkanes in the range from 60 eV to 160 eV photon energy. Using two detection angles relative to light polarization allowed us to extract and compare the asymmetry parameter of the investigated compounds. These results are in agreement with theory by Pi and Landsman (L.-W. Pi and A. Landsman, Attosecond time delay in photoionization of noble-gas and halogen atoms, Applied Sciences 8, 322 (2018)) and previous experiments by Olney et al. (T. N. Olney, G. Cooper, and C. Brion, Quantitative studies of the photoabsorption (4.5-488 ev) and photoionization (9-59.5 ev) of methyl iodide using dipole electron impact techniques, Chemical Physics 232, 211 (1998)) for iodomethane. 2-iodopropane behaves nearly identical to iodomethane, while for iodoethane and 1-iodopropane we find a distinct and consistent, energy dependant difference most prominent at around 130 eV photon energy. This further proves the influence of the chemical environment on core level photoionization. Due to the sensitivity on the exact positions of the carbon atoms and the energy dependence we hypothesise this difference is caused by intramolecular scattering of the outgoing photoelectron wave packet, causing changes in the angular distribution.

Quantum Physics.title: Gaussian entanglement and quantum communication: geodesic optimization and multimode bounds
Quantum Physics.summary: Loss and noise limit the use of light to distribute entanglement, transmit quantum information, and establish secret keys. Gaussian states have a compact description in terms of means and covariance matrices, but their entanglement still requires global optimization. We develop a framework for computing Gaussian-restricted versions of the relative entropy of entanglement and Rains entanglement. An integral representation reveals a convex geometry under matrix geometric means and reduces Gaussian Rains entanglement to relative entropy minimized over Gaussian states with positive partial transpose. We obtain unique optimal reference states and additivity for independent Gaussian input states. Our convex-majorization algorithm has an explicit geometric convergence rate, uniform in the faithful regularization parameter and valid for pure input states. Controlled numerical integration and approximate convex subproblem solutions give a bit-complexity bound that is polynomial in accuracy bits for each fixed rational input covariance matrix, with explicit dependence on covariance size. These calculations bound extractable entanglement and, through the relative entropy of entanglement, extractable secret key. Teleportation simulation, energy allocation, and a convex optimization of passive-basis loss cores give bounds on quantum and private communication under an input-energy constraint, allowing arbitrary two-way classically assisted protocols. Two- and three-mode examples compare the bounds with achievable rates, including matching pure-loss benchmarks. Finally, we separate the Gaussian-restricted quantities from their unrestricted counterparts and give a photon-number truncation method with controlled error for computing the latter.

Quantum Physics.title: On the coincidence of discrete and continuous definitions of Entanglement of Formation
Quantum Physics.summary:
It is proved that every Borel ensemble of pure states on a separable bipartite Hilbert space with finite average entanglement admits a countable ensemble with the same barycenter and arbitrarily small additional average entanglement. Consequently, the discrete and continuous versions of the Entanglement of Formation coincide on the whole space of states of infinite-dimensional bipartite quantum system (with infinite values allowed).
  The main idea of the proof (realized with the AI-assistance) is the identification of a Borel ensemble of pure bipartite states with a Borel probability measure on the unit sphere of the space of Hilbert--Schmidt operators followed by dividing the support of this measure into appropriate cells and replacing each cell by its conditional barycenter. The resulting countable ensemble is obtained by a recursive construction.
Quantum Physics.comment: 14 pages, preliminary vesion, any comments are welcome

Quantum Physics.title: $\mathsf{EFI}\Leftrightarrow\mathsf{1PRS}$
Quantum Physics.summary: A series of recent works has established EFI pairs as the "minimal" assumption for quantum cryptography. Recently, Cavalar et al. [CCC+26] showed that EFI pairs are equivalent to non-uniform expanding single-copy pseudorandom state generators (1PRS), and obtained a non-uniform meta-complexity characterization of EFI pairs. We remove the non-uniformity in their construction and prove that EFI pairs are equivalent to expanding 1PRS. As a corollary, we obtain the first uniform meta-complexity characterization of EFI pairs. Together with the equivalence of statistically verifiable one-way state generators and commitments proved by Batra and Jain [BJ24], this gives a quantum analogue of the classical equivalence between one-way functions, commitments, and pseudorandom generators.

Quantum Physics.title: Relative-Entropy Geometry and Convergence in Nonconvex Wiretap Optimization
Quantum Physics.summary: We develop and analyze an entropic descent method for a nonconvex optimization problem on probability simplices arising in classical and quantum secure communication. The optimization variables describe a randomized encoder, allowing its input distribution and stochastic preprocessing to be optimized jointly. An exact relative-entropy identity yields a channel-independent majorization bound and an explicit mirror-descent iteration with a fixed unit step size. We establish quantitative descent, convergence of objective values, and stationarity of accumulation points on their support faces for arbitrary finite classical channels, without assuming degradedness or less noisiness. For strictly positive transition matrices, a square-root parametrization and a Kurdyka--Łojasiewicz argument establish finite length of the transformed trajectory and convergence of the entire sequence, including limits on the simplex boundary. For less-noisy channels, a restricted convex formulation admits global convergence with an explicit \(O(1/t)\) objective-error bound. We extend the relative-entropy construction to noncommuting quantum outputs and derive monotone alternating updates for covariant encoders, including correlated preprocessing over a fixed block. Numerical experiments compare the method with analytic benchmarks and constrained optimization, reveal multiple attracting values, and demonstrate strict improvements from stochastic preprocessing.

Quantum Physics.title: Deterministic and programmable generation of mechanical multipartite entangled states
Quantum Physics.summary: Multimode mechanical resonators offer a large set of densely packed, long-lived bosonic modes within a single compact device, making them attractive for quantum simulation, quantum information processing, and quantum-enhanced sensing. Many such applications rely on multipartite entanglement, yet deterministic mechanical entanglement has so far been largely limited to pairs of modes. Here we demonstrate the deterministic and programmable preparation of multipartite entangled states among the phonon modes of a high-overtone bulk acoustic wave resonator coupled to a superconducting transmon qubit. By sequentially applying optimal-control-engineered isometries between the qubit and successive modes, we generate matrix product states of bond dimension two, including $W$, Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ), and cluster states. We fully characterize these states via quantum state tomography and certify genuine multipartite entanglement among up to four modes. We further demonstrate correlated-noise sensing by exploiting the complementary decoherence responses of the stored $W$ and GHZ states, isolating inter-mode phase correlations from local decoherence and placing quantitative bounds on collective dephasing. Our results establish a scalable approach to preparing multipartite entangled states in mechanical systems, with promising applications in multiparameter sensing and tests of quantum mechanics with massive objects.

Quantum Physics.title: Quantum-enhanced mechanical sensing with machine-learning estimation
Quantum Physics.summary: Massive mechanical oscillators couple directly to forces, accelerations and gravity, making them attractive probes of new physics and of quantum mechanics at macroscopic scales. Pushing sensitivities beyond the standard quantum limit for signals of unknown phase requires non-Gaussian quantum states, whose metrological advantage has so far been confined to lighter systems such as trapped ions. Here we operate a microgram-scale acoustic mode of a high-overtone bulk acoustic wave resonator as a phase-insensitive quantum-enhanced sensor. A transmon qubit prepares the mode in Fock states of up to seven phonons by optimal control, and resolves its phonon-number distribution after interaction with a weak resonant signal. Bayesian analysis yields a Fisher information five times the vacuum value, a 7.0 dB gain in signal-amplitude sensitivity over any classical probe state, irrespective of its energy, currently limited by state preparation infidelities. We then train a neural network on the measured sensor response to perform Bayesian estimation without any analytical model of the system, showing the same sensitivity gain with half the systematic bias. Our results establish acoustic resonators prepared in non-Gaussian states as quantum-enhanced probes for high-frequency gravitational waves, dark matter and wave-function collapse.

Quantum Physics.title: Fluctuation-dissipation structure of quantum geometry
Quantum Physics.summary: Geometry of quantum states is a fundamental research area with applications ranging from topological materials in condensed matter to variational algorithms in quantum information. Due to their relative simplicity, pure states are often studied, while mixed states are generally needed, for instance to have nonzero temperatures or other statistical mixtures. Mixed-state geometry, however, is much more challenging and has so far lacked any overall structure that relates distance and curvature, like the Kähler structure does for pure states. This work introduces that missing structure. We show that it has the physical meaning of fluctuation-dissipation---by identifying distance with fluctuations and curvature with linear response---and becomes the known structure for pure states, but is non-Kähler otherwise. This paints a simple picture that unifies fluctuation-dissipation and geometry of quantum states. It also applies on parameter spaces, as encountered in condensed matter or estimation theory. Our picture implies that the geometry contains all linear responses and fluctuations, proves the usual fluctuation-dissipation relation, explains that quantum geometry is present in any sum rule, and allows one to geometrically characterize generic transport behaviors.
Quantum Physics.comment: 6 pages + Methods, RevTeX, 2 figures; updated version with improved presentation

Quantum Physics.title: A thermodynamic analysis of nonsecular master equations, beyond strict energy conservation and Gibbs equilibrium state
Quantum Physics.summary: We present a systematic thermodynamic analysis of nonsecular GKLS master equations. When some energy transitions in the system are comparable with the dissipative rate, the secular approximation is not valid, and the positivity of the dynamics must be ensured via other approximations. The dynamics then presents features reminiscent from strong coupling to the environment: e.g. the equilibrium state with an environment at thermal equilibrium is not a Gibbs state of the local system Hamiltonian and the dynamics couples energy coherences and populations. Nonetheless, we build a unified, consistent thermodynamic framework for those dynamics. We focus on two approximations beyond the full secular approximation (the local and the more accurate geometric-arithmetic approximations), and then employ systematic perturbation theory on microscopic expressions for the first and second law of thermodynamics which relate irreversibility to the increase of system-environment correlations. We show that, in spite of the weak system-bath coupling, the system-bath interaction energy participates to the energy balance, and is directly linked to the Lamb-shift Hamiltonian. We compare this microscopic entropy production with the definition based on the contractivity of the reduced system dynamics (Spohn inequality). We show that, unlike for secular master equations, the two entropy production rates differ because of the presence of non-vanishing stationary coherences in the energy eigenbasis. However, in the case of a single thermal bath, the difference is purely transient, and no work can be cyclically extracted from the steady-state despite its non-Gibbs form. Finally, we illustrate our results with simple examples, clarifying and completing the thermodynamic picture of Markovian dynamics in the quantum regime.
Quantum Physics.comment: 18 pages for main text, 9 pages for the appendix and 4 figures

Quantum Physics.title: The quantum lifetime of a future-referential feedback loop: certified index, architecture floor, and thermal bonus
Quantum Physics.summary: A quantum feedback loop that returns information from a forward simulation to an earlier internal time induces a completely positive trace-preserving map on a message register; iterating that map eventually destroys its ability to carry entanglement. The entanglement-breaking index N = n_EB(Phi), the round at which this happens, is studied along two axes, interaction and bath. On the interaction axis, strict contraction onto a full-rank fixed point forces N finite in every dimension, via an explicit separable ball around the limiting Choi state, and across 3997 sampled channels index and stability gap are one clock, N [1 - rho(A)] in [0.60, 1.50]. On the bath axis, a thermal ancilla at polarisation p = tanh(hbar omega / 2 k_B T) makes every channel quantity an exact quadratic in p, and one-sided certificates (no eigensolver) establish N = 3 at the reference circuit at every temperature. The infinite-temperature index is an architecture floor with closed form and exact measure (46.427% of circuits break entanglement in one round at infinite temperature). For exchange collisions (generalised amplitude damping) the index has a closed form and is monotone in p; for the loop the floor is not a bound: certified circuits dip below it in interior temperature windows, at a rate with Gaussian cutoff in epsilon = 1 - ||A_0||_2 (marginal exponent 2.02 [1.90, 2.16], 4.1 million circuits), and shallow-floor valleys survive to epsilon = 0.125. On a certified coupling-temperature surface, temperature moves the index by at most 3/2, the interaction by 1213/3. Applied to quantum-cognition proposals, a per-bath polarisation table at 310 K shows nuclear spins maximally hot and intramolecular vibrations frozen, and a four-input checklist replaces decoherence times by round budgets; Fisher's nuclear-spin proposal specifies its bath and storage coherence, not its processing interaction or rate.
Quantum Physics.comment: 37 pages, 1 figure, 10 tables. v2 adds the closed-form index of the thermal exchange collision (Sect. 8) and an application to quantum-cognition proposals (Sect. 13), and corrects the abstract: the 46.427% floor-1 measure holds at infinite temperature. Ancillary files in three subfolders: zero-temperature/, thermal/ (now with the eight verify_* certificates of Sect. 17) and gadc/

Quantum Physics.title: Finite-energy two-way assisted capacities: Exact formulas for multimode loss and fading
Quantum Physics.summary: We study quantum communication, entanglement distribution, and secret-key generation through multimode bosonic loss and fading channels, assisted by local quantum operations and two-way classical communication. Using sector teleportation, we determine the exact two-way quantum and secret-key capacities of multimode pure-loss channels under a mean photon-number constraint, allowing arbitrary adaptive quantum protocols. We extend these results to continuous frequency-dependent loss under a power constraint and identify the optimal allocation of photons among optical modes. For constant loss over an unlimited bandwidth, we obtain a closed-form capacity proportional to the square root of power. For randomly varying loss, we determine exact finite-energy capacities when the channel realization is publicly revealed, distinguishing knowledge before and after transmission. When fading remains unobserved, we derive capacity bounds and explicit formulas for an on/off channel. We also establish strong-converse bounds, with exact thresholds for the deterministic loss models considered here, observed fading, and unobserved fading with finitely many possible transmissivities. Under mean energy constraints, these thresholds generally exceed the corresponding finite-energy capacities. These results guide energy allocation and provide benchmarks for energy-constrained optical quantum communication with multimode signals and variable loss.

Quantum Physics.title: PULSUS: Direct Frequency-Domain Multidimensional Spectroscopy Beyond the Impulsive Rotating-Wave Approximation
Quantum Physics.summary:
We introduce PULSUS, a direct frequency-domain framework for multidimensional spectroscopy of open quantum systems beyond the impulsive rotating-wave approximation. Coherence-frequency intervals are represented through Liouvillian resolvents, while finite Gaussian pulses are incorporated through operator-valued functions of the field-free Liouvillian. This enables direct evaluation on Cartesian grids or arbitrary spectral coordinates while retaining molecular evolution during the pulse envelopes and, when required, the complete light--matter interaction.
  The implementation is validated against analytical and independent time-domain benchmarks and supports targeted spectral sampling that reduces the number of evaluated coordinates when the response is spectrally localized. A controlled hierarchy of finite-pulse, rotating-wave, short-pulse, and impulsive models separates the errors introduced by each approximation. For a coupled electronic dimer, the total impulsive-RWA error is nonmonotonic in pulse duration: an intermediate regime provides the highest accuracy, whereas ultrashort pulses expose coupling-enabled beyond-RWA pathways and longer pulses develop substantial finite-pulse corrections. These results show that the impulsive and rotating-wave approximations cannot be assumed to improve simultaneously and should be tested when quantitatively interpreting multidimensional spectra. PULSUS provides a direct frequency-domain framework for carrying out that comparison.

Quantum Physics.title: Improving device-independent quantum key distribution protocols through multiple routed Bell tests
Quantum Physics.summary: Device-independent quantum key distribution (DI-QKD) guarantees security with a minimal set of assumptions about the experimental setup. The challenge posed by its implementation could be tackled using routed Bell tests with entanglement swapping, or distant Bell state measurement (BSM) units. However, practical distances still require local tests with close-to-ideal violations or BSMs with high efficiency. We propose a DI-QKD protocol based on a multi-port BSM, and multiple sources and measurement devices, where in each round, routed tests are performed on randomly selected local devices. The violation of local Bell tests is checked even for the subset of rounds where successful BSM projections are achieved. By requiring that this violation remain consistent with the overall average, we specifically show improvements in the critical efficiencies of a three-port BSM, of up to $6\%$ in absolute terms for high visibilities. Without ideal violations, we also achieve arbitrarily small efficiencies with arbitrarily many BSM ports. Our approach enables long-distance DI-QKD, with access to highly efficient loophole-free routing setups, and multiple local tests (possibly imperfect) with very high local detection efficiencies. Remarkably, it avoids the use of quantum memories and the need for long-range Bell tests. Finally, we extend the concept of routing to dimension witnesses, where qubit-bounded sources send states to the BSM. This can be seen as a semi-device-independent extension of the aforementioned protocol.

Quantum Physics.title: Explicitly correlated ground states with a feedback-free variational hybrid algorithm
Quantum Physics.summary: Explicitly correlated methods, which represent dominant short-range correlations by a diagonal Jastrow-type correlator, are designed to accurately describe systems of strongly correlated electrons, such as the fully periodic 2D Fermi--Hubbard model. However, as the reference state is compact in momentum space whereas the correlator acts naturally in real space, there is a fundamental mismatch of bases that classical algorithms resolve only by restricting the reference or the correlator. Here we propose a hybrid algorithm in which a quantum processor prepares a low-entanglement momentum-space matrix product state (MPS), precomputed classically by the transcorrelated method at the cost of a nonvariational energy, rotates it to real space, and measures in bases fixed by the Hamiltonian. Because the measurement bases are independent of the correlator, the correlator can be variationally optimized entirely in classical post-processing with no quantum-classical feedback loop. We demonstrate our algorithm on 32 qubits of Quantinuum's H2-2 with a bond-dimension-4 MPS for the half-filled $4 \times 4$ lattice and achieve a relative ground-state energy error of $16 \pm 4\%$ after postselection, reduced to $3.5 \pm 0.5\%$ by calibration using low-order moments from the MPS. Compared with other feedback-free hybrid algorithms, even under generous assumptions, our method requires fewer samples than quantum-selected configuration interaction and fewer two-qubit gates than quantum Krylov methods.

Quantum Physics.title: Entanglement in the $θ$-vacuum
Quantum Physics.summary: We compute the entanglement entropy and the entanglement spectrum of the vacuum state in the massive Schwinger model at a finite $θ$ angle. By computing two-point correlation functions we show that the correlation length diverges in the critical region. We clarify the physical origin of entanglement entropy enhancement at $θ=π$ by relating it to the competition between distinct electric-flux vacuum branches. We show that the peak near $θ=π$ persists across the range of masses studied and corresponds to the point of maximal competition between distinct vacuum branches with opposite electric-field orientation, where quantum fluctuations due to fermion pair creation are maximized. While this entropy enhancement is generic, a pronounced compression of the low-lying entanglement spectrum at $θ=π$ distinguishes the near-critical case ($m/g\simeq0.33$). Using the Bisognano--Wichmann (BW) theorem, we construct a lattice BW entanglement Hamiltonian and compare it with the exact modular Hamiltonian obtained from the reduced density matrix.
