We first develop the spectral decomposition of the retarded Green function of the matched stellar interior--Schwarzschild exterior, which classifies four separate regimes in time domain: acausal region, prompt wave, surface-reflected wave, and mode+tail. The prompt signal is identical to that of a Schwarzschild black hole with the same mass, which is combined with the surface-reflected wave to be referred as the "direct part". With the Green function and a complex bilinear form on the full metric--fluid phase space, we decompose the linear response of a nonrotating perfect-fluid star into direct, quasinormal-mode, and late-time-tail sectors. Crucially, every sector admits an explicit first-order driven evolution equation: discrete bilinear projections determine the dynamically evolving quasinormal-mode amplitudes, while continuum projections of the same tidal source onto branch-cut states determine the direct and tail amplitudes. The result is a complete modal--nonmodal decomposition of the spacetime and fluid perturbations, which is physically described by the dynamics of a discrete and a continuous-frequency set of oscillators. We verify the decomposition numerically under generic time-dependent tidal driving and discuss applications to black hole perturbations.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 32pages, 9 figures with appendix. Comments are welcome

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Symmetries of cosmological perturbations: The residual low-multipole ambiguity
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: In cosmology, long-wavelength modes are related to large-gauge transformations (LGT), i.e. changes of coordinates that modify the physical geometry of the cosmological patch. These LGTs stand as bona-fide symmetries of cosmological perturbation theory with various applications, from consistency relations constraining cosmological correlators to non-linear conservation laws in the separate-universe approach. In this work, we revisit LGTs and derive two new results. First, we show that the global symmetries already identified in the literature can be extended to local infinite-dimensional symmetries. The associated generators depend on arbitrary functions of time, and generate low-multipole modes that modify the mean curvature energy and the angular momentum of the patch, demonstrating their physical nature. We propose to interpret these low-multipole soft modes as a new cosmological-frame ambiguity that needs to be fixed prior to evaluating cosmological observables. Second, we demonstrate that the adiabatic cosmological perturbations generated by LGTs deform but preserve all the explicit and hidden Killing symmetries of the background geometry. As such, long-wavelength modes stand as a concrete example of algebraically-special cosmological perturbations of Petrov-type O, and inherit the conformal group as isometries and a set of four deformed Killing-Yano tensors and their associated Killing tensors. This opens the possibility to study their effect on cosmological observables in a fully analytic manner.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 34 pages without appendices (45 pages in total), matches published version in JCAP

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Finite-size clocks in quantum field theory and the twin paradox
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Vacuum fluctuations in quantum field theory impose fundamental limitations on our ability to measure time at arbitrarily short scales. To investigate the impact of universal quantum field theory effects on observer-dependent time measurements, we introduce a clock model based on the vacuum decay probability of a finite-sized quantum system. This model defines an effective notion of proper time that depends on the microscopic properties of the clock and on how it samples vacuum fluctuations along its trajectory. We show that, in the long-time regime, this notion of time reduces to the usual proper time of special relativity. However, by studying a microscopic twin-paradox scenario, we find that, in general, time is not determined solely by the trajectory connecting two events, but also by how vacuum fluctuations interact with the internal structure of the clocks.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Enhancing dark siren cosmology via Gaussian process reconstruction of incomplete galaxy catalogs
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We present a novel framework for improving dark siren cosmology by applying a Gaussian process (GP) to the line-of-sight (LOS) reconstruction of incomplete galaxy catalogs. In the standard galaxy catalog method for inferring the Hubble constant $H_0$ from gravitational-wave (GW) dark sirens, missing galaxies are typically assumed to follow a uniform distribution in comoving volume, an assumption that discards galaxy redshift clustering information crucial for cosmological inference. We propose instead to model the LOS galaxy redshift distribution as a non-parametric function drawn from a GP realization, which is fitted to the observed incomplete catalog via a hierarchical Bayesian likelihood that explicitly accounts for the survey selection function. Applied to mock GW and galaxy catalogs extending up to redshift $z\leq0.4$, our method yields $H_0$ constraints that are on average 23% more precise than the standard homogeneous completion when using a 24%-complete galaxy catalog, and 37% more precise for an 8%-complete catalog. The largest improvement, reaching 66%, is obtained in configurations where the GP most effectively reconstructs the redshift over- and under-density features that the homogeneous completion fails to capture.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: On the Mathematical Foundations of Gravitational Decoupling in General Relativity
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We study the algebraic and geometric structures of gravitational decoupling within a fixed class of globally static, spherically symmetric spacetimes with non-vanishing areal-radius differential. We show that (minimal and extended) geometric deformations of the seed metric define a groupoid of partial transformations. We also draw a connection between the geometric deformation procedures and disformal transformations. It is shown that every admissible minimal geometric deformation admits a disformal representation using the areal radius as an auxiliary scalar. For extended deformations, we derive a necessary condition and exhibit a global obstruction that persists under diffeomorphisms preserving the areal radius and the static Killing direction up to constant normalization. Finally, we verify that the disformal construction reproduces the standard minimal geometric deformation source equations and separate conservation law, including anisotropic seeds.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 17 pages, no figures, comments are welcome

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Bilinear products and the orthogonality of quasinormal modes on hyperboloidal foliations
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We explore the properties of bilinear products for black-hole quasinormal modes (QNMs) formulated on hyperboloidal foliations. We find that, although QNM solutions are smooth and finite on future-directed hyperboloids, the integrand of the bilinear form with respect to which the modes are orthogonal is still divergent. This is a result of the reflection (equivalently, CPT) transformation required in the definition of the products, which modifies the behaviour of the integrand at the boundaries. We present several regularisation procedures that yield a finite and well-defined bilinear form. In addition, we examine an alternative definition of the bilinear products that incorporates flux contributions, discussing its advantages and limitations. Finally, we define the QNM excitation factors and coefficients within the hyperboloidal framework in terms of the bilinear products, and compute them explicitly for a choice of mode numbers and constant initial data. For concreteness, we work with the QNMs associated to scalar perturbations of the Schwarzschild family of spacetimes.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: Updated to reflect the published version

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Stable manifolds of heteroclinic chains in Hořava-Lifshitz cosmology
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We consider vacuum spatially homogeneous models in Hořava-Lifshitz gravity, which are expected to describe generic singularities for these modified gravity theories. These models perturb the well-known Bianchi models in general relativity (GR) by a parameter $v\in (0,1)$, in which GR occurs at $v=1/2$. We show that all periodic heteroclinic chains of Bianchi type II orbits are robust for small perturbations of GR, i.e. they exist for any $v\approx 1/2$. Moreover, we prove the existence of a stable manifold for each heteroclinic chain within a Cantor set for the supercritical case, $v\in (1/2,1)$. In particular, we discuss the heteroclinic chains of periods three and four in detail.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Dirac stars in modified $F(R)$ gravity
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We study Dirac mini-stars in modified $R^2$ gravity, where gravity is sourced by both linear and nonlinear spinor fields. Two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) profiles of the mini-star mass are constructed as functions of the spinor frequency (for the 2D profiles) and the central value of the spinor field (for the 3D profiles) in general relativity and modified gravity for various values of the spinor nonlinearity parameter. We show that the modification of gravity alters the properties of these configurations, while increasing the nonlinearity parameter within the framework of $R^2$ gravity significantly changes the profiles of the spinor and metric functions, the effective energy density, and the dependence of the total mass on the oscillation frequency. The most pronounced changes occur at large values of the nonlinearity parameter.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Adiabatic particle production in a time-dependent accelerated frame
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We study a massive scalar field in flat spacetime written in a time-dependent accelerated frame whose fixed-coordinate observers have maximal proper acceleration at $t=0$ and become asymptotically inertial without forming a horizon. The Klein-Gordon equation separates into a modified Mathieu equation in time and a confining Schrödinger problem in space with a discrete spectrum. We impose an adiabatic vacuum at the instant of maximal acceleration and compute the particle number in the inertial future. For the zeroth-order adiabatic state it falls as the inverse eighth power of the initial mode frequency, and raising the adiabatic order cancels successive terms of the endpoint expansion, in analogy with the switching transients of finite-time detectors. Analytic continuation of the spatial eigenfunctions gives the out modes in closed form and an exact expression for the particle number, which is entirely the mismatch at $t=0$ between the initial state and the out vacuum. The spectrum is algebraic rather than Planckian.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Quintic Modification to Lifshitz Quasi-topological Black Holes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We extend the analysis of Lifshitz black holes to quintic order in five-dimensional quasi-topological gravity coupled to a massive Abelian vector field. Starting from a static ansatz with a constant-curvature horizon, we derive the reduced field equations and identify the radially conserved quantity of the one-dimensional effective system. We then analyze the algebraic conditions that permit Lifshitz backgrounds, both in the absence and in the presence of the massive vector field. Since closed-form black-hole solutions are not available for the generic quintic theory, we construct numerical solutions by integrating the field equations outward from regular near-horizon data. We present solutions for the relativistic branch \(z=1\) and the Lifshitz branch \(z=2\), covering the three horizon topologies \(k=-1,0,+1\). The numerical profiles remain qualitatively consistent with those found previously in cubic and quartic quasi-topological Lifshitz gravity. A controlled planar comparison through the genuine quartic point \(\hatμ_5=0\) further shows that the very small quintic couplings used in the representative examples produce nearly quartic profiles, whereas larger admissible values of \(\hatμ_5\) lead to clearly resolved changes in both the normalized radial profiles and the Hawking temperature. We also compute the Wald entropy and Hawking temperature and examine the thermal behavior through dimensionless logarithmic temperature--entropy plots. For the representative branches considered here, the heat capacity is positive. For a fixed-theory planar \(z=2\) family, the conserved radial charge is further used to determine the energy density; the differential and integrated first laws are verified numerically to the precision of the computation, and the corresponding Helmholtz free-energy density is found to be negative relative to the Lifshitz vacuum normalization adopted here.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Spectrally enhanced gravitational redshift signals in photonic interferometry
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Quantum mechanics and general relativity are remarkably successful, yet their joint predictions remain beyond direct experimental reach. Photonic interferometers operating in a gravitational field offer a promising route to test this regime: gravitational redshift differentiates photon propagation between vertically separated arms, leading to a predicted phase shift and reduction in interference visibility. These effects are minute on laboratory scales, motivating existing proposals to consider large interferometer areas to accumulate them geometrically. Indeed, such schemes typically require kilometre-scale optical paths to produce appreciable interferometric signals. Here, we propose a strategy that replaces geometric accumulation with spectral enhancement by coupling the two interferometer arms to optical scatterers based on ultranarrow atomic transitions. These transitions serve as local spectral references: gravitational redshift changes the photon's detuning from each resonance, producing large differences in reflection amplitude and hence substantial visibility loss and interferometric phase shift already for centimetre-scale height differences. We quantify the experimental requirements and assess the feasibility of implementation with current or near-term technology. Our proposal thus opens a route to tabletop optical tests of the interplay between quantum mechanics and general relativity.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Looking for non-gaussianity in Pulsar Timing Arrays through the four point correlator
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Pulsar Timing Arrays have recently reported strong evidence for a stochastic gravitational wave background. In standard analyses, it is modeled through pulsar-dependent Fourier coefficients assumed to follow gaussian statistics, so that the signal is fully characterized by its two-point function. However, if the background arises from a finite population of inspiralling supermassive black hole binaries, non-gaussian features may emerge, making the determination of higher-order correlators essential. In this work, we compute the complete four-point correlator of the stochastic gravitational wave background Fourier coefficients for four arbitrary pulsar positions, identifying it as the leading probe of non-gaussianity. The result separates into a gaussian contribution, proportional to the square of the two-point function, and a genuinely non-gaussian connected component, whose non-trivial angular dependence generalizes the Hellings and Downs correlation to four pulsars. This angular structure depends only on averages of products of antenna pattern functions, and is therefore expected to be independent of the specific physical origin of the background. We further propose to incorporate the four-point correlator into the parameter-estimation pipeline by deriving a marginalized likelihood that perturbatively accounts for non-gaussian effects. Our results provide the theoretical framework to search for non-gaussian features in pulsar timing array data, opening the way to a more complete characterization of gravitational-wave backgrounds.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Kantowski Sachs Cosmological Model with Radiation and Generalized Chaplygin Gas
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: In the present paper we study the evolution of a homogeneous and anisotropic Kantowski Sachs cosmological model coupled with radiation and a generalized Chaplygin gas. Our main objective is verifying if this model evolves to a homogeneous and isotropic Friedmann Robertson Walker cosmological model, which is the more accepted model to describe our present Universe. If this is the case, we may imagine that the Kantowski Sachs cosmological model could had been an early stage of our Universe.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: The paper has 26 pages and 14 figures

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Black hole binaries in shift-symmetric Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: In shift-symmetric Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity, stationary black holes have a non-vanishing scalar charge. During the inspiral, the phase evolution is modified by several effects,primarily an additional scalar dipole radiation, which enters at -1PN order. Including corrections up to 2PN, this effect accelerates the inspiral when compared to general relativity, but changes in the conservative dynamics may do the opposite. Using fully non-linear numerical simulations of quasi-circular, comparable mass binaries, we characterize the late stages of the orbital dynamics. We find that the overall effect is still an accelerated merger phase for the modified gravity case, but noticeably less than predicted by PN alone, which we relate to the conservative dynamics, showing that at the late inspiral stage more energy must be emitted in scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity to induce a given change in frequency. In longer signals, this may lead to a distinctive frequency evolution relative to general relativity as the binary approaches merger, but its effect close to merger is to suppress the difference with GR. This work suggests we may need to revisit existing constraints on the theory that are obtained assuming PN approximations apply up to merger, or based on order by order approximations that neglect backreaction effects on the metric, and shows the importance of including non-linear effects that modify the gravitational sector in the strong field regime.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 14 pages, 9 figures, version accepted by PRD

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Pseudo-spectral methods in gravitational lensing: Spin precession in loop quantum black hole spacetimes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Gravitational lensing is usually treated as an initial value problem: for a given impact parameter of an unbound orbit, one computes the resulting deflection angle. In this paper we advocate the inverse point of view. For a prescribed deflection angle, the orbit is selected by two boundary conditions at spatial infinity, so that the lensing problem becomes a well-defined two-point boundary value problem, with the impact parameter playing the role of a nonlinear eigenvalue. We show that pseudo-spectral methods based on Chebyshev collocation solve this boundary value problem accurately at modest computational cost, and that the parallel transport equations governing the spin precession of the particle reduce to a single linear system on the same grid. As a concrete application, we compute the spin precession of massive particles in backward scattering off two black hole spacetimes from loop quantum gravity: the covariant effective metric and the self-dual loop quantum black hole. All equations are written for a general static, spherically symmetric line element with three free functions, so that both spacetimes are handled on the same footing. We find that the quantum corrections are most pronounced for slowly moving particles, while in the ultra-relativistic limit the universal spin flip is always recovered. The flip itself is universal, but the rate at which it is approached is not: the derivative of $\cosξ$ with respect to the particle speed at $v=1$ is a strong-field quantity in every backward channel and depends clearly on the quantum parameters of both spacetimes. The framework is not restricted to the models studied
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 24 pages, 5 figures in main texts, 1 illustration figure in appendix; comments welcome

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Sound Wave in the Backreaction Affected Spacetime in Analogue Gravity Based on Number-Conserving Approach
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Adopting a number-conserving approach, we show that the sound wave in the backreaction-affected dynamical spacetime obeys the equations of motion for a massive scalar field in an analogue spacetime. Even with backreaction, the analogue metric has the same form as that without backreaction, except that the sound velocity, fluid density, and fluid velocity incorporate small corrections that account for backreaction. Moreover, the modification of the classical fluid-dynamical equations by backreaction introduces a spacetime-dependent mass. We also present a linear form of the modified Bogoliubov-de Gennes equation with number conservation, which allows us to solve it numerically. Using a finite-size homogeneous quasi-one-dimensional Bose gas as an example, we find that backreaction enhances the canonically normal-ordered correlation function at the same point, by about $10\%$ in the bulk and up to about $20\%$ near the edges. The bulk enhancement persists when the finite imaging resolution of cold-atom experiments is taken into account.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Quasiperiodic oscillations as probes of rotating black holes in exponential dark matter environments
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We construct the rotating counterpart of a black hole embedded in a dark-matter halo with the exponential-sphere profile $ρ=ρ_0e^{-r/r_0}$, using the Newman--Janis algorithm in the Azreg-Aïnou form, and study its imprints on test-particle motion and quasiperiodic oscillations (QPOs). We derive closed-form orbital and epicyclic frequencies valid for any Kerr-like metric with a mass function and show that, to first order, the halo enters them only through its central density, acting as an effective cosmological constant $Λ_{eff}=8πρ_0$; the corrections are therefore universal for all cored profiles. The halo moves the innermost stable circular orbit outward and produces an outer boundary of stable orbits, while the sign of the frequency shift depends on the assumed equation of state of the halo. Fitting the relativistic precession model to the simultaneous QPO triplets of GRO~J1655$-$40 and XTE~J1859+226 with Markov-chain Monte Carlo sampling yields spins and emission radii consistent with Kerr and $ρ_0M^2<2.9\times10^{-5}$ and $3.0\times10^{-5}$ (95\%), respectively. In physical units these limits exclude only ultra-dense dark cores, $ρ_0\gtrsim10^{11}$~g\,cm$^{-3}$.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Gravitational Properties of the Monopole Bag
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Axionic cosmologies constitute a class of models with phenomenologically rich symmetry breaking in the early universe. In the case where monopoles are present in such a background, the axion profile may be deformed; it is possible to construct a ``monopole bag" state composed of a central monopole within a closed axion domain wall. We consider the gravitational properties of this composite defect, and propose that there exist both a horizonless and a black hole-like static solution for different input parameters. For the latter case, we present our results as a first step towards a new construction of a dyonic regular black hole, given the monopole bag's potential ability to evade the usual singular gravitational collapse and retain a non-trivial axionic profile by the exotic electromagnetic properties of an axionic Chern-Simons term.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 47 pages, 8 figures (version accepted by JHEP, some discussions added, no change to figures)

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Color-Kinematics Duality and the Double Copy in Curved Spacetimes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The double copy relates gravitational data to gauge-theory data, most sharply through color-kinematics duality for flat-space scattering amplitudes. This review surveys the extent to which this idea can be formulated beyond asymptotically flat backgrounds. After recalling the flat-space ingredients needed for comparison, we describe curved-space constructions for boundary correlators and scattering observables in AdS, dS, and other non-trivial backgrounds. We then review classical and field-level maps, including Kerr--Schild, Weyl, Cotton, twistor, and convolutional double copies. A separate part is devoted to self-dual sectors. Throughout, we emphasize both the common structures that survive from flat space and the obstructions introduced by curvature.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 191 pages plus appendices and references, invited review article for Physics Reports; v2 fixed typos, updated references, and improved some discussions; v3 updated references

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Testing Van der Waals black holes using black hole photon rings
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The Van der Waals black hole (BH) is a non-Kerr model in Anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetime that exhibits characteristic thermodynamic phase transitions. Whether the physical validity of parameters such as the BH molecular volume $b$ and pressure $P$ is feasible still requires observational verification. As a sensitive probe of strong gravitational fields, the BH photon ring directly carries spacetime geometric information, making it an ideal object for model testing. In accordance with the spacetime metric associated with this BH, this study obtains the null geodesic equations for photons and conserved quantities, determines the photon sphere conditions and radii via effective potential analysis, investigates the photon ring classification and radiative properties, and employs measurements from the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) to place constraints on parameters and simulate the optical appearance. The results show that the molecular volume parameter $b$ significantly regulates the radius of the photon sphere radius, photon ring structure, and the luminosity. Within a specific interval, the model exhibits a high degree of agreement with the EHT measurements for M87* and Sgr A*. This interval not only satisfies the energy conditions (weak, strong, and dominant) but also corresponds to a stable Van der Waals-type phase transition region. Furthermore, the photon ring can distinguish between the Van der Waals BH and the Schwarzschild BH: due to the small-black-hole-large-black-hole (SBH-LBH) phase transition and microstructural discontinuities, the photon ring of the Van der Waals BH is particularly sensitive to the parameter $b$, whereas the Schwarzschild BH lacks these features. This work uses the photon ring to probe BH molecular models, linking its microstructure, spacetime geometry and observational signatures, and provides a new way to derive BH microphysics from observations.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: v2: Corrected 13 numerical values in Table 1. Conclusions unchanged

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Exact Holographic Kinematics in AdS/CFT
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We propose that holography contains an exact kinematic sector distinct from holographic dynamics. The appropriate setting for this sector is a CFT on an open solid torus in the Weyl frame. The open solid torus introduces an intrinsic scale, and the Weyl frame makes this scale manifest as an extra bulk direction. The resulting bulk-boundary pairs are exact and finite: no cutoff, large-$N$ limit, strong-coupling assumption, or heavy-operator approximation is required. The AdS geometry appearing in this sector should be understood as a kinematic geometry; only in special CFTs and appropriate limits is it promoted to a dynamical semiclassical bulk. The standard boundary-anchored dictionary entries are recovered only as singular limits. As a striking demonstration, we show that Weyl-frame two-point functions provide a replica-free definition of entanglement entropy.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: V2: added some clarifications. 5 pages, 3 figures

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Scalar-induced gravitational waves from a box-shaped curvature power spectrum
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We compute the stochastic background of gravitational waves (GWs) produced at second order in cosmological perturbation theory by a primordial curvature power spectrum that is flat in $\ln k$ over a finite band $[k_-,k_+]=[k_*e^{-Δ},k_*e^{+Δ}]$ and vanishes elsewhere. This logarithmic box interpolates between a monochromatic spectrum as $Δ\to0$ and a locally scale-invariant plateau as $Δ\to\infty$, and its sharp boundaries make the geometry of the source convolution unusually transparent. Working in the radiation era, we reduce the convolution to a compact integral over the overlap between the momentum triangle and the box, and evaluate it analytically in two regimes. For a narrow box we show that, to leading order in the width, the spectrum equals the Dirac-spectrum result multiplied by a purely geometric overlap factor $Φ_{\rm box}(κ,Δ)$; this factor turns the infrared slope from $k^{3}\ln^{2}k$ into $k^{2}\ln^{2}k$ at a break $k_b=2k_*\sinhΔ$. For a broad box we separate the lower edge, the scale-invariant interior, and the upper edge, derive the leading behaviour in each (an infrared $k^{3}\ln^{2}k$ rise, a scale-invariant plateau, and a quartic cut-off at the hard endpoint $k=2k_+$), and combine them into a single uniform formula cast as a product of two universal, $Δ$-independent edge functions. We also provide an integral-free closed-form surrogate for these edge functions for use in parameter scans.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Classical and quantum scattering of massive Klein--Gordon fields in asymptotically flat spacetimes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We use microlocal tools to define distinguished incoming and outgoing vacuum states of the quantum theory of massive Klein--Gordon fields in non-trapping asymptotically flat spacetimes, including radiative perturbations of Minkowski space. The asymptotic vacuum states satisfy the Hadamard condition, and the incoming and outgoing particle representations are unitarily equivalent, or in other words the quantum S-matrix is well-defined. These results are based on a description of scattering of classical fields which keeps track of the asymptotic distinction between positive- and negative-frequency solutions of the Klein--Gordon equation. Our emphasis is on developing the theory without recourse to explicit asymptotics for classical waves.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: The Promise of Gravitational-Wave Astronomy
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We review the promise of upcoming gravitational-wave (GW) observations in addressing some of the important open questions in astrophysics and cosmology. A decade after the first direct detection of GWs, the field is entering a transformative phase driven by progressive detector upgrades and the anticipated advent of space-based and next-generation ground-based observatories. These instruments will not only push the distance horizon of GW observations to cosmological redshifts, but will dramatically extend the accessible frequency band, opening entirely new source classes that lie beyond the reach of current detectors. The source landscape is rich enough that surprises are likely. This review surveys our current understanding across this landscape and offers some perspective on the discoveries that upcoming GW observations are poised to deliver.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: Invited review for the Focus Point on Surprises from Major New Telescopes (https://link.springer.com/collections/bdijcibaac)

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Exact radial stability threshold for a Minkowski-Schwarzschild thin shell
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We study the stability of a thin shell of ordinary matter that separates a flat interior from a Schwarzschild exterior, which is the simplest model of a subluminal warp drive. The matter content of the shell is fixed by the junction conditions and satisfies all the standard energy conditions except very close to the horizon. For a shell made of causal matter we find an exact radius below which it cannot be stable under radial perturbations. We then place a black hole inside the shell and show that this radius grows with the black hole mass, so that the flat interior is the most favourable case. Since such shells are known to be unstable to non-radial perturbations, our result marks the boundary of the region in which any stabilising mechanism would have to operate.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 6 pages, 3 figures, 1 table. Submitted to Physics Letters B

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Black holes with dark matter halos and a positive cosmological constant: Energy conditions and signatures
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We study static, spherically symmetric black holes surrounded by dark matter halos in the presence of a positive cosmological constant. Assuming vanishing radial pressure, we derive the constraints imposed by the null, weak, strong, and dominant energy conditions on the halo matter. The halo is confined to a finite radial interval separated from both horizons, and the total mass is bounded above by the Nariai value. We construct a Hernquist-type profile and study black hole images, showing that a positive cosmological constant can substantially change the images. We also compute scalar quasinormal modes of the Hernquist-type spacetime. When the dark matter mass is sufficiently small, the relative difference of a selected mode is approximately linear in the compactness of the matter halo, i.e., the ratio of mass parameter $M_{\text{DM}}$ and scale parameter $a$, with a coefficient that depends on the cosmological constant.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Nonoscillatory gravitational quasinormal modes of Reissner-Nordström-de Sitter spacetime
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We revisit quasinormal modes of Reissner-Nordström-de Sitter black holes, a classical and seemingly well-understood solution of Einstein-Maxwell theory with a positive cosmological constant. While previous studies have focused almost exclusively on the oscillatory photon-sphere branch, we show that two additional branches of nonoscillatory, purely imaginary modes - associated with the de Sitter horizon and with the regime of near-extremal charge (zero-damped) - are essential for a complete description of the spectrum. These modes have so far remained largely unexplored for gravitational perturbations despite their relevance for late-time dynamics and stability. In particular, we derive accurate analytic expressions for the purely imaginary quasinormal frequencies in the slow-damping regime, providing a complete description of this sector of the spectrum.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: All toric Hermitian ALE gravitational instantons
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We prove that the only smooth, Ricci flat, ALE gravitational instanton with a toric Hermitian non-Kähler structure is the Eguchi-Hanson instanton. The proof is analogous to the classification of toric Hermitian ALF instantons by Biquard and Gauduchon, although we avoid the use of toric Kähler geometry and instead perform a direct global analysis of the Tod form of the metric in Weyl-Papapetrou coordinates. This supports a conjecture by Gibbons and Bando-Kasue-Nakajima which states that any Ricci flat ALE instanton is self-dual.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Classical soft theorems meet the post-Newtonian expansion
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Classical soft theorems govern the non-analytic structure of electromagnetic and gravitational radiation in the low-frequency regime, with the gravitational memory effect providing the canonical realization of the classical soft graviton theorem. While the soft behavior of radiation from hyperbolic scattering is well understood, its realization in gravitationally bound systems remains less explored. In this work, we study the soft structure of gravitational waveforms generated by compact binaries, focusing on the scattering of emitted radiation off the static background curvature within the multipolar post-Newtonian framework. We isolate the infrared (IR) logarithms associated with hereditary effects, including the tail-of-memory, and their higher generalizations with n-tail insertions. The resulting amplitudes exhibit a Laurent expansion in frequency space consistent with the Sahoo-Sen logarithmic soft theorems, thereby establishing a direct correspondence between gravitational memory effects, their higher-order tail corrections, and the soft expansion. We also comment on ultraviolet (UV) logarithms arising from short-distance sensitivity of the multipole expansion and their associated renormalization-group running.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: v2: 52 pages, 4 figures; typos corrected, references updated

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Gravity from generalized entropy
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Gravity from entropy (GfE) identifies its Lagrangian with the geometric quantum relative entropy (GQRE) between the spacetime metric and a metric induced by matter and curvature, treating the metric itself as a quantum operator. We extend this construction to the Tsallis, Rényi, and Sharma-Mittal families, which we call gravity from generalized entropy (GfGE), and determine their common Einstein limit, weak-field spectra, auxiliary-field formulation, and horizon entropy. The entropy choice controls the leading higher-curvature terms and additional modes. We confirm that the linearized GfE spectrum contains a healthy scalar and a Planck-scale tachyonic spin-2 ghost. We identify the conditions that remove this ghost: curvature must enter through its scalar trace, or the entropy generator must be flat to quadratic order at the identity. The latter gives exact general relativity for Tsallis at $q=0$ and ghost-free $f(R,L_m)$ theories for Rényi and Sharma-Mittal. On shell, the auxiliary G-field is proportional to the tensor in Wald's entropy formula. For analytic entropy functions, horizons with a single curvature scale have an area term followed by constant and inverse-area corrections. We also extend the volume-constraint cosmological constant to the full family; its leading entropy dependence is set by the scalar mass. A finite set of entropy-function derivatives controls the leading weak-curvature departures from general relativity.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Differential Invariants of Carrollian Spacetimes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We compute invariants of Carrollian spacetimes, deriving them from the geometry of the screen bundle. For generic Carrollian structures we specify how to generate the entire algebra of differential invariants, with emphasis on dimension 3, which has special physical relevance. Then, in the framework of jet-spaces, we compute the numerology behind these invariants: the Hilbert and Poincaré functions that govern their numbers according to order. Finally, we compute the Spencer cohomology behind the Carrollian geometry that, in particular, contains the spaces of intrinsic torsion and intrinsic curvature, which are fundamental invariants, important in the equivalence problem and symmetry analysis. Thus, we also discuss symmetry sizes of Carrollian spacetimes.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 24 pages. Minor improvements and typos corrected

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: The WDM time-frequency transform in gravitational-wave data analysis II: Evolutionary spectrum and noise covariance
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Noise cannot be treated as stationary over the timescales required for upcoming gravitational-wave detectors, minutes for ground-based and months for space-based detectors. Nonstationarity leads to a non-diagonal frequency-domain noise covariance matrix, thus motivating a shift to the time-frequency domain. We introduce \emph{evolutionary power spectra} for describing nonstationary noise in the Wilson-Daubechies-Meyer time-frequency basis. Under the framework of oscillatory processes, we show that, to leading order in the ratio of the Meyer filter and the nonstationarity timescales, the evolutionary spectrum is a power-frequency distribution that can be estimated from a single noise realization. We derive the corresponding noise covariance matrix and show that it is band tri-diagonal, like its stationary counterpart. The exact covariance to all orders is positive semi-definite by construction and dense depending on the noise. We further derive the optimal tiling of the time-frequency plane that minimizes the error of a diagonal covariance approximation and show that coarse-graining the plane suppresses correlations quadratically. Using simulated data with a LISA Galactic foreground and a drifting powerlaw spectrum, we show that the stationarity approximation leads to signal-to-noise ratio loss and severely biases inference. For realistic LISA data, approximating the covariance as diagonal in the Wilson-Daubechies-Meyer domain is accurate for the narrow-band analysis of a single resolved Galactic binary, but insufficient for a broad-band analysis. Finally, we provide mitigation strategies for the wraparound correlations induced across the data time edges whenever the spectrum differs between the start and the end of the data.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: The Forgetful Black Hole: Memory Burden and Hysteresis in Hawking Evaporation
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The memory-burden scenario of black hole evaporation proposes that Hawking emission may become increasingly suppressed as maintaining stored quantum information becomes dynamically costly. In this work, we revisit this scenario and investigate the conditions under which information retention can produce a genuine dynamical burden. We derive general scaling conditions for incremental memory accumulation at a fixed fractional mass loss and establish a conditional no-go result: entropy-suppressed, zero-mean deposits with subextensive integrated correlations cannot produce an order-one luminosity modification through unamplified accumulation and bounded feedback. We identify three essential requirements for dynamical memory: a record of the past must be written, retained, and coupled back to subsequent evaporation. We illustrate these requirements with concrete toy models that exhibit either a prolonged but finite black hole lifetime or an asymptotically approached finite-mass state (an effective remnant). We further distinguish kinetic-memory, thermodynamic-memory, and spectral-memory sub-categories of possible memory-burden mechanisms. In particular, we demonstrate that an independently evolving memory variable can generate evaporation-accretion hysteresis, such that a black hole returning to the same mass may possess a different retained memory and consequently a different luminosity. This history dependence may have implications for primordial black hole phenomenology. Finally, we briefly discuss the possibility of "merger rejuvenation", in which black hole mergers reorganize or reset the effective memory state.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Black Hole Fine Structure
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: In General Relativity, axial and polar black-hole perturbations share identical quasinormal-mode spectra, a property known as isospectrality. New physics can break this degeneracy, producing a spectral splitting analogous to atomic fine structure. We perform a theory-agnostic search for such splitting in gravitational-wave observations. We find no evidence for isospectrality breaking and place a combined $90\%$ upper limit of $<28.5\%$ on the relative frequency splitting. We map these constraints onto several modified-gravity theories, constraining the coupling-lengths to be $\lesssim 28\,\mathrm{km}$.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Scalar-Assisted Growth of Supermassive Black Holes: Boson-Mass Windows and Observational Constraints
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We study a phenomenological cosmological model of black-hole growth in which a finite baryonic reservoir and a bosonic scalar cloud feed the black hole simultaneously. The baryonic component accretes through an Eddington-like channel, while the scalar cloud transfers mass through an effective quasibound-state decay rate. Evolving the system directly in redshift within a flat $Λ$CDM background, we scan over $μ$, $M_0$, $M_{c,0}$, and $M_{b,0}$ to assess whether scalar-assisted accretion can accelerate the formation of $10^9M_\odot$ supermassive black holes. We find that the scalar contribution is highly selective in parameter space. For the mass scales explored here, scalar transfer is most efficient for $μ\sim10^{-19}-10^{-16} \mathrm{eV}$, producing rapid cloud depletion and significantly earlier black-hole growth, while outside this interval the evolution remains mainly baryonic. More generally, this efficient window reflects a preferred range of the dimensionless coupling $α=μM_{\rm BH}$ and therefore shifts approximately as $μ\propto M_{\rm BH}^{-1}$. Comparison with observed quasar masses and luminosities instead favors lower boson masses, broadly around $μ\sim10^{-21}-10^{-20}\mathrm{eV}$. These results are not necessarily in tension, since the boson mass that maximizes early growth depends on the characteristic black-hole mass and evolutionary stage. This separation between dynamical efficiency and observational compatibility leaves open complementary roles for different bosonic mass scales in supermassive black hole growth and dark-matter phenomenology.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Strong-Field Gravitational-Wave Lensing from Ray-Traced Arrival-Time Surfaces
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The diffraction integral formalism has been greatly successful in describing gravitational wave lensing effects in scenarios where the wavelength of the signal is comparable to the characteristic length scale of the lens, known as the wave optics regime. However, the assumptions required to construct its integrand break down as the source approaches the strong gravity region of a black hole lens. In particular, we are interested in the lensed signal from a binary (the source) near a massive black hole (the lens). We present a new formalism for obtaining low frequency corrections to sources being lensed in the strong field regime of gravity by leveraging the fact that null geodesics obey the Hamilton--Jacobi equations. In doing so, we are able to construct a time delay surface without relying on the thin lens approximation, and solve the diffraction integral for the resulting surface directly. For a stationary source at $10M$, deep in the strong field regime, when comparing the results with a relativistic wave scattering model, we find $6.5\%$ and $0.3\%$ agreement in the peak amplification and first diffractive fringe, respectively. Furthermore, we find a $< 1\%$ agreement with the amplitude of the point mass lens with a source at $10^4 M$ in the weak field, but noticeable dephasing between the peaks of the amplification function at higher frequencies. This work allows for clean interpolation between otherwise separate regimes, valid for sources from $\sim 6M \to \infty$. It provides a transparent, physically motivated framework for computing beyond-geometric optics lensing effects in the strong field regime.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 14 pages, 4 figures, 0 hats. Comments are welcome

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Thin shells in Lovelock and Quasi-topological gravities
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We derive the junction conditions for spherically symmetric thin shells in Lovelock and Quasi-topological gravities along two independent routes: from the distributional form of the field equations, and from the boundary term that makes the variational problem well-posed in the non-null case. The former method is ambiguous as it stands, since the equations contain products of Heaviside step functions with a Dirac delta. We show that the singular parts of the field equations are exact differentials in the jumping variables, so that the Vol'pert chain rule for functions of bounded variation fixes these singular combinations uniquely and no products of two deltas survive for a single shell, finding that both routes then agree. The same rule yields the null junction conditions, for which no boundary term is available in Quasi-topological gravities, together with the mass conservation law of the shell. These results clarify recent questions concerning the existence of thin shells in these theories. In particular, we show that previous claims that the junction conditions force the shell mass to vary with radius are incorrect and arise from treating a trapezoidal approximation to the relevant distributional products as exact. Our results also provide a basis for the recent analyses of mass inflation in these theories.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Spinformation: do gravitational-wave events carry information beyond effective spins?
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: While the spin vectors of binary black holes offer insight into the astrophysical formation channels of these systems, individual spins are less precisely measured through gravitational-wave observations than the effective inspiral spin $χ_\mathrm{eff}$ and the effective precession spin $χ_\mathrm{p}$. Reducing to effective parameters discards information in the data, but how much information is lost has yet to be demonstrated. Here we show how to quantify whether individual mergers carry information about component spins beyond the constraints implied by effective parameters (a.k.a. spinformation) and apply the technique to GWTC-5. Thresholding on information loss $\gtrsim 0.25$ bits, over $80\%$ of gravitational-wave events in GWTC-5 have component spin posteriors described by $χ_\mathrm{eff}$ alone. Only $\sim3\%$ of gravitational-wave events have substantial spin information not explained by $χ_\mathrm{eff}$ and $χ_\mathrm{p}$. The catalog's component spin information is effectively two-dimensional in $χ_\mathrm{eff}$ and $χ_\mathrm{p}$. Using simulated signals, we find the noise realization can create or destroy over a bit of beyond-$χ_\mathrm{eff}$ information: the structure in real data may therefore be driven by noise. At current sensitivity, component spins provide interpretive\textemdash rather than informational\textemdash advantage over effective parameters.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Identity Crisis: Untangling Mass-Ordering Artifacts from Compact-Object Pairing in Gravitational-Wave Populations
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Mass distributions of binary black hole mergers inferred from gravitational-wave observations offer clues to how binaries form. These distributions conventionally label the heavier component as the primary, with mass $m_1$, and the lighter as the secondary, with mass $m_2$, such that $m_1 \geq m_2$. This ordering folds the physically labeled mass distribution along the equal-mass line, potentially reshaping the underlying population structure. In this Letter, we determine which population features can arise from mass ordering and which require genuine astrophysical structure. We show that ordering alone can produce (1) an $m_2$ distribution that declines more rapidly than the $m_1$ distribution, without intrinsic differences between the physically labeled components, and (2) an apparent concentration along equal masses, without correlations that preferentially pair black holes of equal mass. Moreover, different physically labeled populations can produce the same ordered mass distribution. Crucially, however, a preferred companion mass that remains constant as $m_1$ increases requires a characteristic mass scale already present in the physically labeled population. Applied to binary black hole mergers in the fifth Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog, our model recovers such a scale near $m_2 \simeq 50\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$. Around this scale, the merger-rate density declines much more rapidly toward higher $m_2$ than toward lower $m_2$, ruling out an equal or weaker high-$m_2$ decline at 99.45% credibility. This structure therefore requires a characteristic mass scale in at least one physically labeled component, but masses alone cannot determine which component carries it. Any formation model reproducing the observed high-mass binary black hole merger population must contain such a scale.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: Codes are publicly availdable on GitHub: https://github.com/SoumendraRoy/Mass_Ordering

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Strong Field Gravitational Lensing in Full Wave Optics
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Compact binaries evolving in the vicinity of massive black holes may be commonplace in the Universe, and their gravitational waves carry signatures of their environment. We study the strong lensing of these signals by the massive companion, a configuration that violates the standard assumptions of the lensing literature: geometric optics and thin lenses. Using a perturbative framework, we compute the full wave optics amplification factors for face-on and edge-on binaries, including spinning lenses. In the edge-on configuration, peak amplification does not occur at perfect source--lens--observer alignment, even for a non-spinning lens. This is a consequence of the anisotropic, coherent quadrupolar emission of the stellar-mass binary breaking the axisymmetry of the system. Restricting to the equatorial plane near the optical axis, we then find that the frequency dependence of the amplification factor is universal across every configuration studied, persisting deep into the wave optics regime. Comparing against a strong-field ray tracing calculation, we find agreement at the $\sim10\%$ level for a face-on binary lensed by a Schwarzschild black hole. In the less symmetric edge-on case only the angular peak shift and fringe spacing is reproduced to this accuracy. For a Kerr lens, the face-on amplification factor is described by its Schwarzschild counterpart to the same $\sim 10 \%$ accuracy once the effect of frame dragging is corrected for. A point mass lens, by contrast, fails to reproduce the features of the system, which may have strong implications for forecasts that adopt it for lensing by massive black holes in the strong field.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: EMRIs in Kerr Spacetime: The Role of Inclination Diffusion
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Extreme mass ratio inspirals (EMRIs) are expected to be a major source of gravitational waves (GWs) for the future {\it Laser Interferometer Space Antenna} ({\it LISA}). An EMRI occurs when a compact object, driven by the emission of gravitational radiation, slowly inspirals into a massive black hole (MBH). The classical formation channel involves repeated two-body interactions within dense nuclear star clusters. However, both EMRI event rates and the expected distribution of their orbital parameters remain highly uncertain. A major source of this uncertainty is the poorly constrained ratio between gradually inspiraling EMRIs and direct plunges, which do not produce detectable GWs. While most studies of astrophysical EMRI production focus on the Schwarzschild limit, previous work examining the Kerr metric found that the spin of the central MBH can significantly affect the EMRI-to-plunge ratio. This enhancement depends sensitively on orbital inclination, yet earlier studies held inclination fixed. In this work, we develop the mathematical framework describing inclination evolution driven by two-body encounters evolving along Kerr geodesics. By implementing 3D diffusion into Monte Carlo simulations, we show that initially prograde orbits may evolve into retrograde states, thereby converting potential EMRIs into plunges or vice versa. We estimate the EMRI-to-plunge ratio and find that substantial MBH spin enhances the EMRI rate by a factor of $\sim 2.5$. Additionally, even for a non-spinning MBH, modeling the orbits as relativistic geodesics rather than Newtonian trajectories increases the number of EMRIs by a similar factor of $\sim 2.5$. The distribution of Kerr EMRI inclinations has a substantial prograde bias that may aid in identifying the subset of loss cone EMRIs within large future EMRI samples.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 21 pages, 14 figures, 1 table. Comments are welcome

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Nonlinear Perturbations of Relativistic Stars
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We extend the general relativistic Lagrangian perturbation formalism of Friedman and Schutz [Astrophys. J. 200, 204 (1975)] beyond linear order, retaining full time dependence of the perturbations. We provide general formulae to relate the Lagrangian and Eulerian perturbations to any general perturbative order. As a proof of principle, we apply the framework to tidally perturbed relativistic stars in Regge-Wheeler gauge and reduce the second-order field and conservation equations to master equations with a nonlinear source. Projecting the source onto the star's eigenmodes, we obtain a nonlinear equation of motion for the mode amplitudes and the coupling coefficients, which describe the interactions among the eigenmodes and with the external tidal field. Approximating the tidal field and the coupling coefficients, we compute the static quadratic Love number from the quadrupolar fundamental mode alone and find that it reproduces the direct metric-matching value to a reasonable accuracy of $4\%$, up to a further correction arising from the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints of the second-order tidal field.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Separation of gravitational perturbations of singly spinning Myers-Perry black holes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Gravitational perturbations of rotating black holes in higher dimensions generally obey coupled partial differential equations. We show that scalar gravitational perturbations invariant under rotations of the transverse sphere of a singly spinning Myers-Perry black hole separate, despite the obstruction to a decoupled Teukolsky equation. Two commuting, second-order angular operators organise the three gauge-invariant curvature components into joint eigenfunctions. The physical radial problem is a $2\times2$ first-order system, equivalent to a single second-order equation. This gives a separation of the sector containing both the bar-mode and axisymmetric ultraspinning instabilities. Using only ordinary differential equations, we compute the bar-mode quasinormal spectrum in $d=5,6,7$ and find instability onsets at $a/r_+=0.90498$ and $0.83228$ in $d=6,7$. We also compute the growing axisymmetric modes and their onset rotations in $d=6,\ldots,9$. The construction shows how separability can survive the coupling between gravitational polarisations.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 5 pages, 2 figures, plus 12 pages of Supplemental Material

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Data Free Training of Diffusion Models for Lattice Field Theories
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: Sampling equilibrium field configurations remains a major computational bottleneck in lattice field theory, motivating the development of generative samplers that can produce independent configurations. Diffusion models are promising for this purpose, but their standard denoising score matching objective requires samples from the target distribution, seemingly reintroducing the original sampling problem. Here, we show that diffusion models can instead be trained from their own generated samples using the target score identity, provided access to the unnormalized probability density. Importance-weighted formulations of this identity yield a consistent target throughout training, while unweighted variants define a self-consistent fixed-point training scheme. We benchmark the different approaches in two-dimensional \(φ^4\) theory and identify effective choices that enable efficient training and sampling across the symmetric, critical, and broken phases. Ultimately, our data-free training approach achieves comparable performance to training on HMC reference data.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Emergent Loop Geometry in Gauge-Equivariant Graph Neural Networks
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: Gauge-equivariant graph neural networks generate ordered products of gauge links through local message passing, but the geometry of these internal structures is not captured by the receptive field alone. We investigate the statistical ensemble of closed lattice walks generated by recursive node- and edge-feature operations, independently of network training. Analytical and numerical results reveal a separation between rapid growth of contour length and much slower spatial expansion: deeper compositions generate increasingly long paths through repeated traversal of relatively compact regions. Loop expansions of fermionic observables provide a physical interpretation of this hierarchy, showing how spatial locality remains compatible with high-order dependence on nearby gauge fields. These findings identify complementary roles of network depth in extending spatial reach and enriching the representations constructed within that reach, providing a geometrical perspective on learning lattice gauge observables.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Entanglement in the $θ$-vacuum
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We compute the entanglement entropy and the entanglement spectrum of the vacuum state in the massive Schwinger model at a finite $θ$ angle. By computing two-point correlation functions we show that the correlation length diverges in the critical region. We clarify the physical origin of entanglement entropy enhancement at $θ=π$ by relating it to the competition between distinct electric-flux vacuum branches. We show that the peak near $θ=π$ persists across the range of masses studied and corresponds to the point of maximal competition between distinct vacuum branches with opposite electric-field orientation, where quantum fluctuations due to fermion pair creation are maximized. While this entropy enhancement is generic, a pronounced compression of the low-lying entanglement spectrum at $θ=π$ distinguishes the near-critical case ($m/g\simeq0.33$). Using the Bisognano--Wichmann (BW) theorem, we construct a lattice BW entanglement Hamiltonian and compare it with the exact modular Hamiltonian obtained from the reduced density matrix. We observe agreement in the infrared sector, indicating that the entanglement Hamiltonian is well approximated by a spatially weighted Hamiltonian. Finally, we discuss possible applications to entanglement in topological insulators and quantum wires. In this work, we used the chirally rotated formulation of the Schwinger model Hamiltonian. We identify an additive vacuum-energy artifact induced by the discretization of the chirally rotated lattice and derive its exact free-lattice form to subtract it in the continuum limit.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Neutral Pseudoscalar Mesons, Hadron Light-by-Light Scattering, and the Muon Anomalous Magnetic Moment
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: Continuum Schwinger function methods\linebreak (CSM) are used to provide estimates of pseudoscalar meson pole contributions - $\mathsf P = π^0$, $η$, $η^\prime$, $η_c$, $η_b$ - to the muon anomalous magnetic moment. The analysis framework is benchmarked via successful applications to an array of other meson and nucleon properties. It uses the leading order CSM truncation, augmented by a parametrisation of non-Abelian anomaly effects, to deliver an internally consistent treatment of all the pseudoscalar--two-photon transition form factors required to complete such a calculation. Employing those form factor predictions, the following results are obtained (units $10^{-11}$): $a_μ^{π^0} + a_μ^η + a_μ^{η^\prime} = 84.3(0.8)$ - a value lower than some other contemporary estimates; $a_μ^{η_c} = 0.82(0.04)$; and a value of $a_μ^{η_b}$ that is negligible. The total contribution is $\sum _{\mathsf P} a_μ^{\mathsf P} = 85.1(0.8) / 10^{11}$. Our analysis suggests that this pole contribution to $a_μ$ is still not known with precision better than 5\%.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Prospects for $K_{L}\toπ^{0}ν\barν$, $K_S\toμ^+μ^-$, $K_L\toπ^0 \ell^+\ell^-$ and $\varepsilon^{\prime}/\varepsilon$ after the new $K^{+}\toπ^{+}ν\barν$ result from NA62
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: The recently announced NA62 measurement of the $K^{+}\toπ^{+}ν\barν$ branching ratio, based on 2016--2024 data, is fully consistent with its very accurate Standard Model (SM) prediction. While it is not excluded that the final result based on 2016--2026 data will deviate from the SM prediction, the question arises whether a similar fate awaits the $K_{L}\toπ^{0}ν\barν$ decay. This decay is currently being searched for by the KOTO experiment, with the present upper bound roughly two orders of magnitude above its very precise SM prediction. The proposed KOTO II experiment aims to provide the first discovery of the $K_{L}\toπ^{0}ν\barν$ decay and measure its branching ratio. Building on the findings of several previous papers we demonstrate that in the presence of suitably chosen large new complex phases and of a small amount of new right-handed $\bar s d$ couplings, in addition to the left-handed ones, the $K_{L}\toπ^{0}ν\barν$ branching ratio can still be enhanced by one order of magnitude with respect to the SM prediction while keeping both $K^{+}\toπ^{+}ν\barν$ and $\varepsilon_K$ SM-like. Simultaneously the decays $K_S\toμ^+μ^-$, studied by LHCb, and $K_L\toπ^0\ell^+\ell^-$, searched for by KOTO II, can be strongly enhanced and the anomaly in the ratio $\varepsilon^{\prime}/\varepsilon$, as claimed by Dual QCD, removed. We illustrate this with an example of a specific $Z^\prime$ scenario.
High Energy Physics - Lattice.comment: 31 pages, 11 figures. v2: few references added, minor numerical updates, conclusions unchangedx, v3: minor changes, version published in EPJ C

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Extraction of charmonium branching fractions from $J/ψ\toγη_c$ radiative decays
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We assess the tension between theoretical predictions and the values quoted by the Particle Data Group (PDG) for the partial decay width and branching fraction associated with the radiative charmonium decay $J/ψ\toγη_c$. A profile scan over the most recent PDG data depending on the branching fraction $\mathcal{B}(J/ψ\toγη_c)$ suggests that the correlation between measured branching fractions is compatible with lattice QCD determinations of the partial decay widths $Γ(J/ψ\toγη_c)$ and $Γ(η_c\toγγ)$. We propose a theoretically grounded photon line shape for the radiative decay spectrum and a prescription for the extraction of (product) branching fractions involving the magnetic dipole (M1) transition $J/ψ\toγη_c$. This approach obviates the need to modify the photon energy spectrum line shape using empirical damping functions, as done in the most recent experimental extractions of $\mathcal{B}(J/ψ\toγη_c)$ from the photon line shape, thereby eliminating an inherent ambiguity in the determination of the derived observables.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: The Arf-Brown-Kervaire invariant on a lattice
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We propose a lattice formulation of the Arf-Brown-Kervaire (ABK) invariant which takes values in $\mathbb{Z}_8$. Compared to the standard $\mathbb{Z}$-valued index, the ABK invariant is more involved in that it arises in Majorana fermion partition functions with reflection symmetry on two-dimensional non-orientable manifolds, and its definition contains an infinite sum over Dirac eigenvalues that requires proper regularization. We employ the massive Wilson Dirac operator, with and without domain-walls, on standard two-dimensional square lattices, and use its Pfaffian for the definition. Twisted boundary conditions and cross-caps, which reverse the orientation, are introduced to realize nontrivial topologies equipped with nontrivial $\mathrm{Pin}^{-}$ structures of Majorana fermions. We verify numerically (and partly analytically) that our formulation on a torus, Klein bottle, real projective plane (as well as its triple connected sum), and two types of Möbius strip reproduces the known values in continuum theory.
High Energy Physics - Lattice.comment: Published in Physical Review D. 30 pages, 9 figures

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: A Nontrivial Lattice Scalar Quantum Field Model
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We introduce a new Euclidean quantum model with zero-spin scaled scalar fields on a spacetime hypercubic lattice, which we refer to as the hybrid model. The model coupling parameters are the hopping parameter $κ^2>0$ and the field interaction coupling $α>0$. Using the technique of lattice scaled fields, with a noncanonical scaling that corresponds to a partial renormalization (wave function renormalization), we show that the partition function of this model satisfies both thermodynamic and ultraviolet stability bounds, with constants which are uniform in the lattice volume $Λ_s$ and the lattice spacing $a\in(0,1]$. As a consequence, the model has a finite free energy per degree of freedom in the thermodynamic limit $Λ_s\nearrow\infty$, at least in the subsequential sense. Subsequently, we can also take the ultraviolet or continuum limit $a\searrow 0$. Besides the finiteness property of the free energy, for sufficiently small values of the model coupling parameters $κ^2$ and $α$, we show the model satisfies Osterwalder-Schrader positivity and construct the underlying physical quantum mechanical Hilbert space, and, using a polymer expansion, we show correlations also remain bounded in the thermodynamic limit. Finally, we perturbatively compute an infinite volume truncated four-point correlation showing it is nonzero. Noting that, for fixed $a$, perturbation series in $κ^2$ and $α$ converges, these results are sufficient to show that our hybrid model makes sense as a lattice quantum field theory in spacetime dimension $d=3,4$, with possible extensions to other higher values of $d$.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Renormalization-guided cascade upscaling for lattice field generation
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We introduce a renormalization-group (RG) guided machine-learning algorithm for lattice field generation based on approximate inversion of an RG transformation. A ``perfect blocking'' construction supplies equilibrated long-distance modes, while a conditional normalizing flow reconstructs short-distance details and brief rethermalization removes residual errors. In 2D $φ^4$ theory at criticality, a flow trained at $L\le32$ is reused recursively in cascades reaching $L=2048$ with correct long-distance physics.
High Energy Physics - Lattice.comment: 8 pages, 4 figures. v2: refs and minor numerical updates. Submitted to Phys. Rev. Lett

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Renormalization-guided inverse blocking for lattice field generation: construction and validation
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We propose an algorithm for generating lattice field configurations based on the approximate inversion of a renormalization-group blocking transformation. We optimize the blocking transformation using a ``perfect blocking'' condition so that the blocked lattice distribution is well approximated by a simple coarse action. The blocking is separated into an invertible smoothing transformation followed by decimation. Machine learning, in the form of a conditional normalizing flow, is used to reconstruct the short-distance degrees of freedom removed by the decimation. A short fine-action rethermalization then removes the residual mismatch. Because the coarse ensemble supplies the long-distance modes, the same blocking transformation and conditional flow can be reused recursively on larger lattices, producing a cascade of configurations from an initial small-volume ensemble. We test the method in two-dimensional $φ^4$ theory with $λ=1$ at criticality and demonstrate stable cascade upscaling from $16^2$ to $2048^2$ lattices on local computational resources. Controlled rethermalization tests show that short-distance mismatches relax rapidly, whereas a deliberately introduced mismatch in the relevant thermal direction relaxes much more slowly. The construction uses ingredients that admit natural extensions to higher-dimensional systems and, ultimately, to gauge and fermionic degrees of freedom.
High Energy Physics - Lattice.comment: 24 pages, 15 figures. v2: refs and minor numerical updates. Submitted to Phys. Rev. D

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Born-Oppenheimer chiral effective field theory and its application to $X_b$
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: Following the discovery of the exotic state $X(3872)$ in the charmonium spectrum, the possible existence of an analogous state, $X_b$, in the bottomonium sector has attracted considerable attention of the hadronic physics community. In this work, we lay the ground for the development of Born-Oppenheimer chiral effective field theory (BO$χ$EFT), that allows us to include both quark and hadron degrees of freedom as well as the full complexity of the meson-exchange potential in a systematic way. For illustration, the formalism to leading order (LO) is applied to the system of $χ_{b1}$ states and in particular the $X_b$. The two parameters that are present at this order are constrained using experimental information on the bottomonium spectrum together with lattice input on static quark-antiquark potentials, including string breaking effects. The framework identifies the observed $1^{++}$ state at 10.513 GeV with a predominantly molecular $X_b$, the bottom counterpart of the $X(3872)$, and predicts an additional predominantly compact bottomonium state at 10.544 GeV, about 60 MeV below the $B\bar{B}^*$ threshold.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Fully-beauty tensor tetraquark
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: Parameters of the fully-beauty tensor tetraquark $T=bb\overline{b}\overline{b }$ are computed using QCD sum rule method. The mass $m$ and coupling $ Λ$ of this state are evaluated by means of two-point sum rule approach. Prediction $m=(18530 \pm 86)~\mathrm{MeV}$ for the mass demonstrates that $T$ is stable against decays to pairs of $η_b η_b$ and $ΥΥ$ mesons. But it transforms to conventional particles due to $\overline{b}b$ annihilations to light quarks $\overline{q} q $ and $ \overline{s}s$ followed by creation of mesons $B^{(\ast)+}B^{( \ast)-}$, $ B^{(\ast)0}\overline{B}^{(\ast)0}$ and $B_s^{(\ast)0}\overline{B} _s^{(\ast)0}$. Partial width of these decay channels are calculated by invoking technical tools of three-point sum rule method. The latter allows us to estimate strong couplings at relevant tetraquark-meson-meson vertices and, hence, a width of the process under consideration. Our prediction $ Γ=(48 \pm 6)~\mathrm{MeV}$ along with the mass of this state can be valuable for experimental studies of all-heavy resonances.

Atomic Physics.title: An Aubry-André localized optical lattice clock
Atomic Physics.summary: Optical lattice clocks in space could improve satellite navigation systems and enable new tests of fundamental physics, including gravitational-wave detection and tests of relativity. In microgravity, atoms can tunnel to degenerate neighboring lattice sites, broadening the clock transition and limiting coherence times. We demonstrate Aubry-André localization in a bichromatic optical lattice formed by two magic-wavelength lasers, suppressing tunneling in a horizontal lattice clock emulating free fall. We recover a Fourier-limited clock Rabi spectrum and measure Ramsey coherence times of up to 2 s in shallow lattices, with up to 100-fold improvement over the delocalized regime. These results establish Aubry-André localization as a practical route to controlling tunneling in future space-based clocks, and open a path to operating terrestrial clocks at shallower lattice depths.

Atomic Physics.title: Cavity-modified static polarizabilities of atoms and small molecules within QED full configuration interaction
Atomic Physics.summary: Static dipole polarizabilities of H$_2$, LiH, and helium confined in a single-mode optical cavity are computed using quantum-electrodynamical full configuration interaction (QED-FCI). Response properties are obtained as finite-field derivatives of the coupled electron-photon energy. The cavity-induced modification is found to arise from the competition of two contributions of opposite sign, the dipole self-energy and photon exchange, whose relative strength depends on both the cavity frequency and the number of photons involved in the exchange. The residual change suppresses the response of the molecular ground electronic states. For the metastable states of helium atom this balance changes qualitatively, and the differential response of the $2\,^3S_1 \to 2\,^1S_0$ clock transition, which governs its sensitivity to static electric fields and to thermal radiation, is strongly enhanced instead. Cavity confinement can therefore either reduce or increase the dc Stark and blackbody-radiation shifts of a frequency standard, depending on the electronic structure of the states involved. The reported data serve as a reference for cavity-modified response and underscore the need for an exact treatment of light-matter correlation in cavity-QED predictions.
