Once a reference amplitude satisfying the exchange and qKZ constraints is specified, these transport equations determine the exact wavefunction in every fixed-particle-number sector. Independent reparametrizations of the right- and left-moving characteristics give couplings that depend on both space and time. For the chiral $SU(2)$ Gross--Neveu realization, we solve the qKZ equations for this full characteristic family using off-shell Bethe vectors. The resulting amplitudes are written in the characteristic labels, and their pullbacks give exact many-body wavefunctions for the corresponding space-time-dependent couplings. The two-body amplitude is a ratio of Gamma functions that resums the phase shifts from successive scattering processes. Equal-slope affine maps give a spatially homogeneous specialization in which the coupling depends only on time, and the Bethe ansatz with constant coupling is recovered when the qKZ step vanishes.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Yang-Baxter deformed sigma models on $\mathrm{SU}(N)/\mathrm{SO}(N)$
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study Yang--Baxter deformations of two-dimensional sigma models on compact symmetric spaces $\mathrm{SU}(N)/\mathrm{SO}(N)$, with particular emphasis on their ultraviolet behavior. We claim that the ultraviolet fixed point is described by the $\mathrm{SO}(N,\mathbb C)/\mathrm{SO}(N,\mathbb R)$ non-compact WZW model together with $N-1$ compact free bosons. We determine the leading correction to this fixed point and identify it with the perturbation generated by the corresponding screening currents. We also extend our construction to the broader class of symmetric spaces of maximal rank.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Non-linear evolution of five-dimensional black strings in effective field theory
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We use numerical relativity to study the non-linear instability of five-dimensional black strings in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity. Black strings evolve into a series of black holes joined by thinner string-like segments, but key features of the dynamics depend on the sign of the Gauss-Bonnet coupling. For positive coupling, favored by UV considerations, the growth of curvature invariants is limited within the validity of effective field theory (EFT), suggesting a mechanism for restoring weak cosmic censorship. For negative coupling this cap is absent and curvatures may grow until the EFT breaks down.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 8 pages, 6 figures. v2: companion paper arXiv:2610.13612; version submitted for publication

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Gauge-Invariant Brout--Englert--Higgs Mechanism without Spontaneous Breaking of Local Gauge Symmetry: A Quantum-Reference-Frame Formulation
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The Brout--Englert--Higgs (BEH) mechanism can be formulated in gauge-invariant relational terms without assigning physical spontaneous breaking to a local gauge redundancy. We treat the gauge orientation of the Higgs field as dynamical internal reference data and describe the gauge connection relative to this Higgs frame. On a regular patch where the frame exists, the Higgs kinetic term induces a positive-semidefinite mass-squared quadratic form on the gauge-orbit directions and reproduces the standard tree-level vector masses. A complete Higgs frame yields a gauge-invariant relational connection, whereas a partial frame is defined only up to a stabilizer group $H$ and produces Higgs stiffness only along the coset directions $G/H$. In quantum field theory the normalized frame and relational connection are nonpolynomial composite variables; physical masses are therefore characterized through suitably renormalized gauge-invariant composite correlators, or through fully dressed operators in residual-charged sectors. Applying this construction to the electroweak theory, we show that the Higgs frame relationalizes the $SU(2)_L$ redundancy while leaving a residual electromagnetic $U(1)_{\rm em}$ Gauss law: $W^\pm$ and charged fermionic modes require electromagnetic dressing, whereas neutral channels admit local gauge-invariant interpolators. This formulation connects Higgs dressings, FMS composites, and internal quantum-reference-frame language while keeping local mass generation distinct from global symmetry realization and topological obstructions.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Love at First Loop: Quantum Deformability of Near-Extremal Black Holes
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The static Love numbers of black holes vanish in classical, four-dimensional, asymptotically flat General Relativity. We study how this changes for the response of near-extremal Reissner--Nordström black holes to a minimally coupled massless scalar, at energies where the Schwarzian mode of the near-horizon throat fluctuates strongly. The black hole then responds as a quantum system with a spectrum of states. Its static response is a polarizability, given by virtual transitions between them. For $\ell=0$ the static Love number vanishes, by the shift symmetry of the scalar, but for multipoles $\ell\geq1$ the static Love numbers are nonzero: the finite rotational energy of the spin-$\ell$ intermediate states spoils the cancellation responsible for the classical result. Since the throat no longer has a classical geometry from which to read off a tidal response, we define it through the retarded Green's function, and compute its full frequency dependence at leading order in $r_+ω$. Its conservative part requires renormalization: the near-horizon theory fixes the coefficient of its logarithm, and with it a dependence on the energy that no local term can remove, while its finite local terms are matching data of the four-dimensional theory. The dissipative part is finite and scheme independent. For $\ell\geq1$, it vanishes at low frequencies when the energy is below the rotational gap, while at the gap threshold it becomes non-analytic in frequency and produces a late-time $t^{-3/2}$ tail.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Holographic Pseudo Entropy from the Rindler Method in AdS and Flat Space
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Via the Rindler method, we study holographic timelike entanglement entropy (TEE) for a general timelike interval in AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$ and flat$_3$/CCFT$_2$. The TEE is the pseudo entropy of a timelike interval. In the bulk, the imaginary part of the TEE comes from a timelike geodesic, but in the Rindler picture this geodesic has not been identified. After a Rindler transformation to a rotating BTZ black hole, the two spacelike extremal curves lie on the inner and outer horizons, and exchanging $l_u\leftrightarrow \ell l_φ$ takes one to the other. We find the geometric meaning of the timelike extremal curve: a geodesic stretched between the two horizons. Its length, $iπ\ell$, is independent of the interval, and it alone produces the imaginary part $iπc/6$. We follow the same procedure in flat space holography, where the spacelike curve sits on the cosmological horizon and the timelike curve lies between the cosmological horizon and timelike infinity. Evaluating the holographic TEE for a timelike interval in CCFT$_2$ on the plane, we find that, in contrast with the cylinder, the real and imaginary parts are equal.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: New analytic Janus and $S^4$ solutions for $\mathcal{N}=2^*$
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We construct a three-parameter family of regular analytic supergravity solutions which are dual to (a) the $\mathcal{N}=2^*$ gauge theory on the four-sphere, and (b) $\mathrm{U}(1)^2$-invariant Janus interfaces in $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM with or without the $\mathcal{N}=2^*$ mass turned on. To this end we employ a five-dimensional supergravity model coupled to six scalars which arises as a certain consistent truncation of type IIB supergravity on $S^5$. The curved domain wall solutions feature a hidden integral of motion which allows for their analytic treatment. We relate the three parameters of the solution to field theory sources and vevs and show how regularity of the solutions restricts their range. We briefly discuss the holographic evaluation of the one-point function of the field theory Lagrangian for our family of Janus solutions.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: On the analytic continuation and asymptotic behaviour of the two-point function in massless $φ^4$-theory in Euclidean de Sitter space
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: For the two-point function of the massless, minimally-coupled, real scalar field in Euclidean de Sitter space with $λφ^4$-interaction, we compute the leading-logarithmic terms in the invariant distance of the two-point function to $O(λ^2)$, which counts as the fifth subleading order (N$^5$LO) in the $\sqrtλ$-expansion. We show that the analytic continuation to Lorentzian signature coincides with the expansion of the analogous quantity computed in the stochastic formalism. We determine the large-order behaviour of the stochastic series expansion and prove its Borel summability, which suggests that the Euclidean theory can be used to extract the late-time behaviour of massless correlation functions in Lorentzian de Sitter space.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: What Do Event Generators Compute? Flux Functionals from Detector Operators
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Every physical prediction of an event generator is a statement about the hadronic fluxes that can be recorded by particle detectors. By contrast, the formal backbone of modern event-generator precision is provided by the unobservable partonic final states of the parton shower, with hadronisation included as a model. We construct the probability distribution of the hadronic fluxes non-perturbatively, directly from detector operators acting on asymptotic hadronic states, and encode it in an event generator source functional. This distribution contains every measurement a detector can make, and is therefore what a generator must compute with precision, including the effects of hadronisation. Restricting the functional to the energy flow yields the parton shower source functional, which is infrared and collinear safe and contains every calorimetric observable, making it a natural object against which to assess parton-shower accuracy. We compute its logarithmic structure at one loop in $e^+e^-$ annihilation, finding it directly sensitive to kinematic recoil and hence to the recoil scheme of a parton shower. The parton shower functional depends on a continuum of low scales, one for each resolved direction, and in a toy model its logarithms cannot be entirely resummed within a factorisation whose evolution derives only from the high-scale physics. Our operator-based formulation opens the door to the study of event-generator-like systems in theories beyond QCD, including conformal theories such as $N=4$ super-Yang-Mills theory, and thereby offers a new route to non-perturbative insight into event generation.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Revisiting Critical Higgs Inflation: Electroweak Couplings, CMB Observables, and Perturbative Unitarity
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We revisit the scenario of critical Higgs inflation, in which inflation is driven by the Standard Model Higgs boson with parameters chosen close to a critical point, giving rise to an inflection point in its potential. After reviewing this model, we perform a systematic study of its viability centered around three criteria: (1) consistency with electroweak-scale measurements, (2) ability to reproduce the cosmic microwave background (CMB) observables, and (3) sensitivity of the model predictions to unknown UV physics, based on a breakdown of perturbative unitarity. We first show that compliance with electroweak-scale measurements is controlled by the parameters in the Higgs potential at inflationary scales, also updating the literature values. We then demonstrate how for any choice of potential parameters, agreement with the CMB observables can be achieved through the choice of the nonminimal coupling, in both metric and Palatini formulations of gravity. However, we also find that there exist no regions of parameter space, in either the metric or Palatini formulations, in which compliance with all three physical criteria is possible. While this does not exclude the possibility of the Higgs field driving inflation, it means that predictions for any observable are in principle sensitive to the details of the model's UV completion.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Regularized interacting scalar quantum field theories
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: In this paper we consider self-interacting scalar quantum field theories over a $d$-dimensional Minkowski spacetime with various interaction Lagrangians which are suitable functions of the field. The interacting field observables are represented as power series over the free theory by means of perturbation theory. The object which is employed to obtain this power series is the time-ordered exponential of the interaction Lagrangian which is the $S$-matrix of the theory and thus itself a power series in the coupling constant of the theory. We analyze a regularization procedure which makes the $S$-matrix convergent to well-defined unitary operators. This regularization depends on two parameters. One describes how much the high-frequency contributions in the propagators are tamed and a second one describes how much the large-field contributions are suppressed in the interaction Lagrangian. We finally discuss the limits in which the parameters are removed in some lower-dimensional theories and for specific interaction Lagrangians. In particular, we show, by an abstract argument, that in three spacetime dimensions for a $φ^4_3$ theory one obtains sequences of unitary operators which are weakly-$*$ convergent to bounded operators in the limit of vanishing parameters. Although we lose control over the unitarity of the operator obtained in the limit and although the uniqueness of the limit is not under control, we notice that some basic causal properties are satisfied by the corresponding interacting fields. We furthermore observe that the very same limits, applied at fixed order, give back the ordinary perturbation theory results. Finally, we discuss a possible extension of these results to the case of a $φ^4_4$ theory.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: When does a state-dependent proto-area define a bulk geometry?
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: A holographic code assigns a state-dependent entropy remainder to every boundary region, but such remainders need not be the extremal lengths of any one bulk metric. We study this common-source question for the proto-area of a calibrated recovery, the entropy of a boundary region minus that of the matter recovered from it. At zeroth order the reference values must match the lengths of one reference geometry in a fixed renormalization scheme, and this matching also determines the entropy-to-length factor. On a graph with a fixed minimum-cut chamber the data derivatives must lie in the image of the cut-incidence matrix, whose left null vectors are witnesses. On the hyperbolic disk the first variation of renormalized length is the rank-two geodesic X-ray transform, with closed range in an adapted data space, and the geodesic displacement, fixed by a forced Jacobi equation, enters at second order. The resulting normal Hessian gives a gauge-invariant criterion, necessary and sufficient, for a regular pair of response coefficients to come from one metric two-jet. For the constant-curvature family generated by a boundary reparametrization the Hessian has a nonzero rank-four mode, so the image of the length map is curved. For a fixed recovery the proto-area Hessian is minus the Bogoliubov-Kubo-Mori information lost in recovery, which the Petz map decomposes orthogonally at a product reference, and which, on a finite-dimensional space of logical directions with positive minimum retained fraction, is at most a sharp multiple of the retained information. Geometric realization requires this loss to reproduce the normal length Hessian on every interval. Two codes show that exact regional area operators can fail to sew into one graph geometry, and that a matched reference with vanishing first response can fail at second order. All criteria refer to one recovery branch and one extremal-surface branch.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 114 pages, 5 figures. Revised and expanded, added zeroth-order matching, explicit second-order examples, and a discussion of RT phase transitions

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: From Trees to All Loops: The Combinatorial Geometry of Two-Site Cosmological Wavefunctions
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We prove, at arbitrary loop order and including arbitrary tadpole decorations, the shifted-tree decomposition of two-site cosmological wavefunction coefficients proposed in our previous work, and uncover the combinatorial and geometric structure underlying it. For conformally coupled scalars with polynomial interactions, this decomposition expresses each loop coefficient as a finite signed sum of tree coefficients evaluated at shifted energies. For bubble-like graphs, the alternating sum over a Boolean lattice can be written in terms of finite differences or maximal chains. We prove the maximal-chain identity algebraically by induction on loop order and geometrically by decomposing a cubical Laplace integral into simplices. The maximal chains correspond to permutohedron vertices, whose incident facets encode the chain-dependent divisors. For tadpole-decorated graphs, the finite-difference Leibniz rule gives an explicit expansion indexed by ordered partitions and local maximal chains, which glue into global maximal chains and organize the coefficient as a combinatorial "path integral". A natural ordering of the divisors yields a term-by-term match with graph tubings and completes the all-loop proof, while other orderings give alternative tubing representations of the same coefficient. These identities hold before spatial loop-momentum integration and extend to power-law FRW backgrounds by linearity of the twisted integral. Two-site loop coefficients can therefore be obtained directly from known tree coefficients without solving new loop-level differential systems.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 68 pages, 8 figures. v2: substantially extended, with a new title. The shifted-tree decomposition is now proven for all two-site graphs at arbitrary loop order, including arbitrary tadpole decorations, with explicit application to FRW loop wavefunction coefficients and a unified Boolean-lattice geometric picture

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Vanishing Love Numbers of Kerr-Newman Black Holes
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Tidal Love numbers characterize the conservative response of compact objects to external perturbations and provide a powerful probe of their nature. While the static Love numbers of Schwarzschild, Kerr, and Reissner--Nordström black holes remarkably vanish, the tidal response of a generic Kerr--Newman black hole has remained unexplored due to the intrinsic coupling between gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations. Exploiting a recent breakthrough in the separability of these perturbations, we analytically determine the static tidal response of the most general stationary black hole in four-dimensional Einstein--Maxwell theory. For arbitrary multipole order, charge, and spin, we show that the entire matrix of conservative Love numbers vanishes, including the mixed gravito-electromagnetic couplings. We also compute the nonvanishing static dissipative response induced by frame dragging.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Modular Flow and Holographic Timelike Entanglement Entropy in AdS and Flat Holography
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary:
Timelike entanglement entropy provides a useful probe of holographic theoris, yet an explicit bulk realization of the modular flow underlying its timelike extremal curve construction has so far been lacking. We construct modular flows associated with spacelike and timelike intervals in AdS$_{3}$/CFT$_{2}$ and extend this framework to flat$_{3}$/CCFT$_{2}$. Beginning with the boundary symmetry generators, we explicitly derive the boundary modular flows and extend them into the bulk, providing a systematic procedure that relates bulk modular flows to the extremal curves and holographic (timelike) entanglement entropy.
  For spacelike intervals, the resulting bulk modular flows determine the extremal curves, whose integrated line elements reproduce the standard holographic entanglement entropy. We then generalize this approach to timelike intervals, explicitly constructing the modular flows whose fixed points reproduce the extremal spacelike and timelike curves which gives the holographic timelike entanglement entropy. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first explicit construction of the modular flow associated with a timelike extremal curve for a timelike interval.
  The same procedure is then carried over to flat$_{3}$/CCFT$_{2}$, which give rise to the holographic (timelike) entanglement entropy. Finally, we show that the flat space results obtained in this work can be recovered from their AdS$_3$ counterparts in the flat space limit.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Exact and Finite de Sitter QFT from CFT
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Parallel to the AdS Scale-Space construction in \cite{Yang:2026AdS}, we construct a $(d+1)$-dimensional de Sitter QFT directly from $d$-dimensional CFT data. The dS geometry is the moduli space of oriented balls, and the lifted operators are obtained by conformal-family Casimir completion. The Euclidean parent CFT gives a finite wavefunction representation, while the Minkowski parent CFT gives a double-time representation that is unitary in the parent-time polarization. This provides a CFT-based framework for reexamining puzzles of dS and double-time QFT.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: V3: published version. Briefly reviewed relavant literature and added references

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Mock Modularity, Resurgence, and Dual False Theta Functions
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The $\hat{Z}$ invariant of a three-manifold $M_{3}$, a half-index of the $3d$ $\mathcal{N}=2$ theory $T[M_{3}]$, is well understood for negative-definite plumbed three-manifolds. For orientation-reversed manifolds, however, the known formulas fail to produce $q$-series, and making sense of the operation $q \rightarrow q^{-1}$ remains a central open problem. Seifert manifolds, whose $\hat{Z}$ invariants are built from false theta functions, offer a natural testing ground. We study ``dual false theta functions'', the objects that should replace false theta functions under orientation reversal. Two characterizations of these duals exist in the literature: a modular one, based on mock modularity with a prescribed shadow, and a resurgent one, based on Borel--Mordell integrals and transseries. We prove that the two characterizations are equivalent. We construct a new family of dual false theta functions for values of positive integer $p$ satisfying a Pell-equation condition. Its members are built from Zwegers' indefinite theta functions, have integer coefficients, and have effective central charge $c_{\text{eff}} \leq 1$. We also show that the mock theta functions of Li and Schwagenscheidt satisfy these characterizations and arise from a natural regularization of the divergent product $η^{3}(τ)ψ_{p, a}(- τ)$.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Decoupling Limit of Quiver Theories and the Angular Spectra of Extreme C-metrics
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We investigate the angular eigenvalue problem of the extreme charged C-metric. Starting from a constrained five-point Fuchsian description of the non-extremal angular equation, we obtain its extreme limit by decoupling a hypermultiplet in the dual four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$, $\mathrm{SU(2)}\times \mathrm{SU(2)}$ linear quiver gauge theory. We derive the parameter dictionary and renormalized Matone relations, and connect the physical limit $Q\to M$ to the quiver decoupling by an explicit coordinate transformation. Regular endpoint conditions give an algebraic quantization condition. Eigenvalues obtained from the truncated instanton prepotential are tested against independent angular spectra near extremality and at larger acceleration. The axisymmetric sector recovers the known exact spectrum.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: $\mathcal{N}=4$ single-minus superamplitudes and dual superconformal symmetry
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We construct the $\mathcal{N}=4$ supersymmetric completion of the recently proposed single-minus gluon amplitudes in $(2,2)$ signature, which are nonvanishing for all multiplicities on a half-collinear kinematic locus. The superamplitude factorises into a permutation-invariant measure $Δ^{(n-1)}$ with uniform little-group weight that imposes the half-collinearity constraint, a piecewise constant stripped amplitude $\tilde{A}_{1\ldots n}$ that is helicity blind and dual conformal invariant, and (super)momentum conservation delta functions. For $n=3$, our superamplitude reduces to the known $\overline{\rm MHV}$ superamplitude. We prove dual superconformal covariance of the $n$-point superamplitude, and further analyse the $\mathrm{Gr}(k,n)$ Grassmannian integral at $k=1$. Finally, we present the corresponding single-minus superamplitude in $\mathcal{N}=8$ supergravity.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 24 pages. v3: typos corrected, JHEP version

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Cosmic Colliders in Binary Blazars Probing Ultra-High-Energy Particle Physics
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: While terrestrial colliders and fixed-target cosmic-ray interactions are bounded at center-of-mass (CM) energies $\sqrt{s} \lesssim \mathcal{O}(10^5)\,\text{GeV}$, we demonstrate that bound sub-parsec binary blazars form broad-band, beam-beam hadronic ``Cosmic Colliders'', overcoming such limitation. Driven by modest jet misalignments ($θ_{\rm mis} \sim 1^\circ - 6^\circ$), co-streaming proton beams collide at CM energies reaching $\sqrt{s} \sim 10^{10}\,\text{GeV}$ - six orders of magnitude above the Large Hadron Collider. Operating in a strictly optically thin regime ($τ_{pp} \ll 1$), the system performs a continuous CM energy scan, probing asymptotic QCD scaling, gluon saturation, and Froissart unitarity, while opening a possible high-sensitivity window into physics beyond the Standard Model. Secondary PeV-EeV neutrinos and sub-TeV $γ$-rays fall directly within reach of current and planned observatories such as LHAASO, CTAO, IceCube, and GRAND, establishing binary blazars as laboratories for physics at the ultimate energy limit.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: The Hagedorn Temperature as a Nonequilibrium Dynamical Bottleneck in String Thermodynamics
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We revisit the Hagedorn regime of string theory from a nonequilibrium perspective using Steepest-Entropy-Ascent Quantum Thermodynamics (SEAQT), which formulates thermodynamic evolution directly on the state manifold without requiring a globally well-defined canonical ensemble. Treating the inverse temperature as an instantaneous, state-dependent quantity, we derive its exact scalar evolution equation, governed in the commuting limit by higher-order fluctuation moments. In an open-system extension we prove that the inverse-temperature mobility equals unity identically on the quasi-canonical family: a divergent Hagedorn variance is necessary but not sufficient for slowing-down, and a reservoir coupled democratically to the whole spectrum drives the system across the Hagedorn scale unimpeded. Slowing-down requires instead a hierarchy of injection rates, in which direct production of highly excited strings by the reservoir is slow compared with a cascade through light quasi-particle modes. The mobility then collapses to a floor set by the ratio of the two rates, the intensive variable is pinned near the Hagedorn scale, and energy condenses into the long-string sector at a finite rate; the pinning is a long-lived transient of computable duration. Promoting the Hagedorn scale to a moduli-dependent quantity along emergent-string limits yields a finite critical distance $Δ_*$ at which the thermodynamic inertia diverges as $(Δ_*-Δ)^{a-3}$ for $1<a<3$, and beyond which pinning can activate. Since Kaluza--Klein towers admit no such divergence, this provides a thermodynamic discriminant between emergent-string and decompactification limits.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Matching Tidal Deformability (Wilson) Coefficients to Black Hole Love Numbers in Higher-Curvature Gravity
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We present a consistent mapping between tidal deformability coefficients (tidal Love numbers) and Wilson coefficients in effective field theory (EFT) descriptions of higher-curvature theories of gravity. In this work, we focus on the connection between the static response of a non-spinning black hole and the corresponding Wilson coefficient governing tidal imprints in gravitational-wave signals. We analyze a set of control cases to identify the key ingredients required for a systematic computation and matching procedure. In doing so, we highlight shortcomings in existing results that rely on the standard matching approach used in General Relativity when applied to higher-curvature gravity theories. As an explicit demonstration, we compute the relevant coefficients for cubic gravity theories. Our findings bridge an important gap in the correspondence between tidal Love numbers and Wilson coefficients in EFT extensions of General Relativity, which had not been thoroughly explored previously.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Metric and dilaton information from high-overtone quasinormal modes of analytic Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton black holes
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Black-hole interiors are hidden from exterior observers, yet their geometry can enter the high-overtone spectrum of linear perturbations. We study how this spectrum encodes metric and supporting-matter information in analytic Einstein--Maxwell--dilaton black holes. Coupling a neutral spectator to the dilaton at fixed UV dimension provides a matter-sensitive channel alongside the momentum response. For real-endpoint spacelike connections, the momentum response and mass-label dependence separate the metric exponents from the signed dilaton slope. Near the causal threshold, a complex endpoint controls the spectral family: the mass profiles approach a common value, producing a shared fractional correction, while regular propagation retains label dependence. This mechanism is present at criticality without an inner horizon and continues locally into timelike interiors. Exterior numerical spectra support the reconstruction and the leading complex-endpoint responses. Local scaling and probe coupling set the candidate responses, while wave connection determines their imprint on the exterior spectrum.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Self-Interacting Dark Matter: From Particle Physics Theories to Structure Formation Simulations
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We develop a unified theory-to-simulation framework for self-interacting dark matter (SIDM), connecting microscopic dark-sector physics to nonlinear structure formation. We systematize particle-physics ingredients of representative SIDM models and map microscopic parameters and interactions onto structure-formation simulation inputs. These include internal-state populations and reaction networks, velocity- and angle-dependent cross sections, inelastic and dissipative energy exchange, decay rates and recoil kinematics, and modifications to cosmological initial conditions. The numerical framework builds on the efficient, scalable SIDM infrastructure introduced in our companion work for the moving-mesh code AREPO-2, providing substantial performance gains over AREPO-1. We implement isotropic and anisotropic self-scattering with constant or velocity-dependent cross sections, multi-state and inelastic reactions, and dissipative scattering, complemented by a dedicated dark-matter decay module. For strongly forward-peaked interactions, the anisotropic hybrid SIDM scheme combines frequent small-angle drag-diffusion with explicit rare large-angle scattering, achieving speed-ups of up to $\sim100\times$ relative to fully anisotropic Monte Carlo in the tested configurations. We validate the implementations through beam-lattice deflection experiments, thermalization and uniform-box decay tests, isolated-halo gravothermal core-collapse simulations, and cosmological box and zoom-in simulations. These tests recover analytical predictions, establish consistency between equivalent numerical treatments, and reproduce published inelastic and dissipative SIDM benchmarks. The resulting modular framework connects dark-sector models to nonlinear astrophysical predictions, enabling exploration of microscopic interactions beyond standard isotropic, elastic SIDM.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Where is the conformal coupling in Palatini gravity?
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study the conformal coupling in the torsion-free Palatini formulation with an ordinary scalar kinetic term. Tuning the curvature coupling cannot restore Weyl invariance in a Palatini theory with an ordinary scalar kinetic term because, for an independent and inert connection, the scalar-curvature term is separately Weyl-invariant, and no finite curvature coupling cancels the Weyl variation of the kinetic term. This can be demonstrated by evaluating the energy-momentum trace on the scalar equation of motion and noting that it is explicitly independent of the Palatini coupling. Eliminating the connection, we construct a map between the curvature coupling and the effective coupling for the equivalent metric theory, and demonstrate that the scalar continues to propagate even if the reduced kinetic coefficient vanishes. We also show that it becomes a Weyl compensator with a scale-invariant potential only in the rescaled infinite-coupling limit, which in four dimensions is directly related to Palatini ${\cal R}^2$ gravity. We calculate the running of the couplings at one loop, and we find that the conformal shift in the metric-curvature coupling's beta function generates a metric-curvature coupling on a fixed metric-affine background, whereas the independent-curvature coupling runs homogeneously. Furthermore, we follow an alternate prescription in which the connection is allowed to respond to the scalar fluctuations, which results in a different scalar Hessian and therefore different beta functions. Nonetheless, we find that both prescriptions admit the formal infrared limit $(ξ_{eff},λ_{eff})\to(1/6,0)$ through different limits of the original couplings in the case of positive perturbative quartics. Finally, we note that trajectories starting on the positive gravitational branch encounter a vanishing gravitational coefficient at a finite scale before this endpoint.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Generalized Beth--Uhlenbeck entropy formula from the $Φ-$derivable approach
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We derive a generalized Beth-Uhlenbeck formula for the entropy of a dense fermion system with strong two-particle correlations, including scattering states and bound states. We work within the $Φ-$derivable approach to the thermodynamic potential. The formula takes the form of an energy-momentum integral over a statistical distribution function times a unique spectral density. In the near mass-shell limit, the spectral density reduces, contrary to naïve expectations, not to a Lorentzian but rather to a "squared Lorentzian" shape. The relation of the Beth-Uhlenbeck formula to the $Φ$-derivable approach is exact at the two-loop level for $Φ$. The formalism we develop, which extends the Beth-Uhlenbeck approach beyond the low-density limit, includes Mott dissociation of bound states, in accordance with Levinson's theorem, and the self-consistent back reaction of correlations in the fermion propagation. We discuss applications to further systems, such as quark matter and nuclear matter.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 13 pages, 5 figures, version accepted for publication in the special issue of "Contributions to Plasma Physics" on the occasion of the 65th birthday of Michael Bonitz

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Symmetric Gapped States and Symmetry-Enforced Gaplessness in 3-dimensions
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We establish a comprehensive framework for characterizing the infrared (IR) phases of a fermionic quantum theory in three spatial dimensions, based on its quantum anomalies associated with a finite symmetry. We uncover a fundamental dichotomy among these anomalies: the first class of anomalies can always be realized by symmetric gapped states, while the second class can never be realized by gapped states without breaking the given symmetry, establishing the phenomenon of symmetry-enforced gaplessness in these settings. Moreover, using the construction of symmetry extension, we construct the candidate gapped states that theories with the first class of anomalies can flow to in the IR. As an application, we provide concrete predictions of the candidate IR phases of (3+1)-dimensional gauge theories based on our results. Our results also suggest that systems with discrete chiral anomalies cannot be gapped out by adding arbitrary bosonic degrees of freedom.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Out-of-time-order hydrodynamics and scrambling
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Hydrodynamics as an effective field theory (EFT) has been immensely successful for predicting the behaviour of time-ordered correlation functions in the long-time, large-distance regime. In this paper, we analyse the predictions of hydrodynamics for scrambling as probed by out-of-time order correlators (OTOCs). To do so, we consider an all-derivative order generalisation of the Schwinger-Keldysh EFT of hydrodynamics extended to a four-fold time contour required to capture OTOCs. A crucial ingredient of the construction is a local SL(2,R) symmetry, which has previously been suggested as a mechanism for scrambling. We also derive this exact EFT from the microscopic formulation of the maximally chaotic low-temperature limit of the SYK lattice, thereby determining all transport coefficients for this model. As a novel application, we compute the OTOC of energy currents, find that its exponential growth saturates the chaos bound, and match it to expectations based on a shockwave (or scramblon) effective description. Our work shows that the universality of hydrodynamics degrees of freedom extends beyond traditional time-ordered correlators to more complex observables such as OTOCs.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Exact Evaluation of Lattice-Regularized Scalar Field Vacuum Amplitude via Site Permutations
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: A novel approach to a computation of vacuum amplitude for a single scalar field in any number of dimensions with arbitrary potential on a lattice is proposed. The computation involves symmetrization of kinetic exponential factor in the path integral over all permutations of lattice sites and Waring decomposition of the symmetrized expression.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Conserved-charge diffusion in hot and dense QCD matter
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study the coupled diffusion of baryon number, electric charge, and strangeness in hot and dense quark matter using a three-flavor Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model with self-consistently generated constituent quark masses. The complete diffusion matrix is evaluated within a relaxation-time kinetic approach, including its diagonal and off-diagonal components. We find that the off-diagonal transport coefficients exhibit distinct temperature and baryon-chemical-potential dependence associated with the flavor-dependent composition of the charge carriers. We further investigate generalized charge diffusivities and mobilities obtained from the corresponding susceptibilities. At finite baryon chemical potential, the baryon and strangeness mobility scales cross, reflecting the different density dependence of their transport coefficients and susceptibilities. The results provide model benchmarks for coupled conserved-charge transport in baryon-rich QCD matter.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 11 pages, 7 captioned figures. Submitted for publication

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Scale-separated AdS$_3$ vacua from $G_2$-orientifolds using bispinors
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: In this paper, minimal supersymmetric AdS$_3$ solutions on $G_2$-orientifolds of type IIA and IIB supergravity are studied. These are obtained by techniques of the bispinor formalism. A straightforward argument is derived against AdS$_3$ solutions in massless type IIA string theory on such $G_2$-backgrounds. Furthermore, it is shown that some of the AdS$_3$ solutions in massive type IIA do admit a separation of scales, whereas the same cannot be said for the type IIB vacua. Finally, a formula for the 3d superpotential in the bispinor language is given that is valid for both type IIA and type IIB configurations. It is shown that the supersymmetry conditions of this superpotential lead back to the bispinor equations.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: v3: 18 pages. Added analysis of B-field variations. Corrected and clarified several earlier statements; minor additional revisions. The main results and conclusions remain unchanged

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Cohomological Aspects of Entanglement Entropy: From Information Theory to Noncommutative Geometry
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We develop a cohomological framework for entanglement entropy that unifies information theory, operator algebras, and noncommutative geometry. Entropy is a 1-cocycle in information cohomology; we generalize this to the quantum setting via Hochschild and cyclic cohomology. For an inclusion of von Neumann algebras N contained in M with a faithful normal state w admitting a cyclic and separating vector, and a conditional expectation E: M -> N (whose existence is equivalent to modular invariance of N by Takesaki's theorem), we construct the entanglement complex as the image of the transgression map tau_w on the relative cyclic complex, where A is a dense *-subalgebra of M and B = A intersect N. Our main result identifies entanglement cohomology with the kernel of the restriction map HC*(A) -> HC*(B), up to the connecting homomorphism d of the long exact sequence of the pair (A,B); when d = 0, the identification is exact. The relative modular cocycle u_t = (Dw : D(w|_N) o E)_t generates explicit entanglement classes when E is not w-invariant, with the Araki relative entropy as its infinitesimal generator. The framework accommodates Type III von Neumann algebras, where no local density matrix exists, and leads to a holographic proposal: a subspace of H^1_ent is conjecturally dual to linearized modular Hamiltonian perturbations of the bulk entanglement wedge. We verify the construction in finite-dimensional, type II_1, and type III_1 examples.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: Substantially revised in response to community feedback: restructured Sections 2-4, added explicit von Neumann hypotheses, proved the kernel identification with the obstruction δ, added holographic applications and alternative proofs. Companion paper for full details

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Large condensation in enriched $\infty$-categories
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We demonstrate that many algebraic features of higher condensation theory are really features of higher algebra. We work in the context of monads on the unit of a monoidal 2- category. Assuming that 2-categorical unstraightening is monoidal, we show that the functor which takes such a monad to its Eilenberg-Moore object is lax monoidal. We use this to introduce an analog of condensation for codimension-i symmetries, without assuming dualizability. We give sufficient conditions for Morita equivalence of endomorphisms of condensates. We relate higher centralizers to iterated categories of modules. Along the way, we prove results pertaining to functoriality of Day convolution for enriched infinity-categories, which may be of independent interest.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: V2: Revised for correctness and readability. Main theorem weakened; a necessary 2-categorical hypothesis made explicit and proof simplified. For Morita equivalence, an additional generation criterion added and proof simplified. Condensation procedure modified to avoid set-theoretic issues and simplify notation. Introduction and abstract rewritten; article rearranged for narrative clarity

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: About P-adic Numbers and Professor Igor Volovich on the Occasion of his 80th Anniversary
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We recall a 1987 paper written by Volovich and our subsequent work with Okada which established the Feyman rules for the p-adic string and the related non-local field theory which found diverse physical applications. We add some memories of visits to Moscow during 1989-91.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: To appear in the 2026 Proceedings of the"New Horizons in Mathematical Physics" published by the Steklov Mathematical Institute, Moscow

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: A No-Go Theorem for Nonspherical Bounces with a Single Negative Mode
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: False vacuum decay is conventionally described by a spherically symmetric bounce with a single negative fluctuation mode. This raises a fundamental question: can the single negative mode requirement itself enforce spherical symmetry, independently of action minimization? For a single real scalar field with a smooth potential in flat spacetime, we rigorously prove that every localized nonspherical saddle with zero initial velocity has at least three negative modes. Additional reflection symmetries further tighten these bounds, as illustrated in a sextic scalar model. Our findings exclude nonspherical bounce candidates with a single negative mode, providing a complementary spectral foundation for the spherical bounce description of false vacuum decay.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Gravitational wave scattering at $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$: Murua construction and elliptics
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We compute the amplitude for the scattering of a gravitational wave off of a spinless point particle at fourth order in Newton's constant, using the worldline quantum field theory formalism. A decomposition of our master integrals incorporating Murua coefficients allows us to entirely bypass the cut subtraction needed to convert the scattering amplitude into the Magnusian, the latter mapping directly onto the scattering phase shift in partial wave space. Elliptic functions appear in momentum space for the first time for this process at this order. To compare to the phase shift from black hole perturbation theory, we present an analytical method for performing the partial wave projection of the new elliptic sector to any partial wave order $\ell$, and verify the equivalence of the Magnusian and the phase shift. This demonstrates that point-particle worldline quantum field theory accurately describes Schwarzschild black holes up to $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 8 pages, 2 figures. v2: version accepted for publication, new method for partial-wave projection of elliptics

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Target-space fusion of classical topological defects
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Classical fusion of sigma-model defects is commonly approached by combining their worldsheet actions and eliminating the intermediate fields. This procedure, however, does not systematically identify the resulting target-space defect or its possible branches. We address this problem by formulating fusion as a reduction of the target-space defect data. Local descent of the intrinsic two-form and global descent of the connection determine the admissible branches. For symmetry-preserving bi-branes in the $SU(2)$ WZW model and Hopf-fibre T-duality defects, the prescription reproduces the known biconjugacy-class branches and the finite family of fibre-shift defects. The appearance of several branches provides a classical manifestation of non-invertible fusion. We further use the framework to construct TsT and T-dual biconjugacy defects, including their global consistency conditions. It therefore provides a systematic method for computing classical fusion and constructing new defects from known ones.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Interplay of CPT-Violating and CPT-Conserving Lorentz Invariance Violation at DUNE
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We present a study of Lorentz invariance violation (LIV) in neutrino oscillations, with primary emphasis on the interplay between CPT-violating and CPT-conserving Standard Model Extension (SME) coefficients. We find that $a_{ee}$ and $a_{ττ}$ dominate among the diagonal LIV coefficients, whereas $a_{eμ}$ and $a_{eτ}$ provide the most significant off-diagonal contributions. In contrast, the corresponding $c_{αβ}$ coefficients have comparatively sub-leading effects. Taking DUNE as a representative long-baseline experiment, we show that the sensitivity to CP violation is modified by LIV in a parameter-specific manner. We find correlations between off-diagonal LIV parameters, and non-trivial dependence on the new phases. In absence of LIV, DUNE is expected to establish CP violation at $5σ$ for a limited fraction of $δ_{CP}$ values. We find that the presence of $a_{ee}$, $a_{ττ}$, $a_{eμ}$ and $a_{eτ}$ weakens the CP discovery potential, reducing the achievable significance to below $3σ$ over a substantial fraction of $δ_{\rm CP}$. The independent impact of $c_{αβ}$ terms also results in suppression, but in combination with $a_{αβ}$, they introduce degeneracies, complicating the extraction of $δ_{CP}$. This generally results in a deterioration of CP violation sensitivities below $5σ$. These findings emphasize the importance of incorporating LIV effects in precision oscillation studies at upcoming long-baseline experiments.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: A general proof of integer Rényi QNEC
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We prove the Rényi quantum null energy condition for every integer Rényi order $n\geq2$. In local Poincaré-invariant quantum field theory, this states that the sandwiched Rényi divergence (SRD) of an excited state relative to the vacuum is convex along a future-directed null deformation. We assume that the deformation is realized by the canonical translations of a half-sided modular inclusion and that the divergence is finite for the initial, undeformed algebra. The proof establishes convexity of the SRD along the induced positive contraction semigroup on Haagerup $L^n(M)$, for every non-zero positive initial element. We also establish a Rényi ant formula at every even integer order and, under an additional regularity assumption, at odd integer orders. The Rényi ant formula identifies the negative first null derivative of SRD with a multiple of the infimum of the canonical null-translation energy over vector purifications of an escort state constructed from the excited state and the vacuum.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 43 pages, 1 figure. v2: Significant rewriting to improve exposition; results unchanged. v3: Significant rewriting; added integer Rényi ant theorem; updated abstract

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Couch-Torrence conformal inversion, supersymmetry and conserved charges for D3-branes
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: An asymptotically flat spacetime in $D=4$ can be mapped via Couch-Torrence conformal inversion to the geometry around an extremal non-expanding and non-rotating horizon. At the linearized level, an infinite tower of conserved Newman-Penrose charges can be found at null-infinity, while infinitely many Aretakis charges are conserved in the near-horizon. Couch-Torrence inversion allows one to establish a matching between the two sets of asymptotic charges. In this work we construct the Newman-Penrose and Aretakis scalar charges in higher-dimensional geometries of D3-branes in $D=10$ and D3-brane bound states in $D=4$ and $D=5$ and establish a precise matching between them through the inversion. By exploiting the residual unbroken supersymmetry of Type IIB supergravity, we demonstrate that it is possible to relate scalar (complex dilaton) charges to higher spin charges. In particular, we determine infinite towers of conserved asymptotic spinorial charges associated with the dilatino fluctuations, and determine the map through inversion.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: SymTFT Entanglement and Holographic (Non)-Factorization
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Given two otherwise decoupled $D$-dimensional CFTs which possess a common (finite) symmetry subcategory, one can consider entangled boundary states of their $(D+1)$-dimensional SymTFTs. This roughly corresponds to performing a gauging of the tensor product of two CFTs, and we call this phenomena ``SymTFT entanglement" (or ``S-entanglement" for short). In the case when these CFTs have semiclassical holographic duals, the S-entanglement relates the bulk gauge charges between two otherwise disconnected AdS spacetimes as we highlight in several top-down examples. We show that taking partial traces of such S-entangled states leads to a streamlined approach to preparing ensemble-averaged CFTs in string theory. This ensemble averaging coincides with that generated by $α$-states in the baby universe Hilbert space, and we propose a symmetry-enriched generalization of this Hilbert space via generalized global symmetries. We quantify how this symmetry-governed averaging violates holographic factorization and leads to the emergence of bulk global symmetries. We also consider the eternal (two-sided) AdS black hole geometries, where our SymTFT entanglement considerations imply that there exist refinements of the usual theromofield double state preparation of the system. We show that one may prepare the system in such a way that the total CFT data does not factorize into left and right copies. As anticipated by Marolf and Wall \cite{Marolf:2012xe}, we highlight that such considerations are necessary to define the gauge charges of eternal black holes, and in certain cases, can imply that there exist extended bulk objects stretching across the wormhole which cannot be expressed in terms of a product of left and right CFT operators.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Gravitational Radiation from Shockwave Scattering in the Self-Force EFT
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We investigate the high-energy collision of two spinless bodies within the Self-Force Effective Field Theory (EFT), taking one of them to be massless and highly energetic, such that it generates a gravitational shockwave (GSW) background. The GSW is perturbed by the second body, either massless or massive, satisfying respectively $E_2/E_1\ll1$ or $m_2/E_1\ll1$. Although the Self-Force expansion for shockwaves is frame-dependent, we freely choose a frame in which this EFT manifests its power, obtaining results valid to all orders in Newton's constant that make the underlying resummation patterns evident. Specifically, we push the expansion to 1SF order and prove the all-order vanishing of the so-called recoil operators in light-cone gauge. We obtain the exact graviton propagator on the shockwave background, matching previous results, and use it to compute the on-shell waveform at 1SF order in momentum space, specialising to the massless-massless collision. The waveform is computed to all orders in the Post-Minkowskian, or weak-field, expansion. In the trans-Planckian regime, its resummed form is proved to yield a UV-finite angular spectrum of radiated energy.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Sensitivity of calibration-free DESI DR2 BAO--supernova constraints to a distance-duality tilt
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Recent measurements from DESI baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) have reported a moderate preference for dynamical dark energy, challenging the standard $Λ$CDM paradigm. Nonetheless, such a trend could reflect a tension between the shape and the offset of the Hubble diagrams predicted by current BAO and Type Ia supernovae (SN) data, which may underpin a possible breakdown of the cosmic distance duality relation (CDDR) linking luminosity distances $D_{\rm L}$ and angular-diameter distances $D_{\rm A}$. We explore this possibility by parametrizing deviations from this relation as $η(z) \equiv D_{\rm L} / [{(1+z)}^2 D_{\rm A}] = α{(1+z)}^\varepsilon$, and investigate how the preference for a Chevallier-Polarski-Linder (CPL) dynamical dark energy is modified once $\varepsilon \!\neq\! 0$ is allowed. Using DESI DR2 and uncalibrated SN data (Pantheon$+$, DES-Dovekie, Union3, and Union3.1), we find that allowing $\varepsilon$ to vary freely in both $Λ$CDM and CPL reduces the CPL preference with respect to $Λ$CDM by a larger amount than the addition of spatial curvature $Ω_k$; only Union3.1 exhibits comparable reductions. We also find that the preference reduction is robust to alternative $η(z)$ parametrizations, and that the $η(z)$ constraints remain stable under the removal of BAO tracers or low-redshift cutoffs for Pantheon$+$, whereas the DES-Dovekie preference largely disappears once $z < 0.1$ SN are removed. In a separate calibrated analysis, illustrative Planck sound-horizon and SH0ES absolute-magnitude priors give $α\simeq 0.942 \pm 0.014$, quantifying the normalization mismatch under those assumptions. We also map the CDDR violation onto photon-loss and varying-$G$ scenarios, concluding that the cosmological constraints are much weaker than existing constraints on these physical mechanisms.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 15 pages, 5 figures. The numerical analysis files for the production of the results and figures can be found in the following GitHub repository: https://github.com/Rivillion/Sensitivity_test_distance_duality

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: The Information Content of Krylov Observables: A Machine Learning Approach
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We employ machine learning techniques to estimate the amount of information contained in three Krylov-space observables: the spread complexity $C(t)$, the discrete Wigner negativity $N(t)$, and the normalized negativity $χ(t)=N(t)/|S(t)|$, where $S(t)$ is the survival amplitude. We study thermofield-double evolutions on GUE, GOE and Poisson spectra, and on the integrable $SL(2,R)$ Krylov chain of a two-dimensional CFT primary, with Lanczos coefficients $b_n=α\sqrt{n(n+2h-1)}$. To introduce chaos we add a GUE random matrix to the integrable chain, $H(\varepsilon)=H_{SL(2,R)}+\varepsilon R_0 W_{GUE}$, where $R_0$ is its spectral half-width. Either $C(t)$ or $N(t)$ alone determines the thermofield temperature, with $R^2\simeq0.999$. However, neither can reconstruct the fine structure of the spectral form factor. In the integrable sector all three observables carry the same information. When we turn on chaos an asymmetry appears: $χ$ predicts $C$ better than $C$ predicts $χ$. This gap grows from $+0.33$ to $+0.77$, while the same gap for the raw negativity decays to zero. The extra information comes from the survival amplitude, and $χ(t)$ carries it while $C(t)$ can still be recovered from $χ(t)$. We derive a lower bound on this gap, set by the fraction of the variance of $χ$ that comes from $S$.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 54 pages, 34 figures, 4 tables. Accepted for publication in Physical Review D, https://journals.aps.org/prd/accepted/10.1103/hqts-lp2n

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Analytic results for slow-roll curved-space inflation and exponential potentials
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We derive analytic templates for the scalar and tensor primordial power spectra describing cosmologies that transition from kinetic dominance to slow-roll inflation in the presence of spatial curvature. Our results extend recent works in the literature, allowing us, in particular, to recover the scalar and tensor tilts analytically. We revisit the case of curvature-assisted single-exponential models in light of this framework. In the case of an open universe, the phase space of such models naturally includes cosmologies that start out in a kinetic-dominance regime followed by a parametrically controlled quasi-de Sitter phase. However, they do not fit in the framework of the templates, as their second Hubble slow-roll parameter remains of order one in the quasi-de Sitter regime.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 36 pages, 7 figures, 4 tables. V2: minor changes, appendix B expanded, references added, version to appear in EPJC

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: The poltergeist mechanism - Enhancement of scalar-induced gravitational waves with early matter-dominated era -
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Gravitational waves induced by primordial density perturbations provide a powerful probe of the Universe's thermal history, which may include an early matter-dominated (eMD) era predicted by well-motivated particle-physics models. The induced GWs can be significantly enhanced when the Universe undergoes a sudden transition from an eMD era to an era with pressure, such as a radiation or kination era. This enhancement arises from the growth of density perturbations during the eMD era and their rapid oscillations during the era with pressure. This phenomenon is called the poltergeist mechanism. In this review, we explain the essence of the poltergeist mechanism and explore concrete scenarios in which such an enhancement can occur.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 44 pages, 19 figures, v2: version accepted for publication in Reviews of Modern Physics

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Entanglement and parametric resonance in coupled oscillator systems
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study a system of two quadratically-coupled harmonic oscillators, prepared respectively in the ground state and in a coherent state. This toy model can describe for instance the dynamics of one mode of a quantum field evolving in a harmonically-oscillating classical background. In such situations, it is well-known that, depending on the background oscillation amplitude and coupling strength, the system may exhibit parametric resonance. Using the Feynman-Vernon influence functional, we analyze the interplay between parametric resonance and quantum entanglement by perturbatively computing the purity of the mixed state resulting from tracing over one of the oscillators. We find a runaway behavior of the quantum entanglement between the two oscillators, as well as a rapid breakdown of the validity of perturbation theory, in regions of parametric instability. This provides a quantitative confirmation of various statements in the literature and is highly relevant to questions pertaining to the validity of the semiclassical approximation in coupled quantum-classical systems.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Nonequilibrium framework for first-order phase transitions
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The first-order phase transition is central to electroweak baryogenesis and gravitational wave generation, yet thermal equilibrium effective potential analyses cannot describe the real-time non-equilibrium dynamics of the phase transition process. We use the Schwinger-Keldysh closed-time-path formalism of real-time finite-temperature field theory to study these effects. For the $φ^6$ model, we derive the effective action and the corresponding Langevin equation. We further extend the formalism to the two scalar fields case, obtaining the coupled Langevin equations. These results provide a theoretical framework for the bubble nucleation simulation of the non-equilibrium phase transition process, laying the foundation for reliable predictions of baryogenesis and gravitational wave signals.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Beyond Calabrese-Cardy Scaling: Exceptional-Point Sensitivity and the de Sitter RT Surface
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary:
Entanglement entropy at one-dimensional criticality typically follows
  the Calabrese--Cardy scaling.
  In the non-Hermitian critical free-fermion systems studied here,
  however, we find an additional interval-independent contribution
  $S_{\rm res}=\log(ΔL)$, which allows the entropy to remain
  sensitive to energy gaps below the finite-size scale, $Δ<1/L$.
  We refer to this term as the residual entropy.
  To understand its infrared origin, we examine finite-depth non-unitary continuous multiscale entanglement renormalization on a ring. Terminating the critical RG circuit before its singular final layer leaves a two-site infrared state. We calculate the entropy of this state directly from its correlation matrix and recover the same \(\log(ΔL)\) dependence. The emergent de Sitter geometry provides a complementary geometric interpretation: extremal curves associated with different boundary intervals extend to a common infrared endpoint, suggesting how the entanglement retained there can contribute equally to their entropies.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Triggering Higgs vacuum decay
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The Standard Model Higgs potential seems unstable at field values $h > h_{\rm top} \sim 10^{10}$ GeV. Vacuum decay can be triggered by $N\sim 4π/λ\sim 1000$ overlapped Higgs bosons with energy $\sqrtλ h_{\rm top}$. However, this configuration is stimulated by ultra-high energy collisions with a $\exp(-{\cal O}(N))$ suppression, comparable to spontaneous vacuum decay: no `Higgspolosion' enhancement arises. This implies that ultra-high energy cosmic ray collisions are safe, despite that their number (in production sites) likely is tens of orders of magnitude higher than what usually estimated (in space). We speculate on how vacuum decay could be induced classically at futuristic ultra-high energy colliders (either using a few right-handed electron beams, or a double collision producing an in-coming wave of $N$ boosted Higgs bosons) and on how the resulting vacuum bubble could be controlled to extract energy.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 27 pages, 8 figures. v2: published on JHEP. v3: extra triggering scheme added to section 5.1

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Injectivity of specialization maps in critical cohomology
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Specialization maps are natural maps from equivariant vanishing cycle cohomology to the equivariant cohomology of the ambient space. We study their injectivity problem for moduli stacks of representations of quivers with potentials, including those associated with generalized conifolds and finite subgroups of $SO(3,\mathbb{C})$. Applications to the irreducibility of modules of Reshetikhin type shifted Yangians are also given.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 22 pages. Applications to irreducibility of Yangian modules are added

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Thermodynamic Volumes of Extended Black Hole Thermodynamics with Auxiliary Gauge Fields
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: By applying the Iyer-Wald formalism to the modified Lagrangian form for the gravitational system, where the coupling constants appearing in the original Lagrangian form, such as the cosmological constant, are promoted to the dynamical scalar fields by introducing the corresponding auxiliary gauge fields, we derive the first law of the extended black hole thermodynamics, where the resulting thermodynamic volumes as the conjugate thermodynamic variables to the coupling constants are nevertheless independent of the auxiliary gauge fields and exactly the same as those obtained before via varying the coupling constants by brute force. In addition, it is further shown that such volumes can also be expressed in terms of the auxiliary gauge fields and evaluated on the black hole horizon, validating the proposal made in the previous literature.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Regular-Zero Drinfeld-Sokolov Charges in Doubled Four-Dimensional Chern-Simons Theory
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study classical local conserved charges obtained after finite-defect reduction of doubled four-dimensional Chern--Simons theory. At a finite simple zero, the inhomogeneous derivative term in the affine gauge transformation induced by the twist function vanishes, so the residue evaluations of the two Gaudin currents transform by the ordinary adjoint action. For each simple ideal, we use the Evans-compatible invariant tensors of the principal Drinfeld--Sokolov hierarchy as external algebraic input, construct local circle integrals, and treat the same-zero, distinct-zero, and mixed sectors separately, proving pairwise Poisson commutativity. Under the explicit assumptions of Stedman's simple-pole/simple-zero boundary Hamiltonian, the periodic trivial-monodromy sector, and boundary weights independent of phase-space variables, the reduced Hamiltonian decomposes term by term into finite-pole, infinity, finite-zero, and residual first-class-constraint contributions, which yields conservation of the constructed charges. We distinguish the finite-defect reduced space, the extended space carrying the residual constraint, and the physical quotient. The result is a conditional existence statement for a classical local Abelian Poisson subalgebra; we make no claim of functional independence, maximality, or Liouville completeness. Extensions to higher-order zeros and nontrivial monodromy sectors are outside the scope of this work.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: A first order nonabelian antisymmetric tensor model with hidden higher symmetry
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We present a nonabelian complex self-dual antisymmetric tensor model, with gauged internal symmetry, comprising a complex multiplet of massless self-dual antisymmetric tensor fields and its conjugate (interacting with massless Yang-Mills gauge fields). We build the model at the classical level, via a first order formulation, assigning local fields to a component expansion over the Dirac algebra and a basis of internal matrices, with Lorentz and gauge invariance ensured by tracing, and applying an appropriate bilinear form. The full expansion requires auxiliary place-holder fields, which are not potentials, but become curvatures (field strengths) after elimination via their algebraic equations of motion. The component expansion over the Dirac algebra is closed under multiplication by additional internal matrices, which are not gauge group generators, but mix internal components, and link auxiliary curvatures with potentials. The model is shown to be invariant under such transformations, and thus possesses a type of hidden internal symmetry. We analyze the specific case of gauge group $SU(2)\! \times \! U(1)$, and as higher symmetry candidates, we consider both the Lie group $SU(3)$ and the Lie superalgebra $SU(2/1)$ (with the additional matrices acting via Lie brackets, or graded Lie brackets, respectively).

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Retarded Green Function For Bopp--Podolsky Electrodynamics in Four-Dimensional De Sitter Spacetime
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study classical Bopp--Podolsky (BP) electrodynamics on four-dimensional de Sitter spacetime, focusing on its transverse retarded Green function and gauge-invariant electromagnetic response. Because de Sitter spacetime is maximally symmetric, its vector Green functions admit a covariant expansion in a finite basis of invariant bitensors, with scalar coefficients depending only on the invariant separation. For conserved sources, the fourth-order field operator factorizes into Maxwell and massive-vector operators, yielding the BP retarded kernel as the difference of their transverse Green functions. Using the invariant bitensor decomposition, we reduce the propagator equations to a hypergeometric master equation and determine the distributional structure of its solution. The common leading short-distance singularity of the Maxwell and massive-vector sectors cancels, leaving a logarithmic master singularity and a softened vector-potential wavefront. After one curl, the gauge-invariant field-strength kernel contains a null-cone delta distribution and a regular timelike tail. The smooth Maxwell master tail is annihilated by the curl, so the interior electromagnetic tail is generated entirely by the massive sector. We also derive an exact horizon-regular static potential, demonstrate the cancellation of the Coulomb divergence, recover the flat-space BP potential, and formulate the generalized Gauss law. On global de Sitter spacetime, the compactness of the spatial sections requires the total charge to vanish; we implement this constraint using an antipodal charge configuration with smooth factorized initial data. The analysis is classical and does not assume a quantum Lee--Wick contour or a preferred de Sitter vacuum.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Genuine Multi-Entropy of Fully Symmetric Gaussian States
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study the tri-partite genuine Rényi multi-entropy of fully symmetric Gaussian states as a function of the squeezing parameter for different total number of bosonic modes under different subsystem configurations. Exact results for a few modes are obtained, and we conjecture an asymptotic formula at the limit of large squeezing parameter as a function of the replica index $n$, while also finding subleading subsystem-size dependent terms for $n=3$ under a specific tripartition. We analytically show that the genuine $n=2$ Rényi multi-entropy of any pure bosonic Gaussian states is zero for any number of modes and for any tripartition. Furthermore, to investigate the dependence on subsystem size, we plot the curve of genuine Rényi multi-entropy as a function of the number of modes in the subsystems while keeping the total number of modes fixed. We discuss differences and similarities between this result and studies of the multi-entropy curve for Haar random states. In particular, we identify a subsystem size configuration related with the multi-entropy time in an evaporating black hole for which the behavior of the genuine multi-entropy changes.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: v2: Updated discussion section and references

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Axionic Casimir Torque
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: In the canonical Casimir effect, the quantum vacuum is isotropic, and the minimization of vacuum energy drives only a linear attractive force between the plates. However, the introduction of an axion gradient breaks this rotational symmetry. It can be demonstrated that these asymmetric zero-point fluctuations exert a macroscopic mechanical twist on the plates proportional to $\vec{b}^2 \sin (2\vartheta)$ where $\vec{b}$ is the spatial axion gradient and $\vartheta$ is the angle between the axion gradient and the normal to the plates.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Kinematic Flow for Banana Loops and Unparticles
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We extend kinematic flow to a class of momentum-integrated loop-level cosmological correlators: banana loops of conformally coupled scalars in power-law cosmologies and, in de Sitter, banana loops containing arbitrary mixtures of massless and conformally coupled scalars. Exploiting their dual description as tree-level exchanges of unparticles, we show that the associated correlators are described by a finite set of master integrals obeying a first-order system of differential equations. The corresponding basis is constructed from tubings of marked graphs and is distinguished by the appearance of nested tubes and an arborescence ordering of the vertices. We derive the connection matrices from four combinatorial rules---activation, merger, swap, and copy. The last two are unique to unparticle exchanges: they induce richer mixing among basis functions and introduce new kinematic letters. Our framework extends systematically to arbitrarily complicated configurations, including necklace diagrams, and establishes unparticle exchange as a distinct class of kinematic flow.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Exact Color Kinematics Duality in the Cosmological Correlators
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: In this paper, we study color kinematics duality and related double-copy and BCJ structures in the cosmological Grassmannian framework. The simplicity of these correlators in this framework makes it possible to test the double copy construction beyond flat space. We show that the four-point gluon correlator admits a representation whose kinematic numerators satisfy an algebraically exact Jacobi identity, $n_s$ + $n_t$ + $n_u$ = 0. Replacing color factors with kinematic numerators gives a graviton correlator that reproduces the correct factorization residues and flat-space limit, which matches with the BCFW result up to terms regular in all exchange channels. In addition, we construct a differential bi-adjoint scalar matrix whose null vector gives rise to a differential BCJ relation among color-ordered gluon correlators. We further explore an s-copy construction for general integer-spin correlators and show that for odd spin the corresponding numerators satisfy a Jacobi identity. Finally, we develop a differential representation for scalar four-point correlators with gluon exchange. These results establish algebraic and differential aspects of graviton and gluon correlators in curved spacetime.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 14 pages main text, no appendix. V2: References added, made changes to abstract and title

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Non-perturbative news from the conformal window
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Dynamical symmetry breaking plays a crucial role in mass and scale generation. In QCD-like theories, its dependence on the number of fermion flavours determines the phase structure and the transition to the conformal regime. In this work, we compute non-perturbative corrections relevant to this phenomenom, including momentum dependencies and field invariants essential for an adequate realisation of the global symmetries, by means of the functional renormalisation group and the generalised flow equation. We find that the critical gauge coupling required for dynamical chiral symmetry breaking acquires a strong dependence on the number of flavours and increases sharply at $N_f^\textrm{crit}\simeq 7.30$ for $N_c=3$. This establishes a new picture of the phase transition to the conformal window that disfavours Miransky/BKT scaling and walking regimes but supports a first-order quantum phase transition and a critical region with exotic dynamics and symmetric fermion mass gaps.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Conformal Renormalisation of 8D Einstein Gravity
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We show that Holographic Renormalisation (HR) in eight dimensions is encoded in the unique conformal gravity theory that admits an Einstein sector with constant negative curvature.
