In contrast to the magnetostatic case, the expanding solution exhibits a propagating shockwave-like front separating regions where the magnetic field has already been formed from those that remain causally disconnected from the source. We show that although the expanding field locally approaches the magnetostatic field behind the shockwave-like front, the associated quantum systems remain distinct at all times. In particular, we obtain manifestly different results for the energy, photon number, and their fluctuations in expanding and magnetostatic field configurations. Our results are first derived for a general external current and then illustrated with a specific example.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Catalan polynomials for the Wishart-Laguerre $β$-ensemble
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: By means of $W$-representation, we investigate the Wishart-Laguerre $β$-ensemble and present a compact expression for Catalan polynomials. For a special Nekrasov partition function associated with the Wishart-Laguerre $β$-ensemble, we show that it can be expressed as a exponential form of the special Catalan polynomials. Furthermore, we make a rule to calculate the Catalan polynomials by means of Feynman diagrams and present another expression for Catalan polynomials. We also establish the connection between certain Catalan polynomials and knot theory.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 15 pages, accepted for publication in Physics Letters B

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Tidal deformability of white dwarfs in Eddington-inspired Born-Infeld gravity
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We compute the static quadrupole Love number $k_2$ and the dimensionless tidal deformability $Λ$ of cold white dwarfs in Eddington-inspired Born-Infeld (EiBI) gravity. Matter couples to the physical metric while perturbation equations are solved in an auxiliary metric, so the physical tidal field near the surface depends on derivatives of the equation of state. This dependence is regular for a surface polytropic index $1<Γ_{\rm env}<3/2$, but not for the $Γ= 5/3$ Chandrasekhar equation of state. The mechanism, an algebraic map between the metric that carries perturbations and the metric that matter feels, is common to Palatini-type theories, so the same type of surface condition should apply to tidal calculations in this wider class. We use thermodynamically consistent envelopes that exactly reach zero enthalpy. At five masses from \(0.6\) to \(1.3\,\Msun\) and five sampled Born-Infeld couplings \(κ\), with $|κ|\le5\times10^6\,\mathrm{m^2}$, the EiBI-GR differences are approximately linear in $κ$. The largest absolute fractional shifts are \(3.89\times 10^{-5}\) in the stellar radius $R$, \(4.09\times 10^{-5}\) in $k_2$, and \(2.36\times 10^{-4}\) in $Λ$. Across nine envelope models, half the spread of each quantity relative to the baseline envelope is at most \(0.0186\) in $R$ and \(0.0857\) in \(k_2\), but only \(3.02\times 10^{-5}\) in \(Λ\) as the changes in \(k_2\) and \(R^5\) largely cancel. A high-precision calculation shows that the envelope dependence of the EiBI-GR difference in \(Λ\) is small. Half the spread of this difference ranges from \(1.067\times 10^{-12}\) to \(6.208\times 10^{-11}\) over the 20 nonzero mass-coupling points.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: A quantum probabilistic approach to the emergence of an inflationary Starobinsky Universe
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We propose that the necessary conditions for the existence of inflation could be explained by a quantum probabilistic approach. We interpret physical states $ψ$ obtained via the path integral formulation as probability density amplitudes for the Universe to be measured at a particular geometric configuration. First, we examine the problem of ordering ambiguities in the Wheeler-DeWitt (WDW) equation. We develop a formalism to handle ambiguities in the canonical quantization of a $1d$ minisuperspace by defining ambiguity functions within the WDW equation. We define a Hilbert space inner product for calculating physical observables, and using an argument from the hermiticity of the Hamiltonian, we obtain an expression for its measure $μ$ in addition to constraints on the ambiguity functions. By defining a new quantum state $Ψ=\sqrtμ ψ$ and using the path integral formalism, we are able to resolve ambiguities and prove the theory is universal. We then generalize for any $M$-dimensional minisuperspace system, for which we can prove universality in the semi-classical approximation for a large class of models. We also show that this universality extends to all orders of quantum theory if the target space manifold of the theory is flat. We calculate probability amplitudes for various cosmological scenarios involving Starobinsky inflation. We summarize the Hartle-Hawking no-boundary proposal for GR and we comment on the distinct possibilities of defining a contour of integration: the sign choice of Hartle-Hawking vs that of Linde-Vilenkin. We make an analogous calculation for $R^{2}$ gravity and find that for the Linde- Vilenkin choice it is statistically more likely for the Universe to emerge in its inflationary stage. Finally, we calculate transition amplitudes when the kinetic energy of the inflaton field $φ$ takes non-zero values.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: PhD thesis defended on 20 January 2026; 4+166 pages

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Numerical Sasaki--Einstein metrics and harmonic forms on del Pezzo links
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We numerically construct the Sasaki--Einstein metric on the link of the cone over the second del Pezzo surface $\mathrm{dP}_2$ and two primitive harmonic basic $(1,1)$-forms at its irregular volume-minimizing Reeb vector. Being toric, the metric in symplectic coordinates is encoded in a single convex function on a polygon. We approximate the correction to the canonical Guillemin potential in two ways: polynomial expansion and neural networks. The polynomial fit achieves a held-out mean-squared Monge--Ampère residual below $10^{-13}$, in contrast to the $10^{-2}$ plateau for the non-volume-minimizing regular Reeb vector. We validate our method against closed-form metrics of $Y^{p,q}$ using curvature invariants, and also against the numerical result of Doran et al. (2007) for the Kähler--Einstein metric of $\mathrm{dP}_3$ using the Laplacian spectrum of low torus-invariant modes. The integrated Riemann-squared curvature of the $\mathrm{dP}_2$ link agrees to two parts in $10^{9}$ with the closed form conjectured from the dual field theory. Our data for the metric and harmonic forms can be used to study warped non-conformal holographic IIB backgrounds, the analogues of the Klebanov--Tseytlin solution on the conifold.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Radion/Dilaton portal freeze-in dark matter in extra-dimensional theories
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We perform a comprehensive analysis of a radion/dilaton portal freeze-in dark matter in models of stabilized warped extra-dimensions. We show that the relic abundance of a generic dark matter particle (scalars, vectors, or fermions) is obtained via the conformal coupling of the radial mode in a consistent model stabilized warped extra- dimensions; our calculations show that in scenarios where the reheating temperature is much smaller than the radion mass, keV-TeV scale dark matter particles can saturate the relic density. We perform a comprehensive analysis of a radion/dilaton portal freeze-in dark matter in models of stabilized warped extra-dimensions. We show that the relic abundance of a generic dark matter particle (scalars, vectors, or fermions) is obtained via the conformal coupling of the radial mode in a consistent model stabilized warped extra- dimensions; our calculations show that in scenarios where the reheating temperature is much smaller than the radion mass, keV-TeV scale dark matter particles can saturate the relic density. Furthermore, we show that the model is subject to Lyman-alpha constraints in the keV-GeV range, providing a unique, model-independent probe of this sector. Our calculations extend previous attempts to calculate the freeze-in relic abundance in extra-dimensional portals by providing a consistent theoretical calculation of matrix elements, clearly laying out the underlying motivation and assumptions and providing a comprehensive account of the cosmological constraints on the model.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Some universalities in the partition functions of low-dimensional gravity models
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: In this work, first, we discuss the connections between various low-dimensional quantum gravity models, including 3d Chern-Simons, 2d Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT), 2d background field (BF) theory, 2d Liouville, 2d Wess-Zumino-Witten (WZW), and 1d Schwarzian, which are related through holography and dimension reduction, and discuss some universalities in their partition functions. Then, we specifically examine the JT partition function and the partition function of $\mathcal{N}=(2,2)$ on $S^2$ and $\text{AdS}_2$ and discuss their similarities and therefore examine our proposed universalities. We change the parameters in each model and based on the change in the structure of the partition functions, strengthen our conjectures. We also use eigenfunctions, spectra and the behaviors of Wheeler-DeWitt wavefunctions to generate more universalities between these low-dimensional quantum gravity models, specifically in their partition functions. Finally, we use entanglement entropy, complexity and RG flows, particularly in the context of wormholes, to find more universalities in quantum gravity models.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 49 pages, 28 figures; several figures added, one section removed, a few points clarified

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Nambu's Dynamics, Strings and Gravitized Quantum Theory
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: In this article we present a new view on string theory that is rooted in quantum foundations extended to the domain of quantum gravity in the form of gravitized quantum theory, in which the canonical probability measure captured by the Born rule of quantum theory, turns out to be dynamical and contextual. We claim that this gravitization of quantum theory is the essence of string theory. String theory, according to this view, originates in foundations of quantum theory and Nambu's dynamics, which features in the non-perturbative definition of string theory in terms of a T-duality covariant and non-commutative formulation, called the metastring. Nambu's dynamics and the associated cubic and hypercubic objects also appear as the natural language for exploring the new observables and phenomena implied by a dynamical Born rule, including triple and higher order quantum interference, that can be investigated in experiments involving massive quantum probes, and that are also needed for direct empirical tests of the Born rule, a cornerstone of quantum theory.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Gauge-invariant nonperturbative Wilson action in quantum electrodynamics II
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The gradient flow exact renormalization group (GFERG) is a formulation of the exact renormalization group for gauge theories that provides a renormalization group flow preserving the gauge Ward--Takahashi identity exactly. In this paper, we nonperturbatively solve the GFERG flow equation for the simplest nontrivial gauge-invariant Wilson action, introduced in a previous paper, for $D$-dimensional quantum electrodynamics with~$N_f$ flavors (for all~$D$, flavors are counted in units of four-component spinors). For $D=3$ and~$D=2$, a nontrivial infrared fixed point exists even for~$N_f=1$, and the structure of the critical exponents at the fixed point is qualitatively the same as that in the large-$N_f$ limit. We also obtain the gauge-field propagator in the continuum limit; for~$D=2$, it reproduces the dynamical mass of the Schwinger model within a few percent. To the best of our knowledge, apart from the large-$N_f$ approximation, this is the first example in which the Wilson renormalization group in a gauge theory is solved nonperturbatively while manifestly preserving gauge symmetry.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Magnetically Charged Black Holes from Grand Unified Theory
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Grand Unified models of particle physics inevitably give rise to magnetic monopoles. Often the model will also contain a weakly broken discrete symmetry that leads to the formation of biased domain walls that survive for a limited period in cosmology. For a range of the discrete symmetry breaking parameter, domain walls can collapse to form magnetically charged extremal black holes lighter than $\simeq 1\, {\rm kg}$ but these are not expected to survive until the present epoch due to Hawking evaporation and Schwinger pair production of monopoles. If the parameter is smaller still, the black holes may be astrophysical, with mass greater than $10^{15}\, {\rm g}$ and with sub-extremal magnetic charge: $Q \simeq 10^8$ (for our canonical choice of parameters). The cosmological energy density in residual magnetic monopoles depends on the discrete symmetry breaking parameter and for sufficiently small values of the parameter, the magnetic monopole density can satisfy all observational constraints.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Linear stability matrix and Lyapunov exponents for stationary spacetime
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Lyapunov exponents characterize the average rate at which nearby trajectories in phase space converge or diverge and therefore provide a useful criterion for dynamical stability. In this work, we develop a general framework for analyzing Lyapunov exponents in stationary spacetimes and extend previous studies beyond circular orbits. For a generic stationary spacetime described by $g_{μν}(r,θ)$, we show that the phase space relevant to linear perturbations is spanned by $(r,p_r,θ,p_θ)$ and the corresponding linear stability matrix has rank four. When the spacetime admits a rank-2 Killing tensor, the linear stability matrix can be reduced to a block-diagonal form, allowing the Lyapunov exponents to be obtained analytically. By imposing the appropriate constraint conditions, the formalism further yields the linear stability matrices and Lyapunov exponents for circular and spherical orbits. The validity of the method is illustrated by several representative examples, including the (inverted) harmonic oscillator, planar Kepler motion, and particle motion in Schwarzschild and Kerr spacetimes. These results provide a unified framework for investigating the stability properties of particle orbits in both classical and relativistic dynamical systems.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Isotensor $πππ$ scattering with a $ρ$ resonant subsystem from QCD
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: This work presents a lattice quantum chromodynamics (QCD) determination of $πππ$ scattering amplitudes for the isospin-2 channel with angular momentum and parity $J^{P} = 1^+$. The calculation is performed using unphysically heavy light-quark masses, corresponding to a pion mass of $m_π \approx 400$~MeV, for which the $ρ$ meson manifests as a narrow resonance. The analysis employs a previously developed formalism that non-perturbatively relates the finite-volume spectra of two- and three-pion systems to their infinite-volume scattering amplitudes. We combine earlier lattice QCD results for $ππ$ systems with isospins 1 and 2 with new determinations of the isospin-2 three-pion finite-volume spectrum, obtained for three cubic, periodic lattice volumes with box lengths ranging from $\approx 4/m_π$ to $6/m_π$. These combined data constrain the low-lying partial waves of the infinite-volume three-pion K matrix, from which we solve a set of coupled integral equations to extract the corresponding scattering amplitudes.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 26 pages, 10 figures; the final version includes revisions to the introduction, outlook, acknowledgments, and references, and is updated to be consistent with the published version in Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 111901 (2026)

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Genus-One Rigidity of Bounded Virasoro Pairings for 3D Gravity
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study whether varying the topological boundary of the doubled Virasoro TQFT can produce distinct torus pairings for an ensemble interpretation of 3D gravity. In the ordinary nondegenerate sector, every bounded pairing that commutes with the modular transformations is scalar, and vacuum normalization selects the diagonal pairing. The proof identifies the modular transformations with the even Weil representation and applies the Cowling--Steger lattice-restriction theorem. Under the ordinary block-diagonal vacuum--continuum ansatz, positivity and the two vacuum marginals also make a Borel-measure pairing bounded, without assuming absolute continuity; modular invariance then forces the same diagonal pairing. These two classes therefore contain no distinct torus pairings to average. A nontrivial Virasoro boundary ensemble must involve genus-one data outside these classes, additional sectors or vacuum--continuum couplings, or information invisible in the torus pairing. Elementary proofs in explicit regular sectors explain the rigidity mechanisms, and numerical calculations provide independent checks.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 48 pages, 3 figures; ancillary code included. v3: revised exposition and organization; results unchanged

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Probing scalar-tensor-induced gravitational waves in the nHz band: NANOGrav and SKA
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) have recently attracted considerable interest, both as a possible explanation for the nanohertz signal reported by the Pulsar Timing Array (PTA) collaboration and for their connection with primordial black hole (PBH) physics. In addition to SIGWs, scalar-tensor-induced gravitational waves (STGWs) have emerged as a promising cosmological source of the stochastic gravitational wave background (SGWB). In this paper, we compute the STGWs generated during a generic matter-dominated (MD) era, as well as during an early matter-dominated (eMD) epoch followed by a sudden transition to the standard radiation-dominated (RD) stage, working in the Poisson gauge. We find that, in a purely MD age, the corresponding energy density rapidly dilutes, whereas in the presence of an eMD phase it remains non-vanishing due to the short duration of the eMD period. We then investigate whether the STGW signal could provide a dominant contribution to the \texttt{NANOGrav 15-year} dataset and we forecast the prospects for its detection with future observations by the Square Kilometre Array (SKA). In particular, we consider STGWs generated during both eMD and RD eras, including their linear-order contributions. We further inject the scalar-induced contribution, both as an additional component and as the only signal, and compare the spectra against the same datasets. Our results show that, although the SIGWs still appear to provide the dominant contribution and the posteriors are tightly constrained by the requirement of avoiding PBH overproduction, the GWs induced by scalar-tensor mixing constitute a viable target for future, more sensitive nano-Hz detectors of the SGWB.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Three Point Amplitudes in Matrix Theory
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We compute the three graviton amplitude in the Banks-Fischler-Shenker-Susskind matrix model for M-theory. Even though the three point amplitude is determined by super Poincare invariance in eleven dimensional M-theory, it requires a non-trivial computation in the matrix model. We consider a configuration where all three gravitons carry non-zero longitudinal momentum. To simplify the problem, we compactify one additional dimension and relate the amplitude to a supersymmetric index computation. We find agreement with the expected answer even at finite values of $N$.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 18 pages plus appendices, 5 figures. v2: typos corrected. v3: computed and matched the overall numerical coefficient. v4: corrected minor typos

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Gram--Wishart--Stiefel formulation of the $N=2$, large--$d$ gauge theory in 1D: towards emergent Grassmannian geometry
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary:
We develop the Gram/Wishart/Stiefel formulation of the \(N=2\), large--\(d\) planar endpoint theory of lattice BFSS/BMN matrix quantum mechanics on the lattice. The endpoint variables become rank--two Wishart eigenvalues and relative Stiefel angles, expressing the holonomy invariants \(A\), \(B\), and \(R^2=A^2+B^2\) in radial and angular Gram data. The large-\(R\) aligned contribution \(-A\) is absorbed into the Gaussian sector, producing the shifted mass \((α_Λ)_{\rm eff}=α_Λ-1/2\). The exact \(O(2)\) angular integral encodes this sector in a rank--two Bessel kernel. The pure \(-A\) theory, exactly solvable in Cartesian variables, fixes the leading Bessel/HCIZ structure: its exponential selects alignment, while its prefactor removes the spurious doubled Wishart entropy.
  We then apply this structure to the transverse \(B\)-type expansion and its non-polynomial toy completion. Finite polynomial truncations lead to an apparent large--\(d\) perturbativity bound incompatible with the continuum limit, but this bound is shown to be an artifact of truncation. After summing the local transverse completion and balancing the compensating \(+A\) term, the Wishart saddle is recovered with the physical shifted mass. The resulting continuum behavior reproduces the universal \(-2d\) contribution of the \(D_Λ\)-channel, while the genuinely anisotropic \(β_Λ\)-channel lies outside the scope of a pure transverse \(B\)-type description.
  Finally, we outline the emergent Grassmannian geometry encoded by the two endpoint planes. Their relative angular fluctuations form a \(2(d-2)\)-dimensional sector, whose entropy interpretation is developed in the sequel. For \(d\ge4\), the two planes generically span a relational four-dimensional subspace of \(\mathbb R^d\).
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: Version 2: Substantially reorganized and shortened, with lengthy technical derivations referred to arXiv v1. An added outlook on emergent Grassmannian geometry clarifies the physical significance of the Gram/Wishart/Stiefel formulation beyond its BFSS/BMN origins. This directly addresses concerns regarding physical content while emphasizing the GWS formulation intrinsic significance

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Entropic force in matrix
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We consider the entropic force in matrix theory. We find the gravity in bulk can be emergent from the entropic force.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Quantum-Corrected and Hairy Black Holes via Analogue Gravity
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: This thesis maps two exotic black-hole geometries onto the transonic flow of a de Laval nozzle and reads their perturbative response in aerodynamic variables. The first is the hairy black hole of gravitational decoupling, constrained by the dominant energy condition and by the existence of a horizon. The second is the Calmet-Kuipers metric, short-ranged and governed by the single Wilson coefficient of the dimension-six operator that the two-loop Goroff-Sagnotti divergence identifies. Perturbations of spin 0, 1/2, 1 and 2 reduce to a Schrödinger-type wave equation, whose spectrum the Mashhoon method returns as a whole overtone tower in closed form, every frequency damped. The two corrections are distinguished by which channel responds and by how strongly all of them do, the quantum coupling moving the quality factor by up to 37% in the scalar and Dirac channels and by about 10% in the other two, while the hair acts on every channel alike. Identifying the two tortoise coordinates turns the equality of the potentials into a Sturm-Liouville problem, so that the prescribed barrier fixes the wall profile and with it the flow variables and the thrust coefficient. The hair is felt across the whole divergent section, whereas the quantum correction registers only near the throat and grows as the inverse fourth power of the mass, which confines it to primordial black holes. The analogy is kinematical, so the duct reproduces the scattering of perturbations off these geometries without reproducing the field equations behind them.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: Defended PhD thesis, 202 pp., also contains parts of our published works arXiv:2402.04682 [gr-qc], arXiv:2506.10847 [gr-qc]

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Local supersymmetry implies momentum map/Gauntlett-Pakis equations and vanishing generalized Komar forms
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The first-order differential equations satisfied by Killing spinor bilinears (momentum map equations or Gauntlett--Pakis equations, Killing vector equations and the vanishing of the generalized Komar charge of the supersymmetric Killing vector) can be derived directly from the action of the local supersymmetry algebra on bosonic fields. We show how this comes about in several examples of increasing complexity, one of which is 11-dimensional supergravity.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Casimir Sign Reversal from Finite-Range Bogoliubov Fluctuations
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study the zero-temperature Casimir effect of a three-dimensional Bose fluid with finite-range corrections to its Bogoliubov spectrum. Beyond the universal acoustic contribution scaling as $L^{-3}$, the long-distance expansion contains a nonuniversal $L^{-5}$ correction that can compete with the phononic term. We derive this crossover analytically within a minimal isotropic finite-range model and test the asymptotic result against the full dispersion. A regulator-independent Poisson-resummed calculation confirms that sign reversals of the Casimir energy are possible, while showing that the apparent low-coupling zero inferred by balancing only the $L^{-3}$ and $L^{-5}$ terms is not quantitatively controlled. Robust sign changes instead occur in the stable regime close to roton softening, where the Casimir energy acquires an oscillatory finite-momentum contribution. Strongly dipolar atomic gases provide a natural motivation for microscopic interaction lengths in the nanometric regime. We further discuss how the resulting nonlinear force law could be probed through the frequency response of a driven nanomechanical resonator.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Beyond the polynomial ansatz: regular $AdS_3\times M_8$ solutions of M-theory
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study regular compact solutions of the cohomogeneity-one $AdS_3\times M_8$ system of Gauntlett, Mac Conamhna, Mateos and Waldram, where $M_8$ is an $S^2$ bundle over three constant-curvature Riemann surfaces. We find that an endpoint argument rules out every non-flat curvature-sign sector without a positive-curvature factor, while an analytic deformation gives regular families with four radial shape parameters in all remaining sectors, with the base geometry held fixed. The known polynomial solutions form a proper analytic locus in these families. Non-polynomiality is therefore generic in parameter space, although the deviation from an endpoint-matching polynomial can be very small. Apart from the completely flat exception, the curvature-sign criterion is necessary and sufficient within this ansatz. Four magnetic flux ratios give local coordinates near the reference solution and its small-curvature deformations, and a rational inverse reconstructs candidate endpoint data directly from finite flux ratios. In the fully positive sector we prove that one explicit four-dimensional finite-ratio neighbourhood lies inside the physical flux image. The magnetic periods and leading holographic central charge reduce to endpoint data, and, once the common Brown--Henneaux normalization is fixed, the nontrivial flux dependence of the equivariant localization formula agrees with the endpoint result as an exact algebraic identity. We also quantify the non-polynomial corrections and analyse finite degenerations under explicit convergence hypotheses.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Exact AdS and pp-waves in multi-gravity beyond pairwise interactions
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We construct exact anti-de Sitter (AdS) waves and pp-waves in ghost-free multi-gravity beyond pairwise interactions for an arbitrary number $\mathcal{N}$ of vielbeins, in any spacetime dimension $D\geq3$. Deforming proportional AdS and Minkowski solutions along a common null direction reduces the full nonlinear field equations to coupled linear differential equations for the wave profiles, without restricting their amplitudes. The system is diagonalised in the same eigenbasis as the perturbative Fierz-Pauli mass matrix, separating the solutions into one massless and $\mathcal{N}-1$ massive eigenprofiles. We obtain explicit radial and transverse solutions and impose an AdS boundary falloff. This falloff admits the appropriate radial branch of every mode with non-negative squared mass and excludes profiles with negative squared masses, including logarithmic solutions at the Breitenlohner-Freedman threshold. We also relate the AdS waves to pp-waves through a local flat limit. Explicit examples exhibit wave configurations that cannot be reproduced by ghost-free pairwise theories, demonstrating that genuine multi-field interactions support new exact gravitational-wave solutions.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: The three- and four-loop equal-mass sunset integrals and local Calabi--Yau fourfolds and fivefolds
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We determine the equal-mass two-dimensional three- and four-loop sunset Feynman integrals $I^{(3)}_\circleddash$ and $I^{(4)}_\circleddash$ at large Euclidean momentum in terms of the genus-zero Gromov--Witten theory of the local Calabi--Yau fourfold and fivefold $X_L=\operatorname{Tot}(K_{F_L})$, where $F_L\subset(\mathbb P^1)^{L+1}$, $L=3,4$, is a smooth hypersurface of multidegree $(1,\ldots,1)$. At two loops the sunset integral is governed by the prepotential of a local Calabi--Yau threefold. For $L\geq3$ the moduli spaces of unmarked stable maps have positive virtual dimension and there is no prepotential, therefore the Feynman integral is governed instead by the one-point potential $\mathcal F_{γ_L}$ with insertion $γ_L=H^{L-1}/(L-1)!$, by its gravitational descendants, and by $ζ(3)$ boundary terms coming from the Gamma class. At both loop orders the coefficient of $R^{L-1}$ in the Frobenius expansion in the mirror coordinate $R$ is $-θ_Q\mathcal F_{γ_L}$ with the Novikov variable $Q=\exp(R)$. At three loops the whole Feynman integral is an explicit expression in $\mathcal F_{γ_3}$ alone, because genus-zero recursion determines all descendant series from it; at four loops two diagonal series suffice, and the $ζ(3)$ term is itself corrected by $θ_Q\mathcal F_{γ_4}$. At three loops we also derive the analytic normalization independently, from the Picard--Fuchs equation and the polar part of a Mellin transform, prove integrality of the multiple-cover transforms for arbitrary integral insertions together with an explicit quantum-$K$ formula, and compute the exact period connection polynomials. Finally we give endpoint values along the Euclidean axis, bounds on the Taylor radii in the Novikov variable $Q$, a computer-assisted proof of the four-loop endpoint nonanalyticity, and a comparison of the normalizations at two, three and four loops.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 70 pages. v2: corrected cross reference to the companion paper [arXiv:2610.10828]; stylistic improvements to the text. Source code: https://github.com/pierrevanhove/Sunset-Gromov-Witten, archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23361560

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: All three-loop four-point massless integrals with one off-shell leg
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We present the complete set of massless three-loop four-point master integrals with one off-shell external leg. These are essential building blocks for the three-loop virtual corrections to Higgs-boson or vector-boson production in association with a jet at the Large Hadron Collider, required for next-to-next-to-next-to-leading-order QCD predictions. We construct a complete basis of canonical integrals by identifying integrands with simple poles and unit leading singularities, solely by integrand analysis. This includes an integral family with 371 master integrals and a 19-dimensional top sector. The solutions for all relevant integrals are provided as a map to a minimal set of iterated integrals graded according to their analytic properties, together with high-precision series expansions.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 41 pages, 9 figures. Electronic files with results are available under https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23376162

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Equal-mass sunset integrals and genus-zero local Gromov--Witten theory of Calabi--Yau $n$-folds
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary:
We prove an exact identity, as convergent logarithmic germs at large Euclidean momentum, between the equal-mass two-dimensional $(n-1)$-loop sunset Feynman integral, with $n\geq4$, and the genus-zero one-point descendant invariants of the local Calabi--Yau $n$-fold $X_n=\operatorname{Tot}(K_{F_n})$, where $F_n\subset(\mathbb P^1)^{n}$ is a smooth $(1,\ldots,1)$ hypersurface. Writing $s$ for the momentum variable and $y=-1/s$, the identity reads \[
  I^{(n-1)}_{\circleddash}(s)=(-1)^{n-1}yA\,\Bigl[nR^{n-1}-θ_Q{\mathcal D}_0^Δ\,R^{n-2} +\sum_{j=0}^{n-3}c_jR^j\Bigr], \] where $R=\log y+O(y)$ is the local mirror coordinate, $A=θ_yR$, $Q=e^R$, ${\mathcal D}_0^Δ(Q)$ is the primary one-point potential, and each $c_j$ has the form \[ c_j=c_j^{(0)}+\sum_{a=0}^{n-2}\bigl(c_{j,a}\,{\mathcal D}_a^Δ(Q) +c'_{j,a}\,θ_Q{\mathcal D}_a^Δ(Q)\bigr) \] with the coefficients in $\mathbb Q[ζ(3),ζ(5),\ldots]$ the odd zeta values coming from the Gamma class. The descendant series ${\mathcal D}_a^Δ(Q)$ are given explicitly by the ambient hypergeometric series and the inverse mirror map. We also prove global univalence of the principal mirror map, with explicit upper and lower bounds on the $Q$-Taylor radii, extract the full primary evaluation divisor and its integral cover transform, and reduce the ambient endpoint constants to a finite universal Gamma-class part and $\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor$ real parameters.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 88 pages. v2: updated reference to the companion paper [arXiv:2610.10821]; stylistic improvements to the text and abstract. Source code: https://github.com/pierrevanhove/Sunset-Gromov-Witten, archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23361560

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Generalised entanglement wedges in three dimensions
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Generalized entanglement wedges (GWs), proposed by Bousso and Penington for gravitating regions in general spacetimes, share many properties of ordinary entanglement wedges, including nesting, monotonicity and strong subadditivity of their generalized entropies. In AdS/CFT, the corresponding properties of entanglement wedges are consequences of the structure of the dual CFT. In this paper we ask whether the properties of GWs have a similar origin. We explore this question in vacuum AdS$_3$ at leading order in $G$. We first show that every GW on a static slice is a union of geodesically convex regions. Each such region is an intersection of ordinary entanglement wedges, so every GW is built from unions and intersections of entanglement wedges. We then use the Crofton formula of integral geometry to write the perimeter of a convex region as the measure of the set of geodesics that intersect it. In AdS$_3$ every geodesic is the Ryu--Takayanagi surface of a boundary interval, so this measure can be written in terms of the von Neumann entropies of CFT intervals. Strong subadditivity of the CFT entropy guarantees that the measure is positive. Monotonicity and strong subadditivity of GWs then follow from simple inequalities between sets of geodesics. The strong subadditivity of GWs is therefore a direct consequence of strong subadditivity on the boundary. Our results further suggest that GWs correspond to subsystems of the CFT that are more general than boundary subregions.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Collective Organization of String Fragmentation
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: How coherent confining strings reorganize into hadronic matter is a central open problem in nonequilibrium gauge dynamics. Using real-time tensor-network simulations of the massive Schwinger model, we identify a collective organization underlying string fragmentation. For intermediate masses, the dynamics simplifies and more than $99\%$ of the temporal evolution of the electric-field probability distribution is governed by a single collective mode whose decay tracks the survival probability of the parent string. The extracted survival law exhibits the same Gaussian dependence implied by the Lund world-sheet area law, providing microscopic support for its characteristic area law dependence without assuming the Lund fragmentation mechanism. The same mode controls the transition from the coherent string to the produced mesons, explains the universal non-thermal effective fluid equation of state, and essentially controls the growth of bipartite entanglement through the causal propagation of massive pairs. These results identify collective fragmentation as an organizing principle of coherent string breaking and provide a microscopic perspective on the dynamical origin of a central ingredient of Lund hadronization.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: ACT stands for Awkward Cosmology Theories
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Recent Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) observations, combined with Planck, favor a scalar spectral index in tension with Starobinsky inflation. Two main strategies have been proposed to reconcile Starobinsky inflation with these data: (i) including higher-curvature operators in the gravitational action, and (ii) modifying the post-inflationary reheating dynamics. We critically re-examine both approaches. When higher-curvature corrections are included, dimensional-analysis arguments allow introducing a second mass scale suppressing higher-dimensional operators, resulting in a one-coupling, two-scale effective theory. We show that fitting the ACT data drives this class of effective theories toward a regime of stronger sensitivity to UV physics, potentially implying fine-tuning of the inflationary observables. We illustrate our general point with two concrete models, namely no-scale supergravity and metric-affine gravity, showing that they provide different realizations of the same underlying $f(R)$ theory. On the reheating side, requiring the CMB modes to re-enter the horizon before recombination leads to stringent constraints on the reheating equation of state, and fitting the ACT data favors an exotic reheating phase with $ω_{\rm reh} > 1/3$, incompatible with inflaton oscillations about the minimum of the standard Starobinsky potential. Finally, we explore the possibility that a phase of cosmological stasis, driven by a tower of decaying massive states, could play the role of the post-inflationary epoch. We find that accommodating ACT-preferred $n_s$ in this setup requires a tower of states with negative energy density. Taken together, our results suggest that reconciling Starobinsky inflation with the ACT data demands ingredients that are challenging to motivate from the perspective of UV-complete theories, undermining the minimality of the original Starobinsky model.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 38 pages, 9 figures. v2: matches version accepted in PRD

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Infinite magic and the emergence of the continuum
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Which features of a quantum state are needed for a relativistic quantum field theory to emerge from a lattice system? We address this question by establishing a quantitative relationship between the type classification of hyperfinite von Neumann algebras and the quantum-information-theoretic resource of nonstabilizerness, also called magic. Our results establish two complementary parts of this relationship. First, we prove that any stabilizer system on a lattice defines a canonical GNS Hilbert space in which local von Neumann algebras do not contain type III factors in their central decomposition. As an explicit example, we prove that for stabilizer systems with short-range order, the local algebras are isomorphic to tensor products of hyperfinite factors of type I or type II. This demonstrates that the absence of magic is accompanied by the absence of type III factors in the local algebras, therefore prohibiting the appearance of a quantum field theory. Second, for the hyperfinite factors of Araki, Woods and Powers, we prove a quantitative equivalence: The limiting factor is of type III if and only if the locally optimized min-relative entropy of magic diverges. This divergence is necessary to generate the continuous spectrum associated to a type III factor. Thus, in this setting, the emergence of a type III factor requires not merely the presence of magic, but an infinite amount of it. These results provide a rigorous setting supporting the proposal that infinite magic is a necessary structural ingredient for the emergence of a relativistic continuum from lattice systems.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: All Order Gravitational Wave Tails for Subleading Post-Newtonian Expansion
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The low-frequency gravitational waveform emitted in a classical scattering process contains an infinite tower of late- and early-time tail terms of the form $u^{-r}(\ln|u|)^{r-1}$, $r \geq 1$. In the Newtonian limit, the coefficients of this entire tower have recently been shown to be universal, i.e. fixed by the asymptotic data of the scattering objects alone. At the retained order in the velocity expansion, these leading-logarithmic tails are determined to all orders in Newton's constant $G$. We extend this result to the first subleading order in the post-Newtonian expansion of the asymptotic states. We consider scattering of an arbitrary number of incoming and outgoing nonrelativistic objects interacting only through gravity at long range, and we derive the complete tower of tail terms at this order. The correction arises from the first subleading term in the retardation expansion and is determined by the asymptotic Newtonian trajectories of the massive particles. Its coefficients are again determined entirely by the asymptotic trajectories and are independent of the details of the interaction. For $2\to2$ scattering, the leading-logarithmic series can be summed in closed form. Our results agree with a relativistic conjecture proposed in earlier work arXiv:2610.07134.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: The Magic Barrier: A Universal Feature of Quantum Thermalization
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We show that the emergence of a ``magic barrier'', characterized by a transient maximum of nonstabilizerness during rapid entanglement growth, is a universal feature of thermalization within quantum ergodic theories, which is intimately connected to random matrix spectral properties. Starting from a pure product state, we analytically determine the time evolution of entanglement entropy, antiflatness, capacity of entanglement, and nonlocal trace distance magic under unitary dynamics generated by random matrix Hamiltonians drawn from all three Gaussian ensembles. We find that the transient maxima of antiflatness, capacity of entanglement, and nonlocal magic occur on the same characteristic timescale as the maximum rate of entanglement growth. These results establish that the magic barrier is a universal feature of RMT thermalization, suggesting universality across quantum chaotic systems. We conclude that quantitative simulations of thermalization in ergodic quantum theories inherently require quantum computation.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Spread Complexity for Local Operator Quenches with Conserved Momentum
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study a family of locally excited states in two-dimensional conformal field theories in different setups, defined on the plane, on the cylinder, or at finite temperature. These states are constructed by assigning independent chiral and anti-chiral regulators to a local primary operator, leading to excitations carrying net momentum. We analytically calculate the first few Lanczos coefficients and the early time behaviour of the spread complexity associated with these states. Then, using numerical methods, we obtain the coefficients reaching larger Krylov indices and find the associated spread complexity for a longer range of time evolution. We also compare the rate of change of the resulting spread complexity with the proposed holographic dual quantity, related to the proper momentum of an infalling particle in the dual bulk, but we observe a mismatch.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 39 pages, 8 figures. Typos fixed, references added

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Orientation-Dependent Casimir Energy and Generalized Torque in Lorentz-Violating Rectangular Compactifications
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We derive the renormalized Casimir energy of a free massive real scalar field on the rectangular compactification \(\mathbb{R}^{1,r}\times T^p\) in the presence of a constant CPT-even aether-like Lorentz-violating background. Allowing the spatial part of the background vector to have an arbitrary orientation relative to the compactification lattice, we characterize the resulting orientation-dependent geometric response of the vacuum. Integrating out the noncompact momenta reduces the effective spatial kinetic matrix to its Schur complement, and Poisson resummation yields a closed, exponentially convergent Bessel-function lattice sum within the stability domain. The resulting expression separates an orientation-independent kinetic normalization, \([1+λu_μu^μ]^{-1/2}\), from an orientation-dependent deformation of the image-lattice metric. Coordinate-aligned configurations are recovered as special cases, and the exact massless limit and the compact-direction pressures are obtained. For a two-dimensional compact subspace, we explicitly analyze the angular dependence of the vacuum energy and derive the associated generalized Casimir torque. These results establish how the relative orientation between a Lorentz-violating background and an anisotropic compactification lattice enters the renormalized vacuum energy and its directional response.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: 6d SCFTs and terminal singularities
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The classification of 6d $\mathcal{N}=(1,0)$ SCFTs has been carried out with great success, enumerating consistent elliptically fibered threefolds in F-theory. In this note, we observe that the E-string 6d SCFT can be decorated with extra matter sectors. This decoration exploits an opening allowed by the current classification, implementing terminal singularities nested on the curve of the base of the elliptic fibration that supplies the tensor branch. Additionally, via dimensional reduction on a circle, we identify versions of the 5d $E_n$ theories decorated by extra matter sectors. As a bonus, the end of the resulting RG flow cascade reproduces a 5d theory recently constructed in the literature, explaining its 6d origin. We remain agnostic as to whether the decorated 6d and 5d theories constitute novel SCFTs.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: All-temperature superfluidity in two dimensions
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: In local theories with short-range interactions, continuous symmetries cannot be spontaneously broken in two spatial dimensions at nonzero temperature. $\mathrm{U}(1)$-symmetric models instead admit a Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless (BKT) phase with quasi-long-range order and nonzero phase stiffness, which is normally destroyed at high temperatures by vortex proliferation. Here, we show that a BKT phase, and with it superfluidity, can persist to arbitrarily high temperatures. Using the large-$N$ expansion, we study a $(2+1)$-dimensional quantum field theory in which a complex scalar is coupled to the critical $\mathrm{O}(N)$ model. At the biconical fixed point, where the inter-sector coupling is negative, the thermal effective potential has a circle of minima with nonzero $\mathrm{U}(1)$ amplitude. Integrating out the gapped fluctuations yields an effective theory for the compact phase mode at distances large compared to $1/T$. Since temperature is the only scale at the fixed point, the phase stiffness grows linearly with temperature, with a proportionality factor that scales linearly with $N$ and is fixed entirely by the fixed point. This renders vortex operators irrelevant for sufficiently large $N$. We further show that the vortex fugacity is exponentially small in $N$.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Gluon Scattering in Expanding de Sitter Universe
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We construct an observer-centric S-matrix in the expanding Poincaré patch of four-dimensional de Sitter space. The asymptotic states are defined along the worldline of a comoving, or eternal, observer, the only kind of geodesic observer that remains in the patch for all proper time, and the free Hamiltonian is the conserved charge generating translations in her proper time. The resulting S-matrix is independent of which eternal observer is chosen. We apply the construction to pure Yang--Mills theory in Coulomb gauge and compute the three- and four-gluon amplitudes at tree level. The amplitudes have a structure similar to the cosmological correlators of gauge currents and are constrained by the Ward identities of de Sitter isometries.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Towards ultrarelativistic scattering near the light ring: asymptotic divergence of gravitational-wave fluxes
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Near the threshold between scattering and capture by a Schwarzschild black hole, a particle spends a long time close to an unstable circular orbit, which in the ultrarelativistic limit approaches the light ring. Here we study the behavior of the gravitational wave fluxes emitted by such an ultrarelativistic particle at first order in the mass ratio. The fluxes radiated to infinity and absorbed by the horizon diverge as the inverse distance from the light ring multiplied by its logarithm. Using the Wentzel, Kramers, and Brillouin (WKB) approximation to solve the Regge-Wheeler equation and treating the infinite harmonic sum analytically, we derive an exact expression for the coefficient of this logarithmic enhancement and show that it is identical for both fluxes. We then estimate the coefficients of the subleading pole contributions by combining numerical calculations at low multipoles with the exact asymptotics at large multipoles. We further conjecture an extension to equatorial circular orbits in Kerr. Interestingly, our results also inform the analytical structure of the energy and angular momentum losses of ultrarelativistic scattering orbits near the light ring. More broadly, our work illustrates how WKB methods can provide the asymptotic behavior of self-force observables in regimes where numerical mode sums become increasingly challenging.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Region bounds, error margins and certified positivity in the numerical conformal bootstrap; Or the first mathematically rigorous bounds on the 3d Ising CFT critical exponents
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Numerical conformal bootstrap bounds are commonly called rigorous, yet as published they are not theorems: they hold at sampled points rather than on regions of parameter space, for truncated rational approximations of the conformal blocks, for a finite list of spins, and up to floating-point rounding. We close all four gaps. We show how to search efficiently for functionals positive on regions, including external-dimension space; how positivity on the large-spin crossing vectors can be imposed as such a region constraint; how new analytic bounds on the conformal-block recursion relations give functionals positive on the true, untruncated crossing vectors; and how to certify the positivity of these functionals in exact arithmetic. The certification rests on Bernstein-basis positivity certificates in up to three variables, exact arithmetic in $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt2)$, a compactified treatment of the infinite spin tail, and an explicit bound on the difference between the true blocks and their truncations, so that infinitely many positivity conditions reduce to finitely many machine-checked sign conditions. As a flagship application we certify an exclusion region in the $(Δ_σ,Δ_ε)$ plane: for $Δ_σ\in[0.505,0.5405]$ all of $Δ_ε\in(1/2,3]$ is excluded except a small rectangle containing the 3d Ising island, giving rigorous two-sided bounds on the critical exponents $η$ and $ν$ under explicitly stated spectrum assumptions. The analytic inputs for the mixed $σ$-$ε$ system, which would remove the spin-2 gap assumption, are also proved. The same methods prevent common practical failure modes and can make bootstrap searches faster: region bounds turn the mapping of an island into a handful of one-dimensional bisections. The essential code to reproduce the search and the certification, and all machine-checkable certificates, are released.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 105 pages, 5 figures, 6 tables. Certificates, checkers and search code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21708207 (latest version at https://zenodo.org/records/21708207/latest)

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Quantum critical collapse in the large $D$ limit
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: In analytically tractable models of Einstein-scalar critical collapse, it has been shown that the quantum self-energy of the collapsing matter in the dominant $s$-wave sector grows with Lyapunov exponent $D-2$, eventually competing with the classical instability that controls black hole formation. This competition shifts the naked singularity threshold and produces a finite mass gap within semiclassical control, yet that control may appear threatened as the spacetime dimension $D\to\infty$. We study this quantum growing mode in both continuously (CSS) and discretely (DSS) self-similar critical spacetimes at large $D$ and establish that the universal Lyapunov exponent survives both forms of self-similarity. In CSS, the classical approach to a naked singularity is interrupted by the appearance of trapped surfaces. At large $D$, the horizon tracing reduces to a Bessel problem, yielding a quantum wall whose radius obeys $r_h\propto(D-2)^{-2}$. This radius can remain above the Planck scale at finite $D$, although maintaining this hierarchy becomes increasingly demanding as $D$ grows. In DSS, the same growth is modulated by echoing and can retain memory of previous echoes. The simplest anomaly-induced action exhibits accumulating memory but is singular at the spherical center. We construct a covariant one-loop action whose stress tensor remains smooth throughout the DSS domain and organize it into an echo-periodic structure without memory. This suggests that the smooth vacuum polarization of the genuine four-dimensional DSS Choptuik spacetime may similarly be governed by its exact echoing symmetry.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Efficient numerical evolution of self-gravitating systems with dark-matter-baryon scattering
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We present a fast algorithm to numerically evolve a spherically symmetric system consisting of dark matter and gas, including dark-matter-baryon scattering. The method augments the spherical N-body code NSphere, which collapses the six-dimensional phase space of a spherical collisionless system to three dimensions, with a one-dimensional Lagrangian treatment of gas. Dark-matter-baryon scattering is implemented as a Monte-Carlo process between the dark-matter numerical particles and the gas shells. We also implement an algorithm for radiative gas cooling that is valid for weak cooling. The gas, as well as dark-matter-baryon scattering and cooling, adds only incrementally to the run time of the code, allowing systems to be evolved on a laptop computer, a tiny fraction of the computational resources required for a full 3D N-body/hydro simulation. To illustrate, we show the evolution of a $\sim 10^{13}\,M_\odot$ halo with a dark-matter-baryon scattering cross section $σ_{\rm tot}/m_χ=0.1\,{\rm cm}^2\,{\rm g}^{-1}$ but no gas cooling. We then show examples with radiative gas cooling where the cooling is altered through interaction with dark-matter particles. The resulting code, NSphere-IDM, allows the implications of dark-matter interactions for galaxy evolution to be explored quickly over large volumes of the dark-matter parameter space, and other new physics (e.g., dark-matter self-interactions or anisotropy in the distribution function) is easily incorporated. The code can also provide useful calibrations and benchmarks for fully 3D N-body or hydrodynamical simulations.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 13 pages, 3 figures, NSphere-IDM code available on GitHub at https://github.com/NSphere-IDM/NSphere-IDM

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Worldsheet string theory on $\mathrm{AdS}_3 \times \mathbf{S}^3 \times \mathrm{K3}$
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The RNS formalism describing string theory on $\mathrm{AdS}_3 \times \mathbf{S}^3 \times \mathrm{K3}$ supported by pure NS-NS flux is in principle straightforward to write down. One can directly check that the worldsheet theory reproduces the correct chiral spectrum expected from supergravity by analyzing the BRST cohomology. However, when one attempts to construct the worldsheet partition function using the standard rules of the RNS formalism by appropriately summing over spin structures to ensure worldsheet modular invariance, one finds a result in tension with spacetime supersymmetry. We explain why this is the case and, more importantly, propose a resolution. Specifically, we fix the physical state projection for the partition function uniquely by requiring spacetime supersymmetry. Perhaps surprisingly, the projected worldsheet partition function does not factorize into a bosonic and a fermionic part and involves functions that are not modular covariant. As a consistency check, we show that our prescription for the worldsheet partition function reproduces the supergravity spectrum for both Type IIB and IIA theories. Furthermore, we compute the elliptic genus of the dual CFT from the worldsheet, which has both a holomorphic short string and a non-holomorphic long string contribution. The latter displays characteristics of a mock modular function, albeit with some key differences, while the former has the tantalizing structure of a symmetric orbifold. We also point out the worldsheet construction of a non-supersymmetric theory, whose spectrum is free of tachyons.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Finite-cutoff geometry from double-scaled SYK
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We develop a finite-cutoff holographic description of the double-scaled SYK (DSSYK) model. We construct microscopic deformations of Kourkoulou-Maldacena and thermofield-double SYK states whose double-scaling limits reproduce a lower-dimensional analogue of $\text{T}\overline{\text{T}}$ and $\text{T}\overline{\text{T}}+Λ_2$ deformations, which we denote $T^2$ and $T^2+Λ_1$, respectively. The ensemble-averaged theory describes wormhole states in finite-cutoff sine dilaton gravity, and finite-cutoff anti-de Sitter and de Sitter geometries in the low- and high-energy regimes, respectively. The analysis includes both perturbative and non-perturbative solutions to the energy spectrum flow equation, and the regions behind and beyond the respective horizons. Only the perturbative branch admits physical quantum states. We study how to incorporate end-of-the-world (ETW) branes in the finite cutoff holographic dictionary. The ETW brane leads to an additional boundary theory deformation, which leads to black hole or eternal traversable wormhole geometries depending on the existence of normalizable bound states. We extend the finite cutoff length evaluations for constant mean curvature (CMC) slices, and interpret them as complexity in the boundary theory. We discuss possible extensions with matter. Our results provide a microscopic framework for studying the finite-cutoff boundaries, CMC slices and branes in the holographic dictionary of DSSYK.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: An SYK wormhole under the microscope
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary:
We derive a large-N wormhole saddle in the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model for the variance of the thermal one-point function of a heavy operator across realizations of the microscopic couplings. We propose that this saddle describes a double trumpet geometry. In the double-scaling limit, we express the wormhole as a transition amplitude in an emergent bulk Hilbert space of chords connecting the two boundaries. In the Schwarzian limit, the chords proliferate and the wormhole defines a quantum transition amplitude in the open-universe Hilbert space of Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT) gravity. Comparing the SYK wormhole amplitude with its counterpart in JT gravity coupled to matter provides a direct test of the heavy-operator randomness hypothesis in SYK.
  The microscopic SYK couplings specify the α-parameters of the wormhole. For a fixed realization of the couplings, we compute the observable in the corresponding α-state. We provide the bulk wavefunction of the associated half-wormhole, which exhibits erratic correlations in the length basis that do not self-average. We extend the bulk description to the Hilbert space of a closed universe. We point out that the correlation chords from which the wormhole geometry emerges structurally resemble local observer worldlines.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Quantum Gravity in the Landau background gauge
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We examine, in the Landau background gauge, the effective action of a quantum theory of gravitational and matter fields. We analyse the BRST invariance of this theory and study the Ward identities which implement the symmetry of the background effective action. The off-shell and on-shell counterterm Lagrangians are explicitly calculated in this gauge at one-loop order. We argue that the matter self-energy in the Landau background gauge, which is finite to this order, may be finite also at higher loops.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 15 pages, 4 figures, accepted in Physics Review D

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Constraining the Progenitor Orbits of Sequential Black-Hole Mergers in Hierarchical Triples: Peters-Based Estimates
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Two black-hole merger events may originate from sequential mergers in a pre-existing hierarchical black-hole triple if their spatial localizations overlap and the remnant mass of the first merger is compatible with a component mass of the second. In this scenario, the inner binary merges first, leaving a remnant that remains bound to the tertiary and subsequently undergoes a second merger. We present a method to constrain the progenitor triple's outer orbit by modeling the gravitational-wave-driven evolution of the remnant-tertiary binary using Peters' equations. Given an assumed upper bound on the recoil velocity of the first merger, the method requires only the black-hole masses, the time delay between the mergers, and the eccentricity at a reference frequency - quantities that can be inferred from the merger events themselves. We investigate the potential constraining power by constructing a constraint atlas spanning a range of system properties and identify the conditions under which the method places tight and reliable bounds on the progenitor triple's outer orbital parameters. By imposing an upper bound on the detector-band eccentricity, we also obtain meaningful constraints for candidate hierarchical mergers proposed in the literature, including GW190514-GW190521. We provide numerical tools for applying the method to user-specified systems and evaluating the reliability of the resulting Peters-based constraints. This framework offers a computationally inexpensive first step toward reconstructing hierarchical-merger progenitors and provides a foundation for extensions incorporating more sophisticated relativistic treatments.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Post-Newtonian theory in de Sitter and anti-de Sitter spacetimes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We develop the post-Newtonian framework for the near-zone dynamics of a binary in de Sitter and anti-de Sitter spacetime. We consider a binary interacting via a free scalar field in a fixed (A)dS background in $D+1$ spacetime dimensions, with $D\ge3$ and odd. Using multipole expansion and re-summation techniques, we solve for the field degrees of freedom to obtain an effective particle description in the form of a Fokker action. We derive the equations of motion for the binary up to second post-Newtonian (2PN) order and obtain the corresponding 2PN Hamiltonian and conserved charges in phase space. We show that the conformal algebra, corresponding to the isometry algebra of the (A)dS background, is realised in phase space as a curvature-dependent deformation of the Poincare algebra at each PN order. Our results provide a systematic extension of post-Newtonian effective dynamics to finite-curvature backgrounds. This could serve as a useful framework for studying bound-state dynamics in (A)dS as well as in the corresponding holographic CFT.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Binary-lens amplification of starlight: from magnification flares to quasi-periodic tracking of orbital evolution
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Supermassive black hole binaries (SMBHB) are expected at the center of galaxies as a result of galaxy mergers. The dynamics and evolution of SMBHBs shed light on the evolution and formation of galaxies, the gravitational wave background and the nature of gravity. Many methods have been proposed to identify sub-parsec SMBHBs via the detection of gravitational waves or the modulation of the emission from the surrounding gaseous environment. In a previous study, we proposed a new method of identifying SMBHBs in non-active galactic nuclei via gravitational lensing. The caustics, i.e. the source positions with a divergent magnification, exhibit a complex extended geometry which rotates with the binary period. Each caustic-crossing produces an extreme magnification by up to a factor of $10^{6}$. In this work, we generalize the previous study and describe the rich phenomenology of binary-lens amplification of starlight (BLAST). We explore the electromagnetic transients produced when accounting for the relative proper motion of the source, either a single or a binary star, the eccentricity and precession of the SMBHB, and the relative inclination. Systems where a star rapidly drifts across the caustic produce a single- or double-peaked flare. In the opposite limit, a star with no relative proper motion produces quasi-periodic lensed starlight (QPLS), i.e., repeated peaks that track the system's orbital evolution. We determine the expected magnification and peak duration in different circumstances, and calculate the magnification curves and their Fourier transforms. This study may help construct search pipelines to identify SMBHBs in electromagnetic time-domain surveys.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Cubic Quasinormal Modes in the Black-Hole Ringdown
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We formulate and numerically solve the nonlinear Teukolsky equations through third order, obtaining a first-principles calculation of cubic quasinormal-mode amplitudes for Kerr black holes. Our approach combines lower-order metric reconstruction in split light-cone gauges with a hyperboloidal, compactified formulation solved on complex radial contours. Spin-dependent complex coupling coefficients fix the cubic amplitudes from products of their linear parent amplitudes. We apply these predictions to a nonprecessing numerical-relativity waveform, including cubic products of the $(2,2)$ fundamental mode, its first overtone, and their conjugates. The predicted cubic terms improve agreement over selected early-ringdown fitting windows and shift inferred linear-overtone amplitudes without adding fitting parameters. $3M$ after the peak of $|h_{22}|$, the summed cubic contribution reaches approximately $38\%$ of the total $h_{22}$ signal; $M$ is the initial total mass. These results identify an appreciable cubic response in early ringdown.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Universal Closed Form for Dynamical Love Numbers of Black Holes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Black hole static Love numbers vanish, but their dynamical counterparts do not. We present the entire scheme-independent dynamical response $\bar{F}_{\ell,s}$ of a Schwarzschild black hole in closed form, to all orders in $G$, and for every spin $s$ and multipole $\ell$. The result is $\bar{F}_{\ell,s}/4πR_S^{2\ell+1}=Φ_{\ell,s}(\bar{y})-\tfrac12η\,Φ_{\ell,s}'(\bar{y})$ with $\bar{y}=-\tfrac12η^2τ$ and $η=iωR_S$. Here $Φ_{\ell,s}$ is simply the leading-log solution to the renormalization group equation, but lifting the running logarithm to $τ=\log(R_S/R)-2\sum_{k\ge2}ζ_k\,η^{k-1}$ resums it to all orders. This tower of Riemann zeta values is the Newtonian phase in disguise: it originates from the long-range $1/r$ potential in the far zone, and is universal across multipole and spin. Our result exhibits a factorization pinned to three ingredients: the strength of horizon absorption, the running rate in the near zone, and the dressed logarithm in the far zone. Using shell effective field theory, we independently verify our formula for scalar, electromagnetic, and gravitational perturbations, reaching $\mathcal O(G^{15})$.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 5 pages + references, 1 figure; v3: matches published version

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Separation of variables for coupled radiative perturbations of Kerr-Newman-de Sitter black holes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We extend Hintz's separation of variables for radiative gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations from Kerr-Newman to Kerr-Newman-de Sitter black holes. On subextremal backgrounds with nonzero rotation and charge, an explicit algebraic matrix transformation yields coupled two-component radial and angular ordinary differential systems linked by a common separation constant. The transformation is independent of the frequency and azimuthal number and applies to both signs of spin weight. For real frequencies, we establish a complete angular mode decomposition. We also translate regularity at the future black hole outer and cosmological horizons into ingoing and outgoing boundary conditions, respectively, for the separated radial systems. These results show that exact separation of the coupled radiative equations extends beyond asymptotically flat Kerr-Newman spacetime.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: An extension principle for Einstein-Maxwell-charged scalar field system with finite Doppler exponent
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary:
We prove a new extension principle for the spherically symmetric Einstein--Maxwell--charged scalar field system. Rather than imposing conditions for mass ratio $2m/r$ as in Christodoulou's small-mass-ratio criterion or as in An--Chen--Singh's proof [1] with $2m/r<3/8$, here we work through a proposal by An-Tan [2] with finite Doppler exponent (blueshift). By conducting two successive blow-up analyses, followed by a stationary comparison and a rigidity argument, we establish the uniform boundness of $α'$ with $α'=\partial_vα/\partial_vr$ and $α=\partial_v(rφ)/\partial_vr$. This provides the desired extension principle in An-Tan [2] and completes the picture of weak cosmic censorship developed therein.
  As we were about to release our preprint, Cicortas communicated to us that together with his collaborators, they concomitantly used a different approach to obtain the corresponding extension principle with finite blueshift (Doppler exponent) for the uncharged Einstein-scalar field system. Hence, we decided to put the current paper as an appendix to An-Tan [2], thereby completing the proof of the weak cosmic censorship for the Einstein-Maxwell-charged scalar field system. At the same time, we are working with Cicortas and his collaborators to write a new preprint containing both approaches for the Einstein-scalar field system.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: A Scale-Critical $μ<\frac38$ Extension Principle for Spherically Symmetric Einstein-Scalar Field System
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We present a new quantitative, scale-critical $C^1$ extension principle for the spherically symmetric Einstein--scalar field system. We derive estimates for solutions in the causal past of a possibly singular endpoint $\mathcal{O}$ of the center. Assume that there is no trapped surface in this region and assume that the Doppler exponent (blue shift) along each incoming null cone is uniformly bounded. We then prove that the solution can extend regularly across $\mathcal{O}$ provided the mass ratio $μ=2m/r$ satisfies $\supμ<\frac38$. This improves the small-mass-ratio condition in Christodoulou's extension principle by an explicit threshold of order one. Our proof has three new ingredients. First, we derive several new uniform scale-critical pointwise estimates for the scalar field and its derivatives. Second, we obtain refined estimates in an exterior self-similar domain within the triangular causal past region. Third, we establish a family of higher-order Morawetz-type identities and identify the ranges of $μ$, with which there are coercive spacetime estimates. The unweighted identity yields the threshold $μ\leq\frac14$, while employing extra self-similar weight raises the threshold to $μ<\frac38$ and provides a weighted control, which implies that the solution's BV norm along an outgoing null cone is small, so that Christodoulou's theory of bounded variation solutions gives the extension.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Analytical Time-Domain Waveforms for Black-Hole Scattering in the Post-Minkowskian Expansion
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We present the first analytic computation of the time-domain multipoles of the gravitational waveform from hyperbolic black-hole scattering at leading order in the post-Minkowskian expansion, to all orders in velocity. We perform the partial-wave projection as a cut loop integral, which enables the use of dimensional regularization and associated integration techniques. As opposed to the frequency domain, the time-domain multipoles are logarithmic and do not contain Bessel-like functions. Our results pave the way for the incorporation of post-Minkowskian fluxes in waveform models for binary mergers.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Analytical Time-Domain Waveforms for Black-Hole Scattering in the Self-Force Expansion
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We obtain a systematic understanding of the time-domain gravitational waveform of hyperbolic black-hole scattering at first order in the self-force expansion and all orders in the post-Newtonian/post-Minkowskian (PN/PM) expansion. The continuous frequency spectrum of unbound orbits makes the inverse Fourier transform to the time domain diverge order by order; we introduce a dimensional-regularization-inspired prescription that cures this uniformly. We show that the full waveform then follows, at any PM and PN order, from a single family of integrals, generated by the Lauricella function $F_D^{(3)}$, which we calculate using strategies familiar from the study of Feynman integrals. As a proof of principle, we use this understanding to compute the quadrupolar 1SF waveform through relative 10PM-20PN, that is to order ${\cal O}(G^{10} v^{42})$, the full 1SF waveform to 10PM-10PN, as well as the asymptotic fluxes and the dissipative scattering angle at the corresponding accuracy.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 11 pages, 2 figures and an associated GitHub Repo with the full analytical results at https://github.com/DUsseglio/Scattering-Waveform-1SF

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: A Note on Kinematic Flow and Differential Equations for Two-Site One-Loop Graph in FRW Spacetime
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: In this work, we systematically study the differential systems governing loop-level wavefunction coefficients of conformally-coupled scalar field theory within a general power-law FRW cosmology. By utilizing the twisted cohomology, hyperplane arrangements, and IBP techniques, we derive the canonical differential equations for two-site one-loop bubble and tadpole systems, revealing distinct structural differences. We present new insights into the one-loop tadpole system, uncovering that its integral family can include multiple parent functions due to distinct pairs of relative hyperplanes associated with each function, unlike the single parent function appearing in the one-loop bubble case. Moreover, we demonstrate that the tadpole correlator selectively probes only a subset of the cohomology space, despite the hyperplane arrangement suggesting a higher-dimensional structure. Another novel contribution of this work is the extension of kinematic flow framework to the loop-level scenarios for the first time. Using a graphical approach based on family trees generated by marked tubing graphs, which encode singularity structures, we efficiently construct the differential equations and uncover the hierarchical relationships among the associated master integrals. Additionally, we provide a preliminary discussion on generalization to two-site higher-loop configurations. We propose a general decomposition formula for the canonical form of a two-site diagram with arbitrary loops, breaking it into unshifted and shifted components associated with the fundamental tree-level and bubble-like structures, and establish a block-wise decomposition rule for the matrix $A$ in the corresponding differential system. These advancements provide a unified framework for two-site loop-level correlators and lay the groundwork for future study of more complex multi-site loop systems.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 56 pages. Matches JHEP published version, with updated references and minor revisions to Appendix C

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Dirac Observables for Gowdy Cosmologies Regular at the Big Bang
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Gowdy cosmologies are exact, spatially inhomogeneous solutions of the vacuum Einstein equations which describe nonlinear gravitational waves coalescing at the big bang singularity.
