General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 19 pages, 1 figure; v2: refs added, typos corrected, and the discussion of geodesics revised

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Formation of Trapped Surfaces for the Einstein-Euler System
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We prove the formation of trapped surfaces for the Einstein--Euler system in 3+1 dimensions beyond spherical symmetry. We consider smooth characteristic initial data in a short-pulse regime with rapid fluid injection. Starting from initial data containing no trapped surfaces, we obtain two sufficient criteria for trapped surface formation, corresponding to the shear and fluid contributions, respectively. In particular, for the fluid-driven criterion, we impose no positive lower bound on the shear flux. To handle the multiple propagation speeds associated with gravitational waves, sound waves, and fluid transport, our analysis combines three ingredients: a coercive fluid energy current whose null fluxes reflect the unequal velocity components, curvature renormalizations adapted to the matter terms, and weighted geometric estimates controlling derivatives in all spacetime directions. To ensure that fluid injection alone can lead to trapped surface formation, we use particle-number conservation in a designed spacetime region to control the focusing process and obtain the desired sphere-integrated fluxes.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 147 pages; announced in May 2026 at Fields institute

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Displacement-noise-free gravitational-wave detector using quantum tomography of photon orbital angular momentum states
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Gravitational waves (GWs) induce quantum transitions between photon orbital-angular-momentum (OAM) states with amplitudes $α_{\pm}$. Exploiting this effect, we present a displacement-noise-free detection framework that extracts GW information from the OAM Hilbert space. Parametrized quantum state tomography of the GW-induced OAM sidebands enables a single V-shaped detector to resolve all seven wave parameters: the frequency, propagation direction, two polarization amplitudes, and initial phase of each polarization. Direct detection of the sidebands yields a weak signal of approximately $10^{-15}\,\mathrm{W}$. We therefore introduce a stronger reference state $r |0>_{\mathrm{P}}$, with $r=0.01$, to enhance the detected signal. For an arm length of $L=4\,\mathrm{m}$, $N=160$ round trips, a paraxial parameter of $γ=0.1$, an incident light power of $P_{\mathrm{BS}}=10\,\mathrm{kW}$, a wavelength of $λ_{\mathrm{opt}}=1064\,\mathrm{nm}$, and GW amplitudes of $A=10^{-18}$, we estimate sideband transition amplitudes of $|α_{\pm}|\sim10^{-10}$ and signal powers of order $1\,\mathrm{nW}$, scaling as $P_{\mathrm{BS}}α_{\pm}\propto P_{\mathrm{BS}}ANLγ/λ_{\mathrm{opt}}$. The shot-noise-limited sensitivity floor is $S^{1/2}_n=1.6\times10^{-20}\,\mathrm{Hz}^{-1/2}$. Because the scheme measures OAM transition amplitudes rather than differential arm lengths, it is intrinsically free from displacement noise and provides a broadband probe of GWs, specifically bridging the $0.1$--$10\,\mathrm{Hz}$ mid-frequency gap.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Regge Dilaton Gravity from BF Theory
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: In this work we investigate the relation between gauge and geometric descriptions of two-dimensional dilaton gravity at the level of discrete path integrals. We develop a Regge discretization of Euclidean two-dimensional dilaton gravity using homogeneously curved simplices, as well as a ribbon refined discretization of two-dimensional BF theory adapted to homogeneously curved spacetimes. For Euclidean signature and vanishing or negative cosmological constant we show how the ribbon BF discretization, through appropriate gauge fixings, leads to the Regge dilaton gravity formulation. The resulting correspondence makes explicit how a geometric Regge path integral with its associated measure emerges from its gauge theoretic formulation.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: The hadronic-vacuum-polarization contribution to the muon anomalous magnetic moment in isospin-symmetric lattice QCD with twisted-mass fermions
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We present a lattice-QCD calculation of the leading-order hadronic-vacuum-polarization (HVP) contribution to the anomalous magnetic moment of the muon in isospin-symmetric QCD. We employ the gauge configurations generated by the Extended Twisted Mass Collaboration (ETMC) with $N_f = 2 + 1 + 1$ flavors of Wilson-clover twisted-mass quarks at four lattice spacings and at values of the quark-mass parameters matching the definition of isospin-symmetric QCD given in the FLAG review 2024 and in the 2025 edition of the Muon $g-2$ Theory Initiative White Paper (WP25). After retuning the simulation parameters to precisely match these two definitions of isospin-symmetric QCD, and after carrying out an extrapolation to the continuum limit based on the data at lattice spacings $a \simeq 0.049, 0.057, 0.068$ and $0.079$~fm, and spatial lattice sizes up to $L \simeq 7.7$~fm, we obtain $a_μ^{\rm HVP, FLAG}(\rm{iso}) = (720.0 \pm 6.9) \times 10^{-10}$ and $a_μ^{\rm HVP, WP25}(\rm{iso}) = (714.8 \pm 7.4) \times 10^{-10}$. Our results, which have a relative uncertainty of about $1 \%$, agree well with the corresponding determinations by other lattice groups. After adding to our determination of $a_μ^{\rm HVP, WP25}(\rm{iso})$ the leading isospin-breaking corrections provided in the WP25, namely $a_μ^{\rm HVP, WP25}({\rm IB}) = 0.1(3.4)\times 10^{-10}$, we obtain for the full HVP the value $a_μ^{\rm HVP}= (714.9 \pm 8.1)\times 10^{-10}$. This result translates into a Standard Model prediction for the muon anomalous magnetic moment that is fully consistent with the latest result by the Fermilab Muon $g-2$ experiment and strengthens the tension between lattice QCD and data-driven (pre-CMD3) dispersive determinations.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Radiative transitions of hybrid mesons
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: Radiative transitions of hybrid mesons probe nonperturbative gluodynamics, particularly the interplay between quark spin and gluonic excitations, and are of direct relevance to the search for exotic hadrons at Jefferson Lab. We calculate these transitions across the lowest charmonium-hybrid multiplet in a constituent gluon model based on Coulomb-gauge QCD in the heavy quark expansion. The results for $Y\toη_cγ$ and $Y\to χ_{c0}γ$ overlap the width obtained in quenched lattice computations, whereas $η_{c1}\to J/ψγ$ is substantially below the corresponding lattice estimate.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Critical quench dynamics of Wegner's $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge model: a geometric perspective
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: Wegner's $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge model is the earliest formulation of pure lattice gauge theory and predicts the topological nature of the confinement-deconfinement transition. In three dimensions ($D=3$), the equilibrium critical behavior of the model is understood in terms of geometrically defined objects, namely loop excitations and Fortuin-Kasteleyn (FK) clusters. This work investigates the critical quench dynamics of this model from a geometric perspective, following quenches from both a high-temperature percolation phase and the zero-temperature ground state. Using time-dependent finite-size scaling analysis, we find that the critical non-equilibrium relaxation of the percolation order parameter is governed by a dynamical exponent $z_{\rm p} \simeq 2.6$, consistent with that associated with the energy density, $z_{\rm c}$. Importantly, the value of $z_{\rm p}$ is robust with respect to the initial quench condition and the choice of geometrical objects. Furthermore, we provide a detailed characterization of the kinetics of different geometrical objects during the evolution from the percolation phase. Notably, we observe that the quench dynamics obeys dynamic scaling in terms of a growing lengthscale, $ξ_{\rm p}(t) \sim t^{1/z_{\rm p}}$, despite the absence of a local order parameter.
High Energy Physics - Lattice.comment: Follow-up to Phys. Rev. Lett. 135, 120601 (2025); 25 pages, 12 figures

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Jianmu-Q: Bridging Quantum Field Theory and Quantum Hardware with AI Agents
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: Quantum computing offers a promising approach to non-perturbative simulations of quantum field theories, particularly for real-time dynamics and systems affected by the sign problem. Yet translating continuum field theories into quantum computations remains a challenging interdisciplinary task. Here we introduce \texttt{Jianmu-Q}, a multi-agent framework that transforms natural-language descriptions of quantum field theories into quantum simulation workflows. Specialized agents handle theoretical formulation, lattice discretization, qubit mapping, and circuit design, while physical consistency checks and independent numerical calculations provide validation throughout the workflow. We benchmark the framework on three field theories of increasing complexity: the $(1+1)$-dimensional Nambu--Jona-Lasinio and Schwinger models, and a $(2+1)$-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory. Across these systems, noiseless quantum-circuit simulations converge toward independent exact-diagonalization and tensor-network results, while selected circuits are executed on IBM quantum hardware, demonstrating an end-to-end, validation-guided approach to quantum simulation of field theories.
High Energy Physics - Lattice.comment: 13 pages, 9 figures, 4 tables. Code available at https://github.com/Jianmu-lab/Jianmu-Q

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Quantum Monte Carlo calculations in the nuclear shell model by the complex Langevin method
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: The nuclear shell model is known to describe the properties of various nuclei extremely well. However, the auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo calculations cannot be applied to it with general interactions due to the sign problem. The model has therefore been investigated primarily by variational methods, where the accuracy of the results depends crucially on the ansatz for the wave function. Here we perform the auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo calculations in the case of small systems at finite temperature using the complex Langevin method (CLM), which has been successfully applied to various interesting systems with the sign problem over the decade. In particular, we show the existence of a parameter region in which the validity criterion for the CLM is satisfied and the expectation value of the energy obtained by exact diagonalization is correctly reproduced. Thus the CLM can be a complementary approach to the variational method for large systems.
High Energy Physics - Lattice.comment: 22 pages, 14 figures; v2: minor corrections and two appendices added
